chunks.heading: APPROVAL OF SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURE MANUAL - 4m
chunks.text: EDITION REVISION 03. Reference to your letter OPS/CSTR/TRNG/26/217 dated 12th June 2026. I wish to inform you that the 04th Edition Revision 03 of the Safety & Emergency Procedure (SEP) Manual for the use of Cabin Crew Members of SriLankan Airlines Limited, is hereby approved. The contents of this manual shall not be amended without explicit approval from this office. Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka may at any stage suggest amendment or addition to any of its contents, if deemed necessary. SriLankan Airlines Limited, shall ensure all Cabin Crew Members are in possession of a current SEP Manual while on duty. Furthermore, SriLankan Airlines shall furnish copies of this manual and any amendments or revisions thereto personnel who may require the Manual for reference in the performance of their duties and to such other persons as Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka deem necessary. A copy of this letter shall form a part of the Manual.

chunks.heading: APPROVAL OF SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURE MANUAL - 4m
chunks.text: Message from the Chief Technical Officer SriLankan Airlines has upheld the highest safety standards since its inception and takes great pride in fostering a strong safety culture across all areas of operation. The Cabin Safety function plays a vital role in the prevention of incidents and accidents, ensuring the protection of aircraft occupants through proactive safety management practices and effective hazard identification. The Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual is published in compliance with the requirements of the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL), providing comprehensive guidance, regulatory direction, and operational support to cabin crew members. This manual is continuously reviewed and updated to incorporate industry best practices, ensuring alignment with evolving safety standards and operational excellence. At the international level, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) harmonizes safety and

chunks.heading: APPROVAL OF SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURE MANUAL - 4m
chunks.text: emergency procedures through the respective National Regulatory Bodies of its Member States to maintain global consistency in aviation safety. Cabin crew training programs are developed in accord- ance with ICAO Doc 10002 (Doc 10002-AN/502, SLCAP 4305), which promotes a competency-based training and assessment approach. This framework ensures that cabin crew members are systematically trained, assessed, and continuously evaluated to maintain the highest level of proficiency in performing their safety and emergency responsibilities The CCM SEP manual conforms to the standards and recommended practices stipulated in SLCAP 4300. The ultimate objective of this manual is to ensure that safety remains the highest priority at all times, without compromise. Chief Technical Officer

chunks.heading: CHAPTER 10 - DANGEROUS GOODS REGULATIONS
chunks.text: Contents

chunks.heading: CHAPTER 10 - DANGEROUS GOODS REGULATIONS
chunks.text: 2. Preamble SriLankan Airlines Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual (4th Edition / Revision 03 – 2026) This manual has been compiled in accordance with the requirements stipulated in SLCAP 4300. It is structured into ten chapters, providing a systematic approach to aircraft systems, equipment, and procedures. Fleet-specific variations from the base aircraft are highlighted, with emphasis placed on operational differences. Flight and ground emergencies, as well as land and water survival procedures, are included as reference material for training purposes. This document serves as the current operational Safety & Emergency Procedures Manual for Cabin Crew. All revisions must receive prior approval from the Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) before implementation. It is mandatory that every Cabin Crew Member (CCM) maintains possession of the latest updated manual. An Administration Guide to Cabin Safety is provided separately in the Cabin Safety Training Work Proce-

chunks.heading: CHAPTER 10 - DANGEROUS GOODS REGULATIONS
chunks.text: dures Manual. The manual was compiled in collaboration with the Cabin Safety Inspectors of the Civil Aviation Authori- ty of Sri Lanka (CAASL) and the Cabin Safety Instructors (Training & Standards) of SriLankan Airlines. Cabin Safety remains committed to continuously enhancing safety standards. Think smart, act safe — prevent incidents and accidents. Any clarifications regarding procedures or statements in this manual must be directed to the Cabin Safe- ty Training Manager. Cabin Safety Training Manager

chunks.heading: 3 The Manual Structure
chunks.text: The manual consists of ten chapters. The relevant chapters are organized in a detailed and methodical manner for easy reference. It guides you through regulations, policies, procedures and requirements. The end of each chapter is summarized for quick reference. Amendments that need immediate attention, pending approval will be in chapter 7 as Provisional Issues in yellow colour pages. Cabin Safety Training Section shall upload the updated manual and inform the Crew via e-mail. Crew shall down load the updated manual from AeroDocs and retain on a device for reference and audit purposes. CHAPTER 1 - Administration and Control of Safety and Emergency Procedures This chapter contains the administration and control of the Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual. CHAPTER 2 - General Procedures This chapter is an introduction to the regulatory body, “CAASL” and covers requirements and responsi- bilities of Cabin Crewmembers. The chapter also consists of Flight Crew responsibilities and a detailed

chunks.heading: 3 The Manual Structure
chunks.text: explanation of cabin crew duties at different phases of flight in sequence. CHAPTER 3 - Safety Equipment This chapter consists of all safety equipment available on board. It includes preflight / serviceability checks, operation, precautions and limitations. Diagrams of locations are included for easy reference. CHAPTER 4 - Emergency Procedures This chapter describes emergency procedures and duties to be performed in an emergency evacuation. The information comprises of emergency communication, evacuation procedures and post-crash surviv- al. CHAPTER 5 - Aircraft Specific This chapter consist details of specific aircraft structures and systems. It includes description of cabin, passenger seats, aircraft doors slides/cabin crew seats/lavatories/galleys/emergency lighting and opera- tion of secure flight deck door/oxygen system/seats etc. CHAPTER 6– Single Aisle Aircraft This chapter consist details of relevant safety equipment, systems and emergency procedures.

chunks.heading: 3 The Manual Structure
chunks.text: CHAPTER 7 - Provisional Issues The pages of this chapter are issued in yellow. It consists of amendments that need immediate imple- mentation. Provisional issues are not considered as revision until approved by the DGCA. Once ap- proved, amendments shall be introduced as revisions to the relevant chapters. CHAPTER 8 – Security This chapter consists of aviation security and explains procedures to be followed and guidelines to be adopted with incidents on board.

chunks.heading: 3 The Manual Structure
chunks.text:
CHAPTER 9– First Aid This chapter consists of procedures to be followed as a first aider in the absence of a medical practition- er. Details of the medication carried on board are included (Emergency Medical Kit (A10)/First Aid Kits). CHAPTER 10– Transportation of Dangerous Goods by Air This chapter consists of identifying, handling, limitations and precautions of dangerous goods. It also describes procedures in handling spillages/leakages, PED fires on board.

chunks.heading: 4.3 Change Indicator (Vertical Bar)
chunks.text: Located in the right outside margin, are used to highlight the location of revised or deleted information on a newly published page. With the next revision to the page, previous change indicators are deleted. Change indicators will be used on contents pages to indicate the addition of a new title or procedure, or to indicate a renamed procedure. Change indicators will not be used to indicate format or page number changes or opposite the new date on a revised page.

chunks.heading: 4.4 Words
chunks.text: Whenever the word “shall” is used in a sentence, there would be a process that must be followed as a requirement. Whenever the word “should” is used in a sentence, it is a recommendation that may be followed. “May” means that the application of a procedure or provision is optional. For conciseness, the pronoun “he” is used throughout the text. Where appropriate, “she” should be added or substituted for “he”.

chunks.heading: 4.5 Intentionally Blank Page
chunks.text: INTENTIONALLY LEFT BLANK will be printed on any page that contains no text or graphics.

chunks.heading: 4.6 Record of Revisions
chunks.text: The purpose of a revision is to make additions, deletions or corrections to the manual. The manual may be revised periodically to provide current procedures and information not previously furnished. Each revision shall be approved by DGCA prior to implementation. Revision is by replacement of a whole page bearing the applicable revision number and the date. The affected text will be marked by a vertical bar on the outer margin of the page. The revised manual shall be uploaded to AeroDocs by the cabin Safety Training section. The crew shall down load the revised manual and conformity shall be monitored by the Cabin Safety Training Section. The CCMs shall download the revised manual within the stipulated 14 days.

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text: The following is a description of commonly used terms in this manual. The intent of this list is to clarify terms, and avoid miscommunication. Able Bodied Passenger (ABP) A person delegated to assist Cabin Crew and take over duties in case of incapacitation. Arming The action required to place the door slide system to the “ARMED” mode. This would ensure that the slide system will automatically deploy when the door is opened. Authority Authority means the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka and should be referred to as the CAASL. Bassinet Row This refers to the seat row in which the bassinet(s) is installed. Bracing Position A position adopted, when seated by all crew and passengers during an emergency landing to prevent injury resulting from forced body movement (Impact). Buddy Person delegated to assist fellow passengers in an emergency. Bulkhead Any transverse upright partition which divided the compartments in an aircraft

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text: Cabin Unless otherwise specified, this refers to the passenger compartment and includes the galleys and lava- tories. It does not include the crew rest facility (if installed).

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text: Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024 Cabin Crew member Referred to as a CCM. A trained/approved and designated person carried on a flight for the purpose of performing duties assigned by Sri Lankan Airlines or the Pilot In-Command of the aircraft, in the interest of the safety of passengers, but who shall not act as a member of the Flight Crew Cabin Safety Instructions Refers to cabin safety instructions which shall be issued by Cabin Safety Training Manager for all regula- tory training and procedural changes pertaining to Cabin Safety and cabin crew operations Cabin Safety Notice Refers to Cabin Safety Notices issued by Cooperate Safety Section with regards to regulatory and proce- dural changes Cabin Supervisor Referred to as CS. A trained/approved and designated person carried on a flight for the purpose of performing duties, supervising a part of the cabin and shall be responsible to the Purser or Nominated

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text:
Purser. Code Red Is a secret code used to enter the flight deck through the high security door. Purser shall use the Code Red in case there is no response from the flight deck. Cross-Checking A procedure in which a CCM counter checks a procedure carried out by another CCM E.g. during arming and disarming of slides. Critical Phases of Flight Are as follows:
• Take-off run / Take-off flight path
• Final approach
• Landing, including the landing roll until leaving the active runway Ditching - A term for an aircraft making an emergency landing on water Direct Access - Where passengers can proceed directly to an exit without entering an aisle or passing around an obstruction. Disarming - The action required to place the door slide system to DISARMED mode. Dead heading Crew/Positioning Crew Dead heading crew - A CCM positioning after concluding a flight duty turn. Door - A hinged part of the aircraft which could be opened and closed as required.

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text: Downwind - The direction in which the prevailing wind is blowing away from an object or person

chunks.heading: 4.11 Definitions
chunks.text: Exit A secured opening in the aircraft which could be used as an escape route. Exit Seat Row A row of seats having direct access to an exit/s. Flight Crew member A licensed crew member charged with duties essential to the operation of an aircraft during flight time. Hijack Alert Code given by the PIC for denied entry to the Flight Deck. Hypoxia A condition which could develop during a decompression due to lack of oxygen.

chunks.heading: ICAO
chunks.text: A specialized agency of the United Nations, ICAO was created in 1944 to promote the safety and order- ly development of international civil aviation throughout the world. It sets standards and regulations necessary for aviation safety, security, efficiency and regularity, as well as for aviation environmental protection. The Organization serves as the forum for cooperation in all fields of civil aviation among its contracting states. Line Indoctrination Familiarization Flights Following successful completion of Initial training Manning the Door To position at, to defend or operate a door or exit.

chunks.heading: MEDA Case
chunks.text: Refers to a person who requires medical attention.

chunks.heading: MEDA Form
chunks.text: Medical Information Form. Referred to as incapacitated passenger handling advice (INCAD part 1 and part 11). Provides confidential information enabling the Group Medical Officer to assess the ability of the passenger to travel. Oral and nasal The nose and mouth. Positioning Crew A CCM been positioned to operate a sector or part of a flight. Pilot in Command The Pilot responsible for the operation and safety of the aircraft during the flight. The pilot designated by the operator, or in the case of general aviation, the owner, as being in command and charged with the safe conduct of the flight

chunks.heading: MEDA Form
chunks.text: Purser A Senior CCM designated by SriLankan Airlines to be in-charge of CCMs for the flight and to be respon- sible for ensuring that all safety provisions are met as per the CCM SEP Manual and Standard Operating Procedures. Quick Reference Chart (QRC) A list of the safety equipment which is relevant to each CCM station for guidance of the crew. Relay Briefing A briefing carried out by the Purser / Nominated Purser in order to pass down vital information to CCMs. The method of communication may vary depending on the restrictions. Senior Cabin Crew member A Cabin Crew member who is certified by the DGCA to operate a said type of aircraft and has completed one year of flight duties. Senior Executive-Cabin Safety Instructor A Cabin Safety Instructor Certified by the DGCA to carry out regulatory training/assessments / on-Line assessments on CCMs to maintaining high standards of cabin safety.

chunks.heading: MEDA Form
chunks.text:
Serious injury
1. An injury which is sustained by a person in an accident and which requires hospitalization for more than 48 hours, commencing within seven days from the date the injury was received; or
2. Results in a fracture of any bone (except simple fractures of fingers, toes or nose);or
3. Involves lacerations which cause severe haemorrhage, nerve, muscle, or tendon damage; or
4. Involves injury to any internal organ; or
5. Involves second- or third-degree burns, or any burns affecting more than 5 per cent of the body surface;or
6. Involves verified exposure to infectious substances or injurious radiation. Silent Thirty Second Review (STS) When seated for take-off or landing, a period of time where a Cabin Crew member reviews the respon- sibilities to be carried out in an emergency to evacuate passengers, which comprises of, Bracing for impact, Door operation, Evacuation commands, Evacuation route, Passenger control.

chunks.heading: MEDA Form
chunks.text: Supernumerary Cabin Crew An Additional Cabin Crew: Travelling either for or after duty has been concluded or as an observer. Their duties, take-off and landing stations will be allocated by the Purser on a sector-by-sector basis Supernumerary Flight Crew Additional Flight Crew: Traveling either for or after duty has been concluded. Supplementary Information Additional information provided to assist the manual user.

chunks.heading: MEDA Form
chunks.text: Taxi Movement of an airplane under its own power on ground excluding the take-off and the landing. Training Cycles Defines the type of training and the processes in place for each individual situation of a Cabin Crew member. Warnings, Cautions and Notes The following levels of written advisories are used throughout the manual. An operating procedure, technique, which may result in personal injury or loss of life, if not followed. All warnings are in bold lettering and placed within a red box.

chunks.heading: WARNINGS
chunks.text: Example:

chunks.heading: WARNING: WHEN RESPIRATION RESISTANCE INCREASES, CORRECT THE FITTING OF THE
chunks.text: MASK, CHECK THE FUNCTION OF THE EQUIPMENT BY TAKING A FEW DEEP BREATHS.

chunks.heading: CAUTION
chunks.text: An operating procedure/technique, which may result in damage to equipment if not followed. All cau- tions are in bold lettering and placed within a amber box. Example:

chunks.heading: CAUTION: IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CCMS INSPECT THE LAVATORY SMOKE DETECTOR FOR
chunks.text: TAMPERING PRIOR TO EVERY TAKE OFF.

chunks.heading: NOTE
chunks.text: An operating procedure, technique, etc., Considered essential to follow. Information contained in notes may also be safety related are in bold lettering and placed within a Gray box.. Example: Note: A330-300 aircraft are equipped with 8 main doors which are “TYPE A” doors. Emergency Announcements Announcements relating to emergency are printed in bold red lettering. Example: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,YOUR ATTENTION PLEASE,THIS IS YOUR CAPTAIN, WE PLAN TO MAKE AN EMERGENCY LANDING ON WATER IN.…....MINUTES. PLEASE PAY ATTENTION TO THE CABIN CREW MEMBER’S INSTRUCTIONS AND FOLLOW THEM AT ALL TIMES. YOUR CO-OPERATION IS ESSENTIAL. THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: NOTE
chunks.text: Informatory Announcements Announcements relating to information are printed in bold black lettering. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, AS THE CAPTAIN HAS SWITCHED THE SEAT BELT SIGN, PLEASE REMAIN SEATED AND FASTEN YOUR SEAT BELTS, PLEASE REFRAIN FROM USING THE TOILETS DURING THIS PERIOD, THANK YOU”.

chunks.text: Contents

chunks.heading: 1.0 Introduction To The Manual
chunks.text: Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual shall be compiled as per requirements stipulated in SLCAP 5300- Standards for Manuals and Documents. The SriLankan Airlines Safety & Emergency Procedures Manual shall comply with SLCAP 4300 - Cabin Crewmember Manual Standard and approved by the DGCA prior to being effective to ensure the infor- mation is accurate and legible. Cabin safety training manager shall review the contents of this manual annually and do necessary changers as per requirements stipulated in SLCAIS 002 Cabin Crewmembers shall be in possession of an updated Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual in electronic format, whenever they are engaged in flight duties as a reference guide. The SEP Manual shall be carried in the personal cabin bag of the CCM with unobstructed access. The battery of the de- vice shall be charged to a minimum of 70% prior to the flight and the screen shall not be damaged. The

chunks.heading: 1.0 Introduction To The Manual
chunks.text: recommended screen size is 7 inches or more diagonally. CCM shall ensure that their reference devices are turned on, set to aircraft mode/offline and readily accessible at all times during flight duty except during critical phases, they should refer to the information or announcements stored on these devices as necessary to ensure compliance with safety protocols and to provide accurate information to passen- gers The contents of this manual pertain predominantly to Cabin Crew members and shall be printed in English. However areas such as safety equipment, emergency procedures, survival and first aid which are relevant to Flight Crew members are included as well. Hence, copies of this manual are distributed to the management Pilots as depicted in the distribution list. It is the responsibility of the individual Crew member to ensure that he is in possession of the most current digital copy of the SEP manual during flight duty and same needs to be downloaded from Aer-

chunks.heading: 1.0 Introduction To The Manual
chunks.text: oDocs. CCMs shall not Copy or download the SEP Manual from Social Media platforms/Airdrop/Blue- tooth/Pen drives/E-mail or any other mean as it will not register CCMs name on the system. Failure to do so will result in disciplinary action being taken against the CCM. Joint training programs shall be carried out along with Flight Crew members on selected training pro- grams for better synchronization of safety related duties. The contents of the said manual shall not be communicated or discussed with persons outside SriLan- kan Airlines. Holders of the manuals shall not edit its contents, and if found guilty shall be subject to strict discipli- nary action. Cabin crew shall download the SEP Manual onto a personal device, read and understand the contents. chunks.heading: 1.1 Providing information to cabin crew
chunks.text:
Promulgation of instructions, information of an administrative or operational nature which may supple- ment, or substitute information or instructions contained in the SEPM and the exchange of information relevant to the conduct of cabin safety operations is through the following modes of communication.
1. Electronic Mail (email)
2. Cabin Safety Instructions (CSI)
3. Cabin Safety Notice (CSN)
4. Provisional Issues
5. Telephone call or SMS

chunks.heading: 1.1.1 Electronic Mail (email)
chunks.text: Email is the official and primary mode of communication within SriLankan Airlines. The Cabin safety Training Management communicates most information, supplementary to information contained in the SEPM and other manuals, to crew and staff via email. Cabin crew can access company emails remotely with their iPads, smart phones, laptops or desktop PCs through the company Intranet or Microsoft 365.

chunks.heading: 1.1.2 Cabin Safety Instructions and Cabin Safety Notice
chunks.text: Cabin Safety Instructions (CSIs) and Cabin Safety Notice (CSN) contain information that has an impact on the safety and security of operational activities and procedures and will always override any other instructions in the SEPM. It is the responsibility of the individual Crew member to ensure that he is in possession of the most current digital copies of all CSNs and CSIs during flight duty and same needs to be downloaded from AeroDocs. For audit compliance CCMs shall not Copy or download CSI/CSN from Social Media platforms/Airdrop/Bluetooth/Pen drives/E-mail or any other mean as it will not register CCMs name on the system. Failure to do so will result in disciplinary action being taken against the CCM.

chunks.heading: 1.1.4 Quick Reference Handbook
chunks.text: This Quick Reference Handbook/Edition 04 has been issued as a practical manual for use by CCMs in the performance of cabin operation duties. This manual has been issued by Cabin Safety Training section of Srilankan Airlines in keeping with regulatory requirements. It is the responsibility of the individual Crew member to ensure that he is in possession of the most current digital copy of the QRHB during flight duty and same needs to be downloaded from AeroDocs. CCMs shall not Copy or download QRHB from Social Media platforms/Airdrop/Bluetooth/Pen drives/E-mail or any other mean as it will not register CCMs name on the system. Failure to do so will result in discipli-nary action being taken against the CCM.

chunks.heading: GENERAL PROCEDURES
chunks.text: Contents

chunks.heading: 2.1.1 International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO)
chunks.text: A specialized agency of the United Nations, the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) was cre- ated in 1944 to promote the safe and orderly development of international civil aviation throughout the world. ICAO sets standards and Regulations necessary for aviation safety, security and efficiency, as well as the forum for cooperation in all fields of civil aviation among its 193 member states. The membership of ICAO is obtained by the state. ICAO also develops standards and recommended practices (SARPS) and procedures relevant to the training of cabin crew and the operation of aircraft. The distinction between standards and recommended practices is an important one. ICAO does not prescribe how cabin crew should perform each procedure. Although standards and recommended practices are developed in collaboration with representatives of all member states, each country decides how certain SARPS are

chunks.heading: 2.1.1 International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO)
chunks.text: implemented. Moreover, each airline has some liberty how SARPS are applied.

chunks.heading: 2.1.2 The International Air Transport Association (IATA)
chunks.text: The International Air Transport Association is the airlines trade association. IATA was formed in 1945. Today the membership of IATA is 300 member airlines, which represents 84% of the world air traffic. Membership of IATA should be obtained by individual airlines. Although not a regulator, membership of IATA requires an airline to demonstrate that it complies with all aspects of the IATA operational safety audit (IOSA). IATA also manages a Cabin Safety Task Force (CSTF), which creates guidance material for airlines to operate safely. Meetings with member airlines are held twice a year. During which recent cabin safety related incidents are presented and discussed.

chunks.heading: 2.1.3 European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA)
chunks.text: The national aviation authorities in the European Union joined together to form the European Avia- tion Safety Agency (EASA) in 2002, by Regulation (EC) No 216/2008 of the European parliament and the Council. The purpose of EASA’s mandate is to standardize the regulations between the EU member states; so that the same levels of safety can be assured to the passengers no matter which national authority issues the Air Operators Certificate (AOC).

chunks.heading: 2.1.4 Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL)
chunks.text:
The Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL) was established under the Civil Aviation Authority Act NO. 34 of 2002 on 27 th December 2002 and is deemed a Public Enterprise under Article 154 of the Con- stitution of the Democratic Socialistic Republic of Sri Lanka. Civil Aviation Authorities primary function is to undertake activities that promote civil aviation safety and security in keeping with International Standards and Recommended Practices adopted by International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) and to steer the aviation sector in Sri Lanka as a prime contributor to the growth of national economy, enhancing quality of life of its citizens. Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka shall exercise, perform and discharge the following powers, func- tions and duties,
1. Regulate civil air operations within the territory of Sri Lanka and the operations of Sri Lanka reg- istered aircraft outside the territory of Sri Lanka.

chunks.heading: 2.1.4 Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL)
chunks.text:
2. Develop and promulgate or adopt by reference as appropriate, clear and concise aviation safety requirements, practices and procedures, implement effective enforcement strategies to secure compliance by all persons of the Standards and such aviation safety requirements, practices and procedures.
3. Encourage through comprehensive and timely aviation safety advice and by fostering awareness within the aviation community, the importance of aviation safety, maintaining high standards of aviation safety; provide aviation safety education and training for persons involved in civil aviation activities.
4. Initiate investigations on aircraft accidents and any other related incidents, arrange for the es- tablishment and provision of search and rescue operations; conduct inquiries with regard to any flight safety hazards.
5. CAASL has direct impact on the functioning of cabin crew operations by its approval of two

chunks.heading: 2.1.4 Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL)
chunks.text: foundational documents for each airline: The Operations Manual Approvals, and Issuance of Air Operator’s Certificate (AOC). The Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka consists of eight (08) members appointed by the Minister in charge of the subject of Civil Aviation. Three members, The Secretary, Ministry of Defence, a represent- ative of the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance and the Director-General of Civil Aviation are serving the CAASL as ex-officers. The term of office of the appointed members is three (03) years. The Authority is subject to the direction and control of the Minister in charge of the Civil Aviation.

chunks.heading: 2.1.5 Roles/Functions of CAASL Inspectors
chunks.text: CAASL Inspectors carries out regular inspections of the airline to ensure that it is operating according to the terms of the AOC and procedures detailed in the operations manuals. Ensure safety equipment operating procedures systems are in accordance with prescribed standards and Srilankan air navigation regulations.

chunks.heading: 2.1.6 Inspector Identification
chunks.text: CAASL Inspectors appointed by the DGCA will identify themselves to CCMs by displaying a Civil Avia- tion Inspector credential Card at the time of boarding. It is mandatory that the PIC be informed of the Inspectors presence. Specimen Authorisation Card of a CAASL Inspector

chunks.heading: 2.1.7 Authority of CAASL Inspectors
chunks.text: The Inspectors are authorised to audit flight operations, cabin safety and dangerous goods training, safety equipment, aircraft systems,standard operation procedures (SOP’s), Safety and Emergency Proce- dures Manuals, Safety Training and Standards Manuals, evaluate Cabin Safety Instructors, evaluate and approve safety training devices and training organisations. The aforementioned shall be in accordance with the prescribed standards and Air Navigation Regulations of Sri Lanka. Any person appointed by the DGCA as a Civil Aviation Inspector or Designated Examiner shall be per- mitted to board/fly on any SriLankan Airlines aircraft to observe/inspect or administer periodical tests/ inspections.

chunks.heading: 2.1.8 Carriage of Inspector
chunks.text: CAASL Inspectors or Examiners are permitted to board and fly on SriLankan Airlines aircraft for the pur- pose of observing, inspecting or administering a safety over sight. He shall occupy a passenger seat in the cabin and would be a holder of a boarding card. In the event the aircraft is full and passenger or crew seats are not available, they may occupy flight deck observer seats with the approval of the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.2.1 Minimum Requirements
chunks.text: Specific minimum standards ensure that individuals selected will be capable of satisfactorily completing the training program, be able to perform all designated safety related duties and be competent in deal- ing with safety and emergency procedures in compliance to SLCAIS 089. CCMs shall be able to read and understand written instructions in English, exercise good judgment, communicate effectively with Flight Crew, fellow CCMs and passengers during an emergency. CCMs shall refer the Inflight Services Administrative/Announcement Manual and Standard Operating Procedures for relevant guidance. The CCMs shall be responsible to inform the Inflight Services Admin- istrative Department of any known concerns that would affect the performance on board an aircraft at the earliest. It is the responsibility of the individual CCM to obtain and maintain the relevant immunizations as per the company standards prescribed by the Group Medical Officer/Company Medical Officer.

chunks.heading: 2.2.1 Minimum Requirements
chunks.text: The recommended minimum requirements applicable to CCMs of Sri Lankan Airlines are, Educational Qualifications Ref : HR Peoples admin and policy Manual Chapter 12 Medical Fitness CCMs shall meet the requirements of the Class II medical examination approved by the CAASL.

chunks.heading: Ref. SLCAIS 097

Weight Body Mass Index shall apply- Ref. SLCAIS 097 Eye Sight Uncorrected - 6/60 Corrected - 6/90 (As stipulated by the GMO/CMO) Colour Vision Mandatory Age Minimum : 18 years of age

chunks.heading: 2.3 Prohibitions
chunks.text: CCMs are required to keep the company informed regarding any physical or mental concerns that might affect the performance on-board an aircraft or impair good judgement. Ref SLCAIS 035

chunks.heading: 2.3.1 Consumption of Alcohol
chunks.text:
Alcohol in the system could affect the performance. It is prohibited for a CCM to commence flight duty with a blood alcohol level in excess of 0.02% on the breathalyser. A CCM found above the stipulated alcohol level shall be relieved from duty with immediate effect and shall be subjected to administrative requirements. CCMs shall be subjected to random testing by medical personnel for verification of blood alcohol level. CCM is prohibited from consuming alcohol, 1.08 hours prior to the specified reporting time for flight duty 2.08 hours prior to the commencement of standby duty
3. Whilst on standby
4. During flight duty

chunks.heading: 2.3.2 Drugs and Stimulants
chunks.text: Unless prescribed by a qualified medical practitioner, the use of stimulants and/or drugs are prohibited as it could affect the performance. When stimulants and/or drugs are prescribed for CCMs, they may undertake flying duties only with specific written clearance by the prescribing medical practitioner and clearance approved by Sri Lankan Airlines Group Medical Officer/Company Medical Officer.

chunks.heading: 2.3.3 Psychoactive Substances
chunks.text: CCMs are prohibited from taking psychoactive substances, as it could affect the performance. In the event a CCM is found in violation of the above, he shall be immediately removed from flight duty and referred to the . GMO/CMO’s clearance as per the requirements of the authority is required prior to scheduling the CCM on active flight duty.

chunks.heading: 2.3.4 Deep Water Diving
chunks.text: A CCM is prohibited from reporting to flight duty unless a minimum of 24 hours has elapsed after scuba diving beyond a depth of 10 meters.

chunks.heading: 2.3.5 Donating Blood
chunks.text: A CCM is prohibited from reporting to flight duty unless a minimum of 24 hours has elapsed after do- nating blood.

chunks.heading: 2.3.6 Pregnancy
chunks.text: Once a CCM is confirmed to be pregnant, she shall inform the In-Flight Admin section. She will conse- quently be considered not fit to fly and shall be taken off the active roster. CCM is required to submit a medical certificate to confirm her pregnancy and follow the requirements.

chunks.heading: 2.3.7 Heating of Crew Meals
chunks.text: Crew meals must not be heated along with the passenger meals unless served immediately to Crew. Passenger and Crew meals shall not be reheated as reheating may cause food poisoning.

chunks.heading: 2.4 Mandatory Items to Be Carried By A CCM
chunks.text:
1. Sri Lankan Airlines staff identification card
2. CCM Certificate and Crew Member Certificate issued by the DGCA
3. Passport/Health Certificate (as applicable)
4. Safety and Emergency Procedures Manual (e-format)
5. Relevant keys
6. CCMs dependent on Spectacles/Lenses (contact lenses) shall carry a spare set when on flight duty
7. CCMs who have an endorsement on the CCM Certificate for hearing Aid shall wear them whilst on flight duty.

chunks.heading: 2.4.1 Company ID
chunks.text: A valid Company ID and a Crew Member Certificate shall be displayed by the CCM prior to entering the airport premises and shall remain clearly displayed at all times when on duty within the restricted zone at an airport.

chunks.heading: 2.4.2 Loss of Company ID Card/Security Pass
chunks.text: Loss/theft of Company ID card/Security Pass, shall be reported immediately to the police in the area concerned at base or overseas and Company Security and Investigation Department.

chunks.heading: 2.4.3 Loss of Crew Member Certificate/Cabin Crew Member Certificate
chunks.text: The loss of a CMC/CCMC Shall be reported immediately to the police in the area concerned at base or overseas/Company Security and Investigation Department/Inflight Admin and Flight Operations Admin.

chunks.heading: 2.5 Cabin Crew Member Certificate (CCMC)
chunks.text: Pursuance to SLCAIS 089 it is mandatory that CCMs obtain a Cabin Crewmember certificate from the DGCA in order to operate as a required CCM on board SriLankan Airlines Aircraft. SriLankan Airlines shall ensure to fulfill the conditions stipulated in SLCAIS 089 in order to apply for the Cabin Crewmember certificate. The certificate shall be valid for 5years from the date of issue. The CCM shall be responsible to update the certificate by obtaining endorsements on the relevant pages and shall be in possession of a valid certificate when reporting for flight duty. CCMs shall be responsible to renew the certificate prior to the date of expiry and the renewal process to commence 45 days prior to expiry. CCMs shall notify Cabin Safety Training section in writing if the renewed certificate is not received before 10 days of expiry. Only persons authorized by DGCA shall make endorsements on the certificate. The Regulato-

CCMs shall ensure medical/training records are current before operating a flight. Once a CCMs operates a flight with expired medical/training records he shall be in violation of the regulatory requirement of the authority. Ensuring currency before operating a flight shall be the responsibility of the operating Purser/In-Charge CCM and the CCM concern. chunks.text: To prevent confusion by passengers Positioning/Dead Heading CCM shall not wear, or at least make invisible to passengers, part of the operator’s cabin crew uniform that might identify them as members of the operating cabin crew

chunks.text: DGCA shall issue a CMC as per the requirement Ref. Implementation Standard 007 of 2012. The prima- ry purpose of the issue is for identification as a crew member of an airline or persons essential for the operation of an aircraft. E.g. Flight Crew, Cabin Crew and Flight Engineers if applicable.

chunks.text: There could be Crew listed on the General Declaration who are certified by DGCA to carry out non safe- ty related duties. Ref SLCAIS 07

They shall adhere to the following,
1. Shall be identified in a different uniform from the operating CCMs
2. During a decompression, don an oxygen mask and act as a passenger
3. During an emergency evacuation/ditching, follow instructions

chunks.heading: 2.7 Training Standard SLCAP 4305 (CAASL Publication)
chunks.text: Training for a CCM on regulatory requirements on board an aircraft is a legal requirement. All training required for the issuance of a certificate is published in ICAO Doc: 10002 Cabin Crew Safety Training Manual and SLCAP 4305 -Training Standards for CCMs, Paragraph 12.4 of annex 6 requires that, SriLankan Airlines shall establish and maintain a safety-training program, approved by the DGCA and all persons shall satisfactorily complete it prior to certification as required in SLCAIS 083/089

chunks.heading: 2.7.1 Training Programmes
chunks.text: Regulations require that Sri Lankan Airlines conduct approved training programs for all regulatory train- ing purposes. Only Cabin Safety Instructors approved by the DGCA shall conduct cabin safety training. All training shall be conducted as stipulated in the Training Standard Manual & shall be guided by the procedures laid down in the approved Safety & Emergency Procedures Manual in accordance with

chunks.heading: 2.7.1 Training Programmes
chunks.text: SLCAP 4300.The primary objective of a safety-training program is to motivate safe actions through es- tablishment of a dynamic corporate safety culture. Designing the training shall be to underline the CCM responsibilities on the safety aspects at all times, and in the event of an emergency to react with confi- dence to save lives. The training shall be for CCMs to assume duties in any section within the cabin, not limiting to the work position assigned. If a CCM is incapacitated, another CCM shall assume the others responsibilities as well. The training programme shall also include awareness of the effects caused by loss of cabin pressure, hypoxia, human performance and the theory shall include as stated in ICAO Doc

chunks.heading: 2.7.1.1 Initial Training
chunks.text:
The goal of initial training is to ensure that each trainee acquired the competencies, knowledge and skill required to preform the duties and responsibilities related to the safety of passengers and flight during normal. abnormal and emergency situations The content of Initial training
1. Theory of Flight
2. Knowledge & operation of safety equipment carried on board
3. Safety and Emergency Procedures
4. Aircraft Specific
5. Aviation Security
6. First Aid and Medical emergencies
7. Transporting of dangerous goods by air
8. Human Factors and Crew Resource Management
9. Safety Management Systems
10. Human Trafficking A CCM shall be required to act as a CCM within 90 days of completion of regulatory training, if not fur- ther training or an assessment is required prior to undertaking flight duties as a CCM. Competency Based training shall include but not limited to,
1. SEP/Dangerous Goods Regulations

chunks.heading: 2.7.1.1 Initial Training
chunks.text:
2. Slide Drill/Ditching Drill/Firefighting drill
3. First Aid and Medical emergencies
4. Security & Self Defence Responses An assessment is required on completion of the respective training modules. The question papers, question bank for assessment, any amendment or revisions to the approved training Programme or as- sessments shall have prior approval of the DGCA.

chunks.text: 2.7.2 Training requirements and retention of records, The training section shall maintain training records of CCMs. The records shall be accessible to the CAASL. The guidelines are as per the regulatory training requirement.

chunks.heading: 2.7.3 Maintenance of Cabin Crew member Certificate
chunks.text: DGCA approved Cabin Safety Instructors shall ensure the successful completion of the CAASL approved Initial SEP Training programme as per SLCAP 4305 (Sri Lanka Civil Aviation Publication) prior to issuing a certificate.Once issued, a certificate shall be renewed annually by the holder attending and being suc- cessful at a re-current SEP training program approved by the CAASL as per SLCAP 4305. If a CCM is not scheduled for a recurrent training prior to the expiry, the CCM is required to inform the Cabin Safety Training Section in writing, two weeks prior to the date of expiry. CCM who fails an examination, a re sit will be permitted, if unsuccessful; the Cabin Safety Training Man- ager shall inform the DGCA and relieve the CCM from active flying duties. The Cabin Safety Training Manager may recommend further training and assessments. The CAASL requires that all CCMs hold a valid certificate to operate on a specific aircraft type and the

chunks.heading: 2.7.3 Maintenance of Cabin Crew member Certificate
chunks.text: CCM shall be in possession of it when reporting for flight duty.

chunks.heading: 2.7.4 Withdrawal of a Cabin Crew member Certificate
chunks.text: The CAASL Inspectors/Cabin Safety Training Manager may recommend to the DGCA for the withdrawal of a certificate of CCMs who are incompetent. The DGCA has the sole authority to withdraw the certifi- cate.

chunks.heading: 2.7.5 Familiarization Flights/Line Indoctrination (SNY)
chunks.text: Following successful completion of Initial training, CCMs shall operate at least two supernumerary flights/Line Indoctrination (SNY) on the aircraft types (One on each type) be carried out as specified in SLCAP 4305, supervised, and evaluated by a DGCA approved Cabin Safety Instructor. During the famil- iarization flight the cabin crew trainee shall be additional to the minimum number of operating CCMs. They shall not be identified as CCMs, shall not occupy cabin crew seats and impede operating CCM’s in their duties. The duration of a SNY flight shall be a minimum of one hour of actual flying time. The CCM shall operate supernumerary flights/Line Indoctrination (SNY) flights within 90 days of suc- cessful completion of safety training. On issuance of the CCMC, a CCM shall operate flights as a certified Crew member unless specified by the SriLankan Airlines Cabin Safety Section. On successful completion of operating flights on the aircraft type, a CCM may be recommended to

chunks.heading: 2.7.5 Familiarization Flights/Line Indoctrination (SNY)
chunks.text: operate another aircraft type on completion of a safety assessment carried out on board and being successful at a conversion-training programme. A CCM shall operate two supernumerary flights/ Line Indoctrination (SNY) flights (One on each type) supervised and evaluated by a DGCA approved Cabin Safety Instructor. The duration of a supernumerary flights/ Line Indoctrination (SNY) flight shall be a minimum of one hour of actual flying time. Failures shall be offered an additional supernumerary flights/ Line Indoctrination (SNY) flight evaluated by a DGCA approved Cabin Safety Instructor.

chunks.heading: 2.7.6 Recurrent Training
chunks.text: Recurrent training is conducted as specified by the SLCAP 4305 annually to ensure the maintenance of competencies, knowledge and skills through a series of hands-on exercises, simulated exercises, ex- ams etc., For general training elements relevant to each aircraft type on which the cabin crew member will be assigned duties. It may also be provided to familiarize crew members with new requirements, procedures and/or equipment introduced since their last training. Recurrent training ensures that cabin crew members, by practicing most competencies and skills, maintain the level of performance required for their duties and responsibilities. Recurrent training has a 12-month validity period counted from the end of the month the training was completed, The validity of the training expires on the last day of the month of previous training

chunks.heading: 2.7.6.1 Refresher Training Program
chunks.text: A subject specific Refresher Training Programme shall be conducted for a period of three days and completed with an assessment. If the CCM is unsuccessful at the assessment, CCM shall be referred to Admin.

chunks.heading: 2.7.7 Handing Over Regulatory Documents When On Long Leave
chunks.text: It is mandatory that regulatory documents are handed over to Cabin Safety Training section (Cabin Crew Members Certificate) and to Flight Operations Administration Manager (Crew Members Certificate) prior to commencement of “NO PAY” leave for over 30 days due to Maternity Leave, Long medical leave or being “OFF” the roster for disciplinary reasons/any other reasons. CCMs shall ensure the above doc- uments are repossessed from Cabin Safety Training Section and And Flight Operations Administration Manager on an office day prior to commencing flight duties.

chunks.heading: 2.7.8 Re-qualification Training for CCMs Returning for Flight Duty
chunks.text: If a CCM has been absent from all flying duties for a period not exceeding 30 days, and still remains within the period of validity of the previous Annual Recurrent Training, a Requlification Assessment is not required prior to being assigned flight duties. If a CCM has been absent from all flying duties for a period between 31 to 180 days and still remains within the period of validity of the previous Annual Recurrent Training, a Requlification Assessment as per training cycle 3 is required prior to being assigned flight duties. If the CCM is unsuccessful at the Requlification Assessment, CCM shall be referred to follow a Refresher Training programme. Ref 2.7.6.1 If a CCM has not been absent from all flying duties, but has not, during the preceding 90 days, under- taken duties on a type of aircraft as a CCM, prior to undertaking such duties on that particular aircraft type, the CCM shall carry out 01 SNY flight on the said aircraft type.

chunks.heading: 2.7.9 Re-qualification Training for CCMs Returning to Flight Duty after long Leave
chunks.text: CCMs on approved long leave or not undertaken flying duties for above 2 years (730 Days) shall follow Ab-Initio Safety Training Program, CCMs on approved long leave or not undertaken flying duties from 6 months (181 days) to 2 years (730 days) shall follow an Initial Safety Training program for Senior CCMs. CCMs are requires to be successful at the Ab-Initio Safety Training/Initial Safety Training program for Senior CCMs, prior to re-commencement of flight duty. If the CCM is unsuccessful at the Ab-Initio Safe- ty Training Program/Initial Safety Training program for Senior CCMs, a re-sit is offered on a scheduled day. If unsuccessful at the re-sit, the CCM may cease to continue duties as a CCM. CCMs that are successful will be detailed on 1 SNY flight on each certified aircraft type prior to been assigned for flight duty. An approved Cabin Safety Instructor shall conduct the onboard assessment on

chunks.heading: 2.7.9 Re-qualification Training for CCMs Returning to Flight Duty after long Leave
chunks.text: the CCMs knowledge on SEP and his competence/proficiency. The CCM shall operate on the certified aircraft type for a period determined by the SriLankan Airlines Cabin Safety Section and requires to be trained and be successful at a conversion-training program prior to being assigned to operate another type aircraft.

chunks.heading: 2.7.10 Mandatory onboard Assessments
chunks.text: Each CCM shall undergo a minimum of two mandatory safety onboard assessments for one calendar year, which shall be carried out on board an aircraft by a DGCA approved Cabin Safety Instructor. In the event a CCM is rated ‘C’ for an onboard assessment, CCM shall follow the training cycle 2 prior to been detailed for flight duties.

chunks.heading: 2.7.11 Operation of More Than One Type or Variations
chunks.text:
A CCM shall not operate more than three types of aircraft. However, with the approval of the DGCA, a CCM may operate on a fourth type if the safety equipment and emergency procedures for at least two aircraft types are similar in:
1. Emergency exit operation
2. Type of safety equipment
3. Location of safety equipment
4. Emergency procedures

chunks.heading: 2.7.11.1 Re-qualification Assessment
chunks.text: The re-qualification assessment shall be conducted by an instructor/assessor approved by the authori- ty. The assessment shall be a means for verification of the cabin crew members knowledge on all areas pertinent to the the operation . it shall include questions as a minimum on the following areas, Aircraft specifics/Safety and emergency procedures/Abnormal and Emergency procedures/Oxygen system and decompression/Dangerous goods regulations/First aid/AVSEC. Pass mark for the assessment shall be 90% with viva conducted and marked to 100%. The assessment papers shall have prior approval of the authority A Refresher Training Programme shall be carried out for CCMs who fail to obtain the required pass marks for the Requlification Assessment

chunks.heading: 2.8 Cabin Safety Instructors/Assessor
chunks.text: Cabin Safety Instructors shall be approved by the DGCA as stated and specified in SLCAIS 090. Once approved, they shall be authorised to conduct cabin safety training and CAASL required online evalua- tions. All safety training Instructors shall comply with requirements published in SLCAIS 89 & SLCAIS 90. Cabin Safety Instructors shall renew their certificates annually. The Cabin Safety Inspector (CAASL) shall carry out the evaluation and recommend to the DGCA for renewal. Cabin Safety Instructors shall be fully conversant with the Training Standard Manual (SLCAP 4305) and other requirements pertaining to safety and training. They shall constantly enhance their knowledge on safety training techniques in keeping with international standards. It is Mandatory that Cabin Safety Instructors train the CCMs on initial, conversion training and subject the successful CCMs for an onboard assessment to guide and enlighten them on SMS principles when

chunks.heading: 2.8 Cabin Safety Instructors/Assessor
chunks.text: on flight duty.

chunks.heading: 2.8.1 The Instructor Requirements For Onboard Assessment
chunks.text: As requried by SLCAP 4305 Cabin Crew Training Manual and SLCAIS 89 all manuals shall be kept current and updated. The Cabin Safety Instrucator shall always be satisfactorily current with the Safety Equip- ment/ Aircraft Systems/Standard Operation Procedures/ Safety and Emergency Procedures in order to ensure Cabin Crew are competent and constantly maintaining a high standard of safety management when on duty. It is mandatory for Cabin Safety Instructors to carry out a minimum of two onboard assessments on CCMs when on flight duty for each calendar year. To prevent confusion by passengers the Cabin Safety Instructor shall ensure that they do not perform tasks or wear a uniform in such a way that might identify them as members of the cabin crew. They Shall carry out duties of an instructor as stipulated in SLCAP 4305/ SLCAIS 89. In an emergency, the Cabin Safety Instructors shall act in the best interest of safety.

chunks.heading: 2.8.1 The Instructor Requirements For Onboard Assessment
chunks.text:
They shall also,
1. Monitor pre-flight briefings and communicate to the Cabin Safety Training Manager on recom- mendations for improvements
2. Observe and evaluate CCMs onboard and guide/encourage safety management systems throughout the flight duty period
3. Conduct checks on safety equipment/aircraft systems and safety information on board
4. Liaise with the Flight Crew & Engineering personnel on safety related issues
5. Communicate areas of concerns for continuous improvement to the Cabin Safety Training Man- ager
6. Be of guidance to CCMs on safety and emergency related issues.

chunks.heading: 2.8.2 Mandatory Pre Flight-Briefing
chunks.text:
CCMs reporting for flight duty shall be prepared in advance for the flight. Familiarization on the aircraft type is a key factor for safety awareness and safety management systems (SMS). Only the Purser/In- Charge CCM shall test the CCMs knowledge on SEP/DGR/Security and First Aid prior to each flight, to ensure all CCMs possess the required knowledge to handle an emergency situation. Purser/In-Charge shall not delegate same to cabin supervisors. If the knowledge is below accepted standards, and if the CCM concerned cannot be replaced, he shall not be allocated the duties of a door primary, and a report shall be forwarded to the Cabin Safety Training Manager. Guidance for a pre-flight testing/ briefing shall be as follows, Cabin Safety Training Pre Flight-Safety Briefing Cabin Safety Training FO/CST/001/23
