chunks.heading: 2.9.1 Cabin Crew member
chunks.text:
1. CCM’s shall comply with all safety related duties and instructions at all times as specified in the SEPM. CCMs shall be under the command of the PIC and be identified in SriLankan Airlines CCM uniform
2. Be responsible for the safety and security of the aircraft and it’s occupants from the time of boarding to disembarking.
3. CCMs shall be responsible for promptly notifying the PIC, by the quickest available means, of any aircraft accident resulting in serious injury or death to any person, or causing substantial damage to the aircraft or property
4. Follow and enforce company policies/procedures/regulatory requirements and standard operat- ing procedures (SOP) as specified
5. Be in possession and familiarize self with the contents of the SEPM and any subsequent amend- ments and revisions for reference during flight. This shall include all CSIs, CSNs and Safety Relat- ed Notices.
6. The aircraft shall not be left unattended whilst passengers are on board and CCM’s shall be vigi-

chunks.heading: 2.9.1 Cabin Crew member
chunks.text:
lant during catering and cleaning for any abnormalities.
7. Execute duties that relate to the safety of the aircraft and its occupants
8. CCM’s shall report to the PIC any observation/fault/failure/malfunction/defect including emer- gency systems, or any incident that endangers the airworthiness or safe operation of the aircraft if not already reported by another CCM.
9. CCMs shall be responsible for their personal baggage and shall not leave them unattended at any time and if lost shall report same to the authority immediately. CCMs shall ensure, baggage left at layover stations are locked for security reasons
10. CCM’s shall comply with all applicable flight time, flight duty period, duty period limitations and rest period requirements.

chunks.heading: 2.9.2 In Charge Cabin Crew Training
chunks.text:
Cabin Crew members who are identified and promoted as Pursers and Cabin Supervisors shall receive a specialised leadership training in accordance with the applicable regulations and standards of the oper- ator prior to being assigned duties.
1. Responsibilities to the commander
2. Briefing of CCMs - normal, abnormal, emergency situations
3. Safety briefing of passengers
4. Accident & Incident reporting
5. Documentation
6. Leadership
7. Decision making

chunks.heading: 2.9.2 In Charge Cabin Crew Training
chunks.text:
8. Individual and team responsibilities
9. Effective two way communication
10. Flight time, Flight duty period, Rest period
11. CRM and human factors

chunks.heading: 2.10 Purser/In-Charge CCM
chunks.text:
SriLankan Airlines operates flights with a Purser appointed, whenever assigning more than one CCM for flight duty. The Purser shall be acceptable to the authority, under the command of the PIC, and be responsible to the PIC for the conduct/co-ordination of normal, abnormal and emergency procedures as specified and shall,
1. Ensure the required number of CCMs are available for duty
2. Ensure self and all detailed CCMs are in possession of valid regulatory documents and an updat- ed SEP Manual for guidance and reference.
3. Purser/In-Charge crew shall be responsible to check the cabin crewmember certificates (Blue Dockets) of all CCMs to ensure the currency of the following before operating each flight, The pages to be checked are,
• Page I - Personal Information
• Page III – Validity of SEP
• Page V – Validity of Medical Records
• Page VI – Validity of the certificate and Special Endorsements (CCC)

chunks.heading: 2.10 Purser/In-Charge CCM
chunks.text:
• Page VII – Validity of Competency Training
4. Assign duties/responsibilities to CCMs as required for each flight.
5. Brief and test CCMs on the safety competencies prior to each flight
6. Ensure the Pre-departure Safety and Security checks are carried out, VR signed
7. Conduct a briefing with the PIC prior to depature. Obtain code red and hijack alert (denied entry code) and communicate the hijack alert to the CCMs
8. Ensure, all laid down procedures /SOP’s are adhered to by all CCMs
9. Be responsible for the health/safety of the operating CCMs and the passengers
10. Be responsible for the discipline of all CCMs, whilst on duty/on company time
11. Be responsible to ensure safety regulations are adhered to in the cabin
12. Brief CCMs on routine door operations
13. Be responsible to prepare for an emergency when instructed by the PIC
14. Carry out systems check on FAP for defects; and an “ALL STN” call for serviceability.

chunks.heading: 2.10 Purser/In-Charge CCM
chunks.text:
15. Pre-flight check on the logged defects, keep the PIC/Engineer and CCMs informed. Concerns or missing items in reference to the MEL, shall be logged immediately and communicated to the PIC and the Engineer for airworthiness.
16. Report technical irregularities in the cabin in consultation with the PIC
17. Ensure documentation is completed as specified

chunks.heading: 2.10 Purser/In-Charge CCM
chunks.text:
18. Be vigilant and responsible for the general safety and security at all times
19. Report to the Cabin Safety Training Manager on safety related concerns or of any deviations to laid down service procedures due to safety concerns
20. Ensure SOP’s are followed when the aircraft is on ground or in flight
21. Be responsible for effective man management to enable the crew to react efficiently in case of an emergency
22. Brief CCMs to be vigilant on Personnel (Authorised/Unauthorised) entering the aircraft and the nature of duties carried out by them
23. Ensure the following details are completed on the General Declaration (GD) on all sectors before landing.
• Declaration of health (Any Pax with symptoms stated))
• Details of disinsection (Number of aerosol cans sprayed)
• Total Passenger count (Indicated on right corner)
• Signature of Purser/In Charge CCM at the bottom
• Counter signed by the Pilot in Command

chunks.heading: 2.10 Purser/In-Charge CCM
chunks.text:
24. Positioning/Dead Heading Cabin crewmembers, In the absence of a Purser/In-charge CCM, the operating Purser shall check the validity of the CCMC, medical and training records.
25. Shall check the Passenger Information List (PIL) for special handling passengers and the type of assistance required and communicate same to the rest of the crew through the cabin supervi- sors before depature and will ensure the relevant assistance is provided upon arrival. If wheel- chair/Ambu lift is not available on arrival same should be coordinated with the ramp cooridnator

chunks.heading: 2.10.1 Nomination of a Purser from-base
chunks.text: In the absence of the assigned Purser, a Cabin Supervisor who has completed a minimum 3 years of flight duties in the category of Cabin Supervisor shall be assigned to operate a certified type of aircraft. He will carry the designation of Acting Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.10.2 Replacing the Operating Purser during flight
chunks.text: In the event the scheduled Purser is unable to continue to operate the flight, SriLankan Airlines shall assign the next most senior Cabin Supervisor to operate as the Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.10.3 Purser Relieved Of Duty
chunks.text: When the Purser relieves himself from in-flight duty, The PIC shall be informed and the Purser shall nominate a Cabin Supervisor to be responsible for Purser’s duties. The Purser shall re-brief the Cabin Supervisor of the (code red/hijack alert). In the event of an emergency, the Purser shall takeover re- sponsibilities.

chunks.heading: 2.10.4 Under The Supervision of Purser/Cabin Supervisor
chunks.text: The Purser or in his absence the Cabin Supervisor shall be in charge of and has authority over all CCMs on duty regardless of the years of experience.

chunks.heading: 2.10.5 Responsibilities of Primary Crew Member
chunks.text: A CCM who has been assigned as a door primary for a designated door/exit shall carry out routine and emergency operations. When there are two Cabin Crew seats located at a door, the Primary Crew shall sit at the outboard seat.

chunks.heading: 2.10.6 Exception to the Primary Crew Member
chunks.text: The door assist at L1 station, shall be responsible for the safety equipment check at L1 and L1A.

chunks.heading: 2.10.7 Responsibilities of Assist Crew Member
chunks.text: The designated CCM shall sit at the inboard seat and assist the Primary Crew to carry out routine and emergency operations.

chunks.heading: 2.11 Flight Time Limitation
chunks.text: State limitations applicable for flight time, duty periods and rest periods for CCMs employed to operate in aircraft/airlines registered in Sri Lanka for public transport is contained in SLCAIS 054 and SLCAP 4210. CCMs shall be guided by the Flight Operations Manual (FOM) - Chapter 08 Flight time limitation training shall be carried out as per approved Srilankan Airlines Cabin Crew Train- ing Standards Manual. CCM requiring clarification shall contact the crew-scheduling department with specific details. CCMs may address concerns on his personal schedule in writing. The records shall be maintained by the crew scheduling department for a minimum period of 15 months

chunks.heading: PROCEDURE
chunks.text:
1. Purser is responsible to ensure that CCM’s adheres to crew rest procedures and requirements.
2. Purser shall determine the allocation of crew rest time.
3. Purser shall advise the PIC prior to application of the crew rest.
4. Half the number CCMs shall be active in the cabin at all times.
5. Prior to the Purser commencing his rest a senior CCM shall be appointed to carry out his duties and the PIC shall be kept informed.
6. Crew rest will commence after completion of inflight meal service.
7. Purser may disrupt or cease crew rest at any time should in-flight circumstances require (emer- gency/medical etc.)

chunks.heading: 2.11.2 Fatigue Management System (FMS)
chunks.text: A data-driven flexible alternative to prescriptive flight and duty time limitations which is based upon scientifically valid principles and measurements, and which involves a continuous process of monitoring and managing fatigue within the context of Srilankan’ Safety Management System

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: Authority, Duties and Responsibilities of the Pilot in Command The PIC assumes command the moment he enters the aircraft with the intention of operating a flight. His command continues until relieved either by another Commander/suitably qualified Pilot or until the termination of the flight when he completes all post flight documents and leaves the aircraft. Duties and responsibilities of the PIC are laid down in various parts of the Flight Operation Administra- tion Manual. It is, however, intended to bring to the attention of a Commander, important aspects of his responsibilities in the operation and conduct of a flight. The PIC is responsible for the safety and security of the aircraft and all crew, passengers and cargo. He will supervise and direct the other members of the crew in the proper discharge of their duties. He is responsible for the safe operation of flights, regulatory compliance, efficiency, on time performance,

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: courtesy, passenger comfort and economy of operation. He has the necessary authority to carry out the above responsibilities. The PIC whether handling the controls or not is responsible for the operation of the aircraft in accord- ance with rules of the air except that he may depart from these rules in circumstances that render such departure absolutely necessary in the interest of safety. It is incumbent on the PIC to comply with laws, regulations and procedures of the state in which the air- craft is flown. This includes complying with all health, customs and immigration laws in force. He shall ensure that no crew member violates any of these laws and no contraband or unauthorized articles are placed anywhere on board the aircraft. If an emergency situation arises which endangers the safety of the aircraft or personnel and necessitates taking action, which involves violation of local regulations or

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: procedures, the PIC shall notify the appropriate local authority without delay. A report shall be submitted of any such emergency action to the DGCA through the Senior Manager Flight Operations as soon as possible. All Crew Members will report to the PIC to enable him to give specific instruction, if any, regarding the conduct of the flight. He shall ensure that the crews are on board well in time and all pre-departure procedures and safety checks are completed. Should a Commander’s duties detain him and he is una- ble to board the aircraft before the passengers he must ensure that all preparations are made by the re- mainder of the crew so that departure can be made avoiding a delay, once he has boarded the aircraft. The PIC is responsible for ensuring that all passengers are fully briefed on safety procedures and that all safety exits are unobstructed during taxi take off and landing. PIC shall ensure that all equipment and

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: baggage are properly secured for take off, landing and whenever deemed necessary in the interest of safety and security The primary responsibility of the PIC is that he must not commence a flight when in his judgment the aircraft is not in a satisfactory condition to maintain a high level of safety. It is his obligation to report to the management Flight Operations regarding any areas of operation, which could be detrimental to safety. The PIC is responsible for filling de-briefing reports and ensuring reporting of accidents/inci- dents.

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text:
In the absence of SriLankan Airlines ground personnel the PIC during his period of command is respon- sible for the safety of the aircraft, passengers, crew and their comfort while on the ground. He shall make all efforts to mobilize available resources until SriLankan Airlines ground personnel are available to takeover and resume their responsibilities. The PIC has the necessary statutory authority to carry out his responsibilities during his period of command and exercise this authority over all crew and pas- sengers at any stage when on duty. This authority is without question and any disagreement shall be furnished in writing after compliance. The authority of the PIC is final irrespective of the rank/position of the passengers or the crew. 2.12.1.1 The Pilot in Command Has Full Authority Over:
1. All members of his crew on duty and off duty when away from home base.
2. His passengers during flight, i.e. from closing until opening of the cabin doors.

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text:
3. The final authority as to the disposition of the aircraft while in command.
4. Supervision and direct other members of the crew in the proper discharge of their duties while under his command. It is incumbent on all crew members to carry out the instructions of the PIC at all times.
5. All air crew are subject to the disciplinary control of the PIC from the time they report to him at the airport till the completion of the flight duty and return to home base.
6. All air crew are responsible to the PIC for their competency and knowledge of, emergency proce- dures as well as the location and use of emergency equipment.
7. To ensure that the above responsibilities of air crew are enforced at overseas stations:
8. The PIC is responsible for ensuring that the provisions of the Air Navigation Act with regard to the airworthiness, equipment and the operation of aircraft are fully complied with.

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text:
2.12.1.2 The Pilot in Command will ensure,
1. All necessary equipment/documentation for the flight are on board the aircraft.
2. The aircraft is loaded in accordance with prescribed regulations in the Weight and Balance Man- ual. (Specified for each aircraft)
3. His crew members are currently licensed to perform their duties and have in their possession valid travel and health documents and are within stipulated flight and duty time limitations;
4. He is expected to make himself known to the passengers in the air and on the ground. When circumstances permit, regular in-flight announcements should be made to keep passengers informed of the progress of the flight.
5. When making up lost time, the PIC must be satisfied that his crew will not be excessively fa- tigued and the destinations ahead can adapt to the amended schedule. The PIC and his crew will complete such reports as the Head of Flight Operations and or relevant au-

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: thority requires in respect of the flight. It is his duty to be knowledgeable of the circumstances, which would warrant the filing of a report. The PIC shall ensure that check-lists and SOP’s as laid down are properly used by crew members at ap-

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: propriate stages of flight. Only in extraordinary circumstances, and then only after specifically briefing the crew, will procedures other than SOPs be used. The PIC shall be responsible for bringing to the at- tention of the ground engineers all known or suspected defects of the aircraft. The PIC has the authority and responsibility to declare an emergency whenever deemed necessary. As far as practically possible, he shall keep the appropriate air traffic control centre fully informed of the progress of the flight, his intentions, and any action taken in such a situation. The PIC has the authority to disembark any person including CCM or any part of cargo that may pose a potential hazard to the safety and security of the aircraft or it’s occupants. PIC may refuse passengers including inadmissible passengers, deportees or persons in custody or disruptive passengers if they still behave in an objectionable and offensive man-

chunks.heading: 2.12.1 Authority of the PIC
chunks.text: ner or refuse to follow orders given for their own or other passenger’s comfort, safety and security. Persons intoxicated and or under the influence of narcotics shall be refused boarding.

chunks.heading: 2.12.2 Chain Of Command While On Duty
chunks.text:
1. Pilot In Command (PIC)
2. Captain or Cruise Captain
3. Cruise Pilot or First Officer
4. Junior First Officer
5. Trainee Junior First Officer/Cadet Pilot
6. Purser
7. Cabin Supervisor
8. Cabin Crew members in order of seniority
9. Positioning Flight Crew Note - In the case of pilot incapacitation, any suitably qualified positioing flight crew may utilized in accordance with chain of command

chunks.heading: 2.12.3 Authorisation to Enter Flight Deck
chunks.text: No person other than a Flight Crew assigned to operate a flight shall have access to the flight deck un- less authorized by the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.12.4 Authorisation to occupy a flight Deck Observer Seat
chunks.text:
The PIC may authorize a non-revenue passenger to occupy a Flight Deck observer seat with the follow- ing conditions:
1. Above 14 years of age.
2. Not suffering from an ailment which impairs his free movement.
3. Briefed on safety/emergency procedures and security requirements by Flight Crew.
4. Not under the influence of alcohol/drugs
5. Shall not be served/consume alcohol
6. Of good judgment, the person would not endanger the aircraft or its occupants Note - Briefing for passengers occupying flight deck observers seat shall be done by the flight crew. Ensure passenger is seated before the flight deck door is closed

chunks.heading: 2.12.5 Authorisation to Occupy a Cabin Crew Seat
chunks.text:
The PIC may authorize a non-revenue passenger to occupy a CCM assist seat with the same conditions applicable for occupation of a Flight Deck observer seat. CCM shall brief on safety/emergency proce- dures and security requirements. The ground staff shall inform the Purser in advance when allocating a CCM seat to a passenger. Note - A321 L2/R3 Crew Seats Shall be allocated only to a non-revenue, able-bodied adult above 18 years who appear to be capable of operating or assisting with the operation of the exit 2.12.6 Briefing passengers occupying a CCM assist seat, In the event a cabin crew assist seat is occupied by a passenger, the following briefing shall be conduct- ed,
1. The seat is a foldable seat and the usage of the seat belt
2. The location and the use of the Life Vest
3. Drop down oxygen system
4. Ordinance signs display location
5. Closest and alternate exits

chunks.heading: 2.12.7 Secure Flight Deck Door
chunks.text: SriLankan Airlines operated aircraft are equipped with a secure flight deck door. It is designed to resist penetration by small arms fire, grenade shrapnel and resist forcible intrusion by unauthorised persons. It is fully compliant with rapid decompression requirements.

chunks.heading: 2.12.8 Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text:
Unauthorized persons are prohibited access to the flight deck. Flight Crew shall ensure the immediate vicinity of the door is clear and may require a CCM to move passenger(s) from the galley area prior to unlocking the door in compliance with CAASLIS 033. CCMs shall ensure the following,
1. The door shall be kept closed/locked at all times
2. Be vigilant to prevent any person from trying to enter the flight deck
3. When entering the flight deck, ensure the lavatory adjacent to the flight deck is vacant
4. Once communicated with Flight Crew, face the video monitor above the door for identification

chunks.heading: 2.12.9 Sterile Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text: For departures - Duration of the Sterile Flight Deck shall be from the time the Flight Deck Door is closed for the purpose of push back & until such time the SEAT BELT sign is switched off after the initial ascent. For arrivals - Duration of the Sterile Flight Deck shall be from the time the SEAT BELT sign is selected on before the commencement of the Descent until the seat belt sign is switched off after landing. Note : Sterile Flight Deck Policy Is Maintained To Prevent Any Interruption To The Flight Crew Work- flow, Which May Cause Distraction As This Is The Critical Phases Of The Flight.

chunks.heading: 2.12.9 Sterile Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text:
If it is clearly identified as an emergency, which requires the immediate attention of the PIC, a CCM shall press “PRIO Capt”/”EMER call” on the interphone to inform the PIC. Such situations arising during flight shall also be communicated to the PIC at the earliest, It shall be, but not limited to,
1. Fire/burning odour/smoke outside or inside of the aircraft
2. Critical medical emergency- Injury or Illness Crew/Passenger
3. Unusual noise or vibration
4. Fuel or other fluid leaking from the aircraft
5. Door/ Slide being unable to be closed/ locked/unlocked / armed/disarmed
6. Suspicious/unclaimed bag or package
7. Passengers behaving aggressively or potentially dangerous

chunks.heading: 2.12.10 Common language and safe two-way Communication Practices
chunks.text:
Flight Crew and Cabin Crew shall communicate in English at all times as a regulatory requirement. Two-way communication between the Cabin and the Flight Crew shall be via the inter phone during normal, abnormal and emergency situations. In case these systems do not work, during PIC and Purser Briefing: Specific alternate communication methods shall be determined and briefed before the flight. Crew shall use standard wording, terminology, and specified verbal commands for all types of commu- nication with the flight crew.
1. CCM shall use the code red to enter the flight deck if Flight Crew incapacitation is suspected.
2. CCM shall follow instructions of PIC in the event of a suspected hijack situation.
3. CCM’s shall constantly monitor the Flight Deck door area and bring to the notice of the PIC, if a suspected event is taking place or likely to take place in the aircraft.
4. CCM shall use “PRIO CAPT”/”EMER call” to inform PIC of any, but not limited to any Safety/secu-

chunks.heading: 2.12.10 Common language and safe two-way Communication Practices
chunks.text:
rity/medical emergencies
5. During in-flight rest periods, any request from the operating flight crew to wake the Commander or any resting flight crew member shall be acted upon without delay Flight Information - The Purser shall obtain relevant information required for the flight during the PIC/ Purser briefing. Ref 2.14.2 

chunks.heading: 2.12.11 Flight Deck Service
chunks.text:
CCMs shall be cautious when serving beverages in the Flight Deck to avoid spillage on the center con- sole. Beverages shall be offered less than ¾ full, placed on a tray and offered on the left side to the PIC and on the right side to the First-Officer. All glasses and crockery shall be cleared from the flight deck before every take-off and landing.
1. Clearance for Take-off: Prior to closing the last cabin door
2. Clearance for Landing: Once “Cabin Crew Prepare Cabin for Landing” announcement is made
3. Ensure the similar type of food is not offered to both Flight Crew members.

chunks.heading: 2.12.12 Checking on Flight Crew
chunks.text: It is mandatory that CCMs check on the well-being of the Flight Crew every thirty minutes on all appro- priate flights. Safe two way communication procedures shall be practiced.Prior to opening of the flight deck door, Flight crew to check with Cabin crew if surrounding area is free of passengers.

chunks.heading: 2.12.13 Flight Crew two-man operation
chunks.text:
In a two-man flight deck operation, it is mandatory that a cabin crew member is positioned in the flight deck prior to the flight crew member leaving the station and until the flight crew member has returned. When a Flight Crew member requires leaving the Flight Deck, it is the duty of the Flight Crew member to inform a CCM. Ref SLCAIS 33
1. CCM shall disengage from other duties, inform the Purser and enter the flight deck.
2. Position self, close to the locking device on the flight deck door.
3. Remain until the Flight Crew member returns to the flight deck. Flight Crew member shall follow the standard entry procedure to enter the flight deck.
4. In the event of a pilot incapacitation, emergency or any other abnormal situation or behaviour takes place, CCM shall Open door, summon for assistance and remain in the flight deck.
5. CCM shall also be familiar with the opening, closing and locking/unlocking the flight deck door

chunks.heading: 2.12.13 Flight Crew two-man operation
chunks.text: from inside the flight deck. Note: In the event the door is locked electrically, it can be overridden by using the door handle manually from inside.

chunks.heading: 2.13.1 Minimums for each aircraft
chunks.text: It is a requirement that SriLankan Airlines shall establish, to the satisfaction of the DGCA, the minimum number of CCMs required to be operating on each aircraft type, based on the seating capacity and the number of floor level exits of the aircraft type. The minimum crew compliment required to operate each aircraft type shall be as follows covering the specified exits.

chunks.heading: OCCUPIED

chunks.heading: 2.13.2 Inexperienced cabin crew members
chunks.text: The number of inexperienced cabin crew members to be present on board the aircraft shall be deter- mined based on the aircraft type/variant. A CCM shall be considered as “inexperienced” and should be detailed as assist crew member until they complete 20 sectors (A321 - L2 or R3) The 20 sectors shall commence from the date a Cabin Crew Member Certificate has been issued by CAASL. Each flight operated shall be documented by the individ- ual CCM along with the signature of the Purser/In-Charge CCM on the document provided.

chunks.heading: 2.13.3 Ferry Flight with Cabin Crew
chunks.text:
When an aircraft is dispatched without any passengers, CCMs shall ensure for take-off and landing:
1. Galleys/lavatories are secured.
2. All doors/slides are closed, armed/disarmed and cross checked.
3. Indicate cabin ready to the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.13.4 Operation of Flights under Exceptional Circumstances
chunks.text: In unforeseen circumstances, the required number of CCMs may be reduced in accordance with proce- dures acceptable to the DGCA and a report shall be submitted to the DGCA on completion of the flight.

chunks.heading: 2.13.5 VVIP Flights
chunks.text: Prior approval shall be obtained from DGCA to operate with less than the required minimum number of CCMs. All slides shall be armed/disarmed, cross checked for take-off and landing. (Cross checking shall be carried out by the opposite door primary, where available) The purser shall delegate the exits to be occupied.

chunks.heading: 2.13.6 Non-Revenue Flights
chunks.text:
The following flights are categorized as non-revenue flights.
1. Ferry Flights
2. Delivery Flights
3. Positioning Flights When such flights are operated with additional personnel such as cargo loaders, Load sheet officers, other than Positioning/Dead Heading tech and cabin crew the following procedure shall be carried out,
1. All additional personnel names shall appear on the general declaration (GD).
2. A safety demonstration shall be carried out indicating the use of seat belts, oxygen mask, brac- ing positions and exits to be used before take-off. In case the safety demonstration cannot be carried out they shall be briefed individually using the safety card.
3. Required doors (L1/R1) or as required shall be armed/disarmed following SOPs.
4. Cabin shall be secured ensuring all carry-on baggage is stowed as per SOPs and PIC informed.
5. Ensure they remain seated during taxi, take-off and landing with the seat belt secured and seat-

chunks.heading: 2.13.6 Non-Revenue Flights
chunks.text:
backs in the upright position.
6. They shall be advised not to enter restricted areas such as galleys and flight deck unless required by the operating crew.
7. Announcements shall be made pertaining to turbulence, abnormal and emergency situations and CCMs shall ensure instructions are followed.
8. No smoking policy shall be strictly adhered to and they shall not be permitted to obstruct the duties of tech/cabin crew.

chunks.heading: 2.13.7 Upgrading A320 /321 to A330
chunks.text:
If an A 321/320 aircraft is upgraded to an A 330 operation, the minimum crew complement shall be six (6) provided the following conditions are adhered to,
1. Passenger load is limited to
• A320 – 162 passengers
• A 321- 188 passengers.
2. Doors L1/R1, L2/R2, L3 and R4 are manned by CCMs
3. The CCM responsible for L3 shall be responsible for R3 door and the safety equipment at L3/R3 doors/respective areas
4. The CCM responsible for R4 shall be responsible for L4 door and the safety equipment at L4/R4 doors/respective areas All slides shall be armed/ disarmed for take-off and landing.
5. If and when such a flight is operated necessary CAA approvals are obtained NOTE: The passenger load shall not exceed the maximum load capacity on the particular aircraft type available in the fleet.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8 Incapacitated CCM
chunks.text: A CCM who has reported for duty and subsequently unfit to perform his duties in the aircraft due to injury, medication, sickness of other similar causes, or CCM is in any doubt of being able to accomplish assigned duties or knows of suspects that CCM is suffering from fatigue or feeling otherwise unfit, to the extent that the flight may be endangered

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.1 Prior to Departure ex Base
chunks.text: The PIC shall be informed, CCM offloaded, and appropriate documentation completed by the Purser and forwarded to the Cabin Safety Section. Another CCM shall be nominated to operate the flight.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.2 Prior to departure en-route
chunks.text: If the CCM cannot be replaced, the PIC shall be informed for guidance.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.3 Incapacitated Door Primary During Flight
chunks.text: The PIC shall be informed, and the Purser shall re-delegate door primary duties to another CCM. The incapacitated CCM shall act as a passenger.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.4 Prior to Departure - Minimum Crew Operation (ex. Other Stations)
chunks.text: If the CCM cannot be replaced, PIC to be informed for guidance.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.5 During Flight - Minimum Crew Operation
chunks.text: One CCM incapacitated The PIC shall be informed and an ABP shall be selected and briefed accordingly. The ABP shall be relo- cated to a passenger seat, closest to the crew seat. More than One CCM incapacitated The PIC shall be informed and the remaining CCMs shall be re delegated to cover the most appropri- ate doors. ABPs shall be selected and briefed accordingly to cover all unmanned doors. The ABPs shall be relocated to passenger seats, which is closest to the relevant crew seats. The seat shall be placarded as “Crew seat”.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.6 Purser Incapacitated During Flight
chunks.text: The PIC shall be informed, and the next most suitable CS shall take over duties.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.7 Cabin Crewmember Injury/Sickness
chunks.text:
Holders of Class II (Cabin Crew) medical certificates shall seek aero-medical advice from UL Medical Centre/GMO/CMO to assess their medical fitness and decide whether they are fit to exercise the privi- leges of their license, as stipulated in SLCAIS 36, when they:
1. Have undergone a surgical operation or invasive procedure.
2. Have commenced the regular use of any medication.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.7 Cabin Crewmember Injury/Sickness
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
3. Have suffered any significant personal injury involving incapacity to function as a member of the flight crew.
4. Have been suffering from any significant illness involving incapacity to function as a member of the flight crew.
5. Are pregnant.
6. Has been admitted to hospital or medical clinic.
7. First, require correcting lenses. If a CCM has been injured or fallen sick, and/or is unable to perform his duties, during a layover, on ground at the airport or inflight, the following shall be applicable:
1. Prior to reporting for a flight, if a CCM has sustained an injury, fallen sick, he shall consult the GMO/CMO and obtain ‘fit to fly’ clearance prior to operating the flight.
2. During flight - Page for a medical practitioner and obtain a medical assessment on the illness report.
3. During flight- If a medical practitioner is unavailable and if any medication is administered to a

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.7 Cabin Crewmember Injury/Sickness
chunks.text:
CCM a medication consent form, Illness report shall be submitted along with other reports if available.
4. On ground - Medical assistance will be obtained as appropriate through the layover hotels res- ident, on-call doctor OR emergency medical services OR At the airport; A medical assessment shall be obtained on the illness report.
5. During a layover or on ground at the airport - If a CCM has been injured or fallen sick and/or is unable to perform his duties, the Purser shall inform the PIC. The PIC shall inform the station staff and the AOCC.
6. The PIC shall contact the UL Medical Centre/Company Medical Officer (GMO/CMO), through the AOCC. The injured /sick CCM shall not be used for flight duties until a ‘Fit to Fly’ clearance has been issued by the GMO/CMO. The ‘Fit to Fly’ clearance shall be communicated (company email and verbally to the PIC, by the AOCC. This shall be indicated on the voyage report along with an

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.7 Cabin Crewmember Injury/Sickness
chunks.text:
incident/accident report and the illness report/s.
7. If a Cabin Crewmember appears injured or sick, but states that he/she is fit to operate the flight; the PIC shall be responsible to take the final decision.
8. If the CCM is unable to carry out his duties a replacement CCM will be allocated by crew sched- uling department. If a replacement CCM is not allocated, the flight shall be operated taking into consideration a minimum crew operation. If not the passenger load shall be reduced using the inoperative door procedure as guidance. Ref 2.32 Note 1: During layovers, the PIC shall be authorized and responsible for managing any cabin crew- member injury/sickness scenarios. Note 2: If a Cabin crewmember appears injured or sick, but states that he is fit to operate the flight; the PIC shall be responsible to take the final decision. Note 3: When required chain of command documented in SEP manual Ref: 2.12.2 shall be applica-

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.7 Cabin Crewmember Injury/Sickness
chunks.text: ble for the above procedure.

chunks.heading: 2.13.8.8 Inter Personal Conflicts Between CCMs
chunks.text: Cases of personal conflict arising from, personal differences, misunderstandings, disagreements, or incompatible expectations or needs. Situations of this nature should be immediately addressed by the Purser/In-Charge crew , who should act as the neutral mediator to resolve it and ensure smooth functioning of the in-flight operation continues.If the CCM feels emotionally traumatized, CCM should consult the GMO/CMO and obtain fit to fly clearance before operating the flight.

chunks.heading: 2.14.1 Cabin Crew Pre Flight-Safety Briefing
chunks.text:
1. It is mandatory only the Purser/In-Charge CCM shall conduct a pre-flight safety briefing as re- quired prior to operating a flight and ensure:
2. CCMs are in possession of an updated copy of the SEP Manual(e-manual)
3. Verify all CCMs are in possession of valid CAASL, Crew Member Certificate (white ID), CCM Cer- tificate (Blue docket),
4. The CCMs are in possession of items indicated in point 3 for immediate verification
5. All CCMs are aircraft type certified
6. All CCMs possess the required knowledge to handle normal, abnormal and emergency situa- tions.
7. All CCMs are current and knowledgeable on the operating aircraft
8. Assign work position and responsibilities to CCMs
9. Ensure the CCMs clearly understand their role and responsibilities
10. Provide additional information. The CCMs shall be provided with briefing rooms/areas at base and at lay over stations. In the event of a delayed reporting or any other restriction, crew shall proceed to the aircraft directly and conduct the

chunks.heading: 2.14.1 Cabin Crew Pre Flight-Safety Briefing
chunks.text: mandatory safety briefing prior to the commencement of Pre-departure duties.

chunks.heading: 2.14.2 PIC/Purser Briefing
chunks.text:
The PIC shall conduct a pre-flight briefing with the Purser/In-Charge CCM regarding the flight and at his discretion may carry out a general briefing for all CCMs including the following but not limited to,
1. Purser shall hand over to the PIC the signed Pre-departure Safety and Security checklist con- firming all responsibilities are completed
2. Confirm CCM names on the GD
3. Purser has carried out a pre-flight safety briefing for CCMs
4. Confirm all CCM’s records/documents are in order
5. Distance of taxi way or to the runway
6. Estimated flight time and Anticipated weather
7. PIC shall be notified of any passengers with alerts
8. Functioning of the security camera
9. Emergency two way communication (Inclusive of medical situations)

chunks.heading: 2.14.2 PIC/Purser Briefing
chunks.text:
10. Normal/ abnormal/ emergency situations
11. A hijack alert and the code red for the secure flight deck door

chunks.heading: 2.14.3 Passenger Safety Briefing/ Demonstrations
chunks.text: Appropriate passenger safety briefings/demonstrations shall be carried out as stipulated by the DGCA. It is mandatory to carry out the safety demonstration prior to take off. The CCMs shall ensure all lavato- ries are checked /locked/ and all passengers are seated prior to the head count and safety demonstra- tion.

chunks.heading: 2.14.4 Passenger Safety Announcements/Briefings
chunks.text:
1. Pre departure safety announcement
2. After take-off/during flight announcements
3. Turbulence announcements
4. Top-of-descent announcement - Ref 2.15.5
5. Pre-landing announcement
6. Demonstration of exits on flights, four hours or more
7. Aerodrome restrictions (if applicable)
8. After landing announcement/use of PED/Remain seated
9. Briefing passengers with alerts - Ref 2.24
10. Briefing on special doors/hatch operations - Ref 6A.6/2.14.6/2.25.2

chunks.heading: 2.14.5 Safety Information Card
chunks.text:
Passengers are provided with a Safety information card which is easily accessible, Which contains ap- propriate information, instructions, restrictions and locations relevant to but not limited to
1. Seat Belts, Passenger oxygen masks
2. Emergency Exits, emergency path lighting (If Applicable)
3. Life jackets, Bracing positions
4. Smoking restrictions

chunks.heading: 2.14.6 Preflight briefing for Pax seated at the emergency exits
chunks.text:
The Passengers occupying seats adjacent to the emergency exits shall be briefed prior to departure as stated below:
1. CCM shall introduce self
2. State that the passengers are seated next to an emergency exit (point to the exit)
3. Inquire the willingness to help in an emergency (If not change seating and keep Purser informed)
4. Act on command of CCM/s
5. Inform pax to refer the safety card for door operation (show safety card)

chunks.heading: 2.14.6 Preflight briefing for Pax seated at the emergency exits
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
6. Check for any clarifications

chunks.heading: 2.14.7 Communicating Safety Concerns of Passengers
chunks.text:
When a passenger requires the attention of a CCM in relation to a safety concern, CCM shall pay com- plete attention to passenger’s concern and:
1. Shall not pre determine the concern
2. Clarify all doubts/specific details and thank the passenger
3. Informing the PIC, timely and specifically
4. If the concern is of an emergency, the CCM shall inform the PIC immediately by pressing “PRIO CAPT” / ”EMER CALL” on the handset.
5. Preventive measures should be communicated by the PIC through the Purser
6. Communicate the feedback to the passenger. Purser shall report such concerns to the Cabin Safety Training Manager

chunks.heading: 2.15 Cabin Crew Member Duties
chunks.text: CCM’s safety related duties are categorised according to the phases of flight such as, Pre-departure /push-back/taxi/take-off/ascent/cruise/descent/approach/landing/after landing.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2 Pre-Departure
chunks.text:
CCMs shall stow their baggage in the allocated location. Each CCM shall carry out the mandatory safety and security checks but not limited to, when boarding an aircraft for duty, during a crew change and on completion of any maintenance work performed. Safety Equipment Check Lists referred to as quick reference charts (QRC) are located under each primary crew seat with safety equipment locations for the relevant station. CCM shall confirm the safety equipment accuracy by placing the signature on the voyage report. Cabin Supervisors shall carry out a mini safety briefing to stress on key areas of safety concerns and to ensure CCMs carry out the safety and security checks prior to boarding of passengers. The checks shall consist of the following but not limited to, serviceability/ correct location/correct num- ber /correctly secured and clear from obstruction.
1. Portable Safety/ Survival Equipment

chunks.heading: 2.15.2 Pre-Departure
chunks.text:
2. Demo equipment/ Safety equipment guided by the QRC
3. Passenger Seats, Crew Seat, Seat Belt and Harness
4. P.A. and Inter-phone
5. Emergency Doors
6. Safety and security check in lavatories
7. Relevant Passenger Safety Cards/ Disruptive Passenger Information Leaflet
8. Crew / Passenger life vests
9. Security check in stowage compartments
10. Locking and restraining devices in the galleys
11. Security check-to ensure the aircraft is free of any foreign objects or unauthorized personnel on board.
12. Surveillance cameras are not obstructed.
13. A320/A321 - Check if the snap hook is attached to the survival pack Identified defects or discrepancies shall be communicated to the PIC and Ground Engineer, and entered in the Cabin Defects Logbook for rectification prior to take off. The duty Engineer shall only be responsi- ble for entries in the Cabin Defects logbook to sign off the aircraft as airworthy.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2 Pre-Departure
chunks.text: Note: Spare QRCs – are located at L1 stowage compartment or overhead compartment

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.1 Cabin Defects
chunks.text: Log Book - Cabin Defects Log Book is located in the flight deck. The Purser shall go through it as a pre departure duty and inform the CCMs of any pending defects. He shall liaise with the Ground Engineer to rectify any pending defects. In the event a discrepancy is observed/ reported during the pre-depar- ture checks, the Purser shall inform the Ground Engineer and enter it in the Cabin Defects logbook. The Ground Engineer shall comment on all reported defects prior to signing off the aircraft for airworthi- ness. CIDS - Any alerts on the FAP shall be communicated to the PIC and informed to the Ground Engineer for rectification prior to departure. All cabin defects observed by CCMs, during pre-flight/in-flight and post- flight shall be recorded, dated and signed by the Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.2 Voyage Report
chunks.text: The Voyage Report is a mandatory document to be completed for all flights, either in electronic format (CCVR) or as a hard copy. The Purser is responsible for entering all relevant voyage details and concerns. In the absence of a Purser, the In-Charge crew member shall complete the report. Cabin Crew Members (CCMs) shall sign to confirm reporting, designated working positions, and that all safety and security checks have been completed prior to passenger boarding. The Purser shall not initi- ate or mandate signing during the briefing or before completion of these checks. All applicable fields must be completed or marked as N/A where not applicable.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.3 Safety and Security Checks
chunks.text: Purser shall ensure the safety equipment/survival and the security check of the aircraft has been car- ried out prior to the passenger boarding. The CCMs shall be guided by the QRCs at each location for the safety equipment check. CCMs are responsible to ensure the safety equipment is located as per the applicable decals. Once the checks are completed, CCMs shall confirm by placing a signature on the Voyage Report. The Cabin Supervisor shall ensure safety and survival equipment in the area under his purview is as per QRC and confirm by counter signing the VR. If a door assist is not detailed, the Door Primary shall carry out the checks and tick the relevant column and inform the CS. Any irregularities shall be communicated to the Purser at the earliest. Ref 2.35

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.4 Pre-Departure Safety/Security Check List - PSSCL
chunks.text: The Purser shall fill the Pre-Departure Safety/Security Check List sign and present it to the PIC informing him on the checks carried out. The PIC shall carry out the PIC/ Purser briefing and counter sign the form and attach it to the Flight Deck VR. Change of Flight Crew – The Purser shall complete and forward a new PSSCL to the taking over PIC for his signature and the PIC/Purser briefing. Change of Cabin Crew – The taking over Purser shall complete and forward a new PSSCL to the PIC for his signature and the PIC/Purser briefing. The taking over Cabin crew shall carry out the baggage iden- tification of the transit passengers and shall be responsible for the Safety /Security checks and signing the voyage report. When passengers are on board the PA check shall be carried out at L1 only. The serviceability of all inter phones shall be carried out. Passenger Life Vests, Safety Cards and Disruptive

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.4 Pre-Departure Safety/Security Check List - PSSCL
chunks.text: Passenger Information Leaflets checks are not required at transit stations with passengers on board.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.5 Pre departure Safety and Security Checks
chunks.text: All CCMs on duty shall be responsible for the specific safety, and security checks in the Cabin/ Galley and Lavatories but not limited to, which are as follows:

chunks.heading: CCM RESPONSIBLE AREAS
chunks.text: L1 Door Primary FAP-CIDS/System checks/IFE/Defects log book, PA/Inter -phone/ personal survival equipment. Door Primaries PA/ Inter-phone, safety/ survival equipment as per the check list All CCMs Crew/ Passenger seats, seat belts, life vest/safety/ survival equipment Aisle chair The Door Primary closest to the location Refuelling procedures Shall be adhered to by all CCMs Cabin Checks All CCMs detailed for cabin duties - L/vests, Seat belts,Safety cards, and Passenger Information leaflet, Safety/Security of -O/H bins/closets and lavatories.

chunks.heading: CCM RESPONSIBLE AREAS
chunks.text: Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024 Galley Checks Designated galley in charge BC –EY Safety/Security/ locking, latching of carts/containers

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.6 Unserviceable hand set
chunks.text: Prior to departure all handsets shall be serviceable. If one handset is unserviceable at a station, the adjoining handset shall be serviceable for safe dispatch. If the L1 handset becomes unserviceable during flight, the PIC shall be informed and the adjoining hand set shall be used. In the event there is no serviceable handset at L1/R1 area, the handset in the flight deck shall be used with the permission of PIC. If not an alternate handset shall be used and the infor- mation shall be communicated to the PIC and other CCMs. Purser may nominate a Cabin Supervisor or another CCM at a serviceable handset location to carry out required announcements. During flight if all handsets at L1/R1 area becomes unserviceable, PIC and Purser shall discuss and agree on a flight deck entry procedure and hijack alert procedure and communicate the information to the rest of the crew.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.6.1 Aircraft Door Slide Pack
chunks.text: The slide pack is a critical component of the aircraft’s emergency evacuation system, designed to facili- tate rapid egress. It is crucial for the safety of all passengers and crew aboard an aircraft that the emer- gency exits, including the door slide packs, always remain unobstructed particularly when the aircraft is on the ground. Items should not be placed on top of slide packs and sitting or placing the feet on the slide packs is strictly prohibited. This ensures that in the event of an emergency, the slides can be deployed rapidly and efficiently, allowing for a swift and orderly evacuation. Regular safety briefings and checks are essential to reinforce this protocol and maintain the highest standards of safety.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.7 Serviceability Check on Crew Seat
chunks.text: CCMs shall ensure that allocated seats are fully functional (spring loaded seat pan) equipped with a shoulder harness and a seat belt which should have a functioning single point release mechanism. The straps should not be twisted, damaged or frayed. In the event of non-designated crew seats, CS in charge of the area shall be responsible for the checks.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.8 Systems Check on Two way communication
chunks.text: The Purser shall ensure the PA/Inter phone and video system is operational. Door primaries shall ensure the individual screens/PA/Inter phone system is functioning and confirm same with Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.9 Serviceability Check; Passenger Seats
chunks.text: CCMs shall ensure all passenger seats are equipped with Seat Belt Functioning (Fastening and Opening) Life Vest In packing/in place Safety Card Relevant to the aircraft (In the seat pocket/visible/placed vertically) Disruptive Passenger Informa- tion leaflet In the seat pocket/visible/placed vertically PSU Serviceability(Information display)

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.10 Safety and Security Checks in the Cabin
chunks.text: The Purser to ensure, CCMs carry out the safety and security checks as follows Purser Walk around S1/S2 L1/R1 to L2/R2 cabin and B/C lavatories S3/S4 L2/R2 to L3/R3 cabin and lavatories L2/R2 S5/S6 L3/R3 to L4/R4 cabin and lavatories at L3/R3 / L4/R4 CS2 L2 to L4 Cabin (Recheck)confirm to CS3 CS3 R4 to R2 Cabin (Recheck) Confirm to CS1 CS1 Check and ensure flight deck and galleys cleared and confirm to Purser Purser - Walk Around

chunks.heading: FS5
chunks.text: CS3 Re Check

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.11 Safety and Security Checks in the Lavatory
chunks.text:
Designated CCMs/ CSs shall ensure:
1. The smoke detector is free of obstruction
2. Lavatory waste bin extinguishers are serviceable
3. Waste bin flaps are spring loaded
4. Waste bin container is in place and the waste bin door can be latched
5. Water supply to the heater is not closed
6. No foreign objects in the cavities
7. Serviceability of the attendant call button

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.12 Safety and Security Checks in the Galley
chunks.text:
Designated CCMs shall check and CS in charge of the area shall ensure:
1. Fixed galley primary and secondary locking/latching restraining devices are functional
2. Containers/air larder doors can be closed/latched and fits into the slot
3. Service carts/Waste carts are equipped with restraining devices and functioning
4. Service cart doors can be closed/locked and latches are operational,
5. Waste cart , waste bin flap is not bent or damaged and seals the waste cart opening securely
6. Fixed waste bin in the galley, the waste bin flap is not damaged or bent and seals the waste con- tainer in the closed position.
7. Circuit breakers are not popped out
8. Safety equipment located in the galley are checked and secured
9. No foreign objects are placed in the cavities.
10. Break catering seals from all carts/containers/headset bags and check the contents Items that cannot be stowed, secured, restrained, shall be brought to the attention of the Purser imme-

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.12 Safety and Security Checks in the Galley
chunks.text: diately to be off loaded or replaced. Heaters, chillers, water system or the vacuum system defects shall be brought to the attention of the ground Engineer through the Purser. All defects shall be logged for rectification prior to departure.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.13 Passenger Boarding
chunks.text:
Purser shall ensure the following is completed prior to passenger boarding, and if not communicate with the flight dispatcher:
1. The minimum required CCM’s are on-board. Ref 2.13.1
2. Pre departure safety & security checks are completed and VR signed by CCM’s
3. Half the number of exits shall be manned
4. Refuelling procedures are followed
5. Aero bridges/ Steps are positioned appropriately
6. Passengers board with approved size carry-on baggage. Announcement on stowage of luggage is to be carried out periodically during and on completion of boarding.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.13 Passenger Boarding
chunks.text: “Ladies and Gentlemen, Please stow, all your hand luggage in the overhead compartments or under the seat in front of you. Please ensure, that the items stowed in the overhead bin do not fall out and cause injury to passen- gers. Hand luggage, shall not be stowed under the seat in front of the exit rows. Please retain your boarding card for inspection, by airport staff at your final destination. Thank you for your attention.” In the event a carryon baggage is retrieved, CCM shall check with passenger for DGR items/valuables/ travel documents, prior to dispatching it as checked in luggage and keep the Purser informed. If a passenger informs the cabin crew about spare lithium batteries in their checked luggage while the aircraft is still at the gate, the cabin crew will notify the ground staff to retrieve the passenger’s luggage. The passenger will then be required to remove the spare lithium batteries and place them in their car-

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.13 Passenger Boarding
chunks.text:
ry-on luggage, ensuring compliance with IATA DGR 2.3.A table. Furthermore, CCMs shall be vigilant during boarding for following passengers, who may be unfit to travel,
1. A person who appears to be intoxicated or who demonstrates by manner or physical indications that the individual is under the influence of psychoactive substances
2. Passengers who have sustained serious injury prior to boarding.
3. Passengers who are medically unfit due to illness e.g. Any contagious illness
4. Unruly passengers, Non adherence to crew instructions Inform PIC/Dispatcher and off load passenger if required.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.14 Passenger Count
chunks.text: Passenger Count In keeping with security regulations, it is mandatory to carry out a passenger count. The passenger count shall tally with the load sheet prior to take off. The Purser shall inform the physi- cal count to the PIC and Dispatcher. In the event the passenger count is to be taken after all passengers have boarded the aircraft, Purser shall initiate a PA announcement requesting all passengers to be seat- ed prior to the commencement of the count. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, TO ENABLE THE CREW TO CARRY OUT A PASSENGER COUNT WE REQUEST YOU TO REFRAIN FROM USING THE TOILETS AND REMAIN SEATED, THANK YOU FOR YOUR COOPERA- TION”. The responsible CCMs shall ensure EY lavatories are checked/locked, monitored until informed by the Purser. The CCMs responsible are as follows, F/SS 2 BC Lavatories F/SS 3 R2 Lavatories F/SS 4 L2 Lavatories F/SS 5 R3 Lavatories F/SS 6 L3 Lavatories G 2 L4/R4 Lavatories

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.14 Passenger Count
chunks.text: The head count shall be carried out from the steps/aero bridge or by C/S -2 and C/S -3 on a wide body and C/S on a narrow body aircraft, after boarding is completed. In the event of a discrepancy – In the event of a discrepancy, the purser shall get involved in the pas- senger count and achieving two counts tallying with the load sheet is mandatory. The Purser shall initiate the following announcement on completion and confirmation of the count.

chunks.heading: “CREW YOU MAY RESUME DUTIES”
chunks.text: Passenger Count at Transit Stations The disembarking crew shall carry out the passenger count of the transit passengers on board and veri- fy with ground staff. The crew taking over shall carry out a total passenger count prior to departure.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.15 Closing and arming Doors Prior To Departure
chunks.text:
Purser shall ensure that all carry-on baggage in the cabin is stowed, Overhead bins are closed and all passengers are seated prior to closing doors. On confirmation/completion of relevant documents, Purs- er shall request permission from the PIC to close doors and ARM slides. And ensure the Flight Deck door is closed before the last door is closed. Purser shall initiate a precautionary announcement for any ground personnel in the aircraft to disem- bark. “ALL GROUND STAFF ARE REQUESTED TO DISEMBARK FROM THE AIR CRAFT”. Purser shall inform the door primaries to close the doors through an ‘all station call’ Once a door is closed the PIC’s authorisation is required to open it. The following procedure shall be followed by cabin crew members before closing cabin doors
1. The aircraft dispatcher shall confirm with the Purser/In-charge CCM when to close the last door.
2. Announcement prior to closing doors requesting ground personnel to disembark is mandatory.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.15.1 Aircraft Door Re-Opening after arming of slides
chunks.text:
The following procedure shall be followed if an aircraft door has to be re-opened after closing and arming of slides (e.g. door not closed properly, additional delivery of catering and/or supplies, requirement to reconnect boarding equipment, as and when required by the ground handling personnel etc.),The request to re-open the aircraft door shall be communicated to the PIC through authorized ground personnel via flight to ground interphone system and the authorization to reopen the cabin door(s) shall be communicated to the Purser/In-charge CCM by the Pilot in Command.
• The Purser/In-charge CCM shall ensure door disarming and opening procedure is followed according to section 2.15.10

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.15.1 Aircraft Door Re-Opening after arming of slides
chunks.text: Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.15.2 Single CCM operation
chunks.text:
1. The operating CCM shall carry out a walk around the cabin prior to closing doors to ensure cabin is free from unwanted objects/ ground personnel have disembarked and the cabin, galleys, lava- tories are secured for take-off. Confirm with PIC cabin ready for take-off and ARM L1/R1 doors
2. On arrival CCM to ensure the operating F/O is present when disarming doors. (L1/R1). This is a mandatory requirement in preventing an inadvertent slide deployment.
3. CCMs shall strictly adhere to the sterile flight deck policy once flight deck door is closed for the purpose of push back unless an emergency

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.16 Arming of Slides
chunks.text: The Purser shall advice CCMs to arm slides once all doors are closed, by initiating the following PA an- nouncement. “CREW ARM SLIDES AND CROSS CHECK”. Door primaries shall arm the designated slides and cross check. Purser shall initiate an all station call to ensure slides are armed, cross-checked and confirm on FAP. Only door primaries shall operate the desig- nated doors during routine operations.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.17 Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text: The flight deck policy begins once the last cabin door is closed and CCMs compliance required.Ref2.12.8

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.18 Sterile Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text: The sterile flight deck policy (for take-off) shall be active from the time flight deck door is closed for the purpose of push back & until the fasten seat belt sign is switched off after the initial ascent.Ref 2.12.9

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.19 Use of Electronic Devices
chunks.text: Purser shall initiate a PA announcement informing passengers on the use of electronic devices. CCMs shall ensure passenger compliance when checking the cabin. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,

chunks.heading: OUR SAFETY REGULATIONS REQUIRE THAT ALL ELECTRONIC DEVICES INCLUDING MOBILE PHONES ON
chunks.text: AIRCRAFT MODE BE SWITCHED OFF. THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.20 Ordinance Signs
chunks.text: Passengers are required to adhere to ordinance signs. CCMs shall carry out an announcement and mon- itor the cabin for compliance.

chunks.heading: “AYUBOWAN!
chunks.text: LADIES & GENTLEMEN, ON BEHALF OF OUR CAPTAIN AND THE REST OF THE CREW, WE WELCOME YOU ON BOARD THIS FLIGHT. (Code share if applicable)

chunks.heading: “AYUBOWAN!
chunks.text: Revision No 02 Revision Date 15 August 2024 AN ESPECIALLY WARM WELCOME TO OUR FLYSMILES AND ONEWORLD FREQUENT FLYERS. In the event of a delayed departure

chunks.heading: “WE SINCERELY APOLOGISE FOR THE DELAYED DEPARTURE WHICH WAS
chunks.text: DUE TO... (REASON - OPERATIONAL/ TECHNICAL) AND REGRET THE INCONVENIENCE CAUSED”. WE SHALL BE PREPARING FOR PUSH BACK SHORTLY. WE KINDLY REQUEST YOU TO ENSURE THAT ALL HAND LUGGAGE IS STORED IN THE OVERHEAD COMPARTMENTS OR UNDER THE SEAT IN FRONT OF YOU. SMOKING OF ANY FORM IS NOT PERMITTED ON THIS AIRCRAFT. SAFETY REGULATIONS REQUIRE THAT ALL ELECTRONIC DEVICES BE SWITCHED OFF FOR TAKE-OFF. WE WILL MAKE EVERY EFFORT TO ENSURE THAT YOU EXPERIENCE THE BEST OF SRI LANKAN HOSPITALITY THROUGHOUT THIS FLIGHT. WE SHALL NOW BE SCREENING A VIDEO WHICH CONTAINS OUR SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROCE- DURES PERTAINING TO THIS AIRCRAFT, AND YOUR COMPLETE ATTENTION IS NECESSARY. WE WILL MAKE EVERY EFFORT TO MEET YOUR EXPECTATIONS. PLEASE FEEL FREE TO CONTACT ME SHOULD YOU REQUIRE FURTHER ASSISTANCE’. ‘THANK YOU FOR YOUR CO-OPERATION”. Screen Safety Video

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.22 Passenger Safety Briefing
chunks.text:
CCMs to ensure passengers remain seated during the safety briefing. Carrying out the safety briefing could be manually or on video. The aircraft shall not be airborne unless the passenger safety briefing is completed. The Purser shall ensure the following is completed prior to commencement of the passen- ger safety briefing.
1. All doors closed
2. Service related duties discontinued
3. The cabin lights and volume adjusted appropriately Video screening CCM shall ensure that the video screens are positioned in applicable seats and cabins for a clear view prior to screening of the safety video. In the event the main screens are not functioning CCMs are required to take out the relevant individual screens for the safety video. A physical demonstration shall be carried out of the closest and alternate exits. CCMs shall be positioned appropriately in the cabin prior to and remain until completion of the video presentation. CCMs shall not move about in the cabin

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.22 Passenger Safety Briefing
chunks.text: whilst the safety video is screened. In the event of a breakdown in the video system or if any mal- function in the safety video screening occurs, CCMs shall immediately notify the purser and a manual demonstration shall be carried out A 330-300 (B/C) The screens shall be unlocked for passengers seated at the window seats prior to the screening of the safety video and may remain in the said position for Take-off. In the event a delay oc- curs in the screening, the Purser shall advice the PIC of the progress of the safety demonstration. Note : Video PA Shall Not Be Used During Critical Phase Of The Flight

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.23 Content of Passenger Safety Briefing
chunks.text:
1. Stowing of seat back/tray table/individual video monitors/window blinds
2. Use of seat belts
3. Showing of emergency exit/alternate exits and floor path markings
4. Oxygen system
5. Use of life vest
6. Regulation on smoking/ electronic devices/ carry-on baggage
7. Bring passenger concerns to the attention of the crew

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.24 Locking of Lavatories
chunks.text: The EY lavatories shall remain locked during push back till the seat belt sign is switched off. CCMs re- sponsible for locking/unlocking lavatories are: L2/R2 Lavatories S4 L3/R3 Lavatories S5 L4/R4 Lavatories S6 A 320/21 refer: chapter 6/6A

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.25 Cabin Checks Prior to Departure
chunks.text:
CCMs designated for the relevant work position shall ensure the following preparations are carried out prior to departure and report to the cabin supervisor in relevant work area. Purser announcement. “CABIN CREW PREPARE CABIN FOR TAKE OFF”.
1. Passengers seated and secured
2. Seat backs adjusted upright/Seat belts fastened
3. Tray tables stowed and latched
4. Window blinds opened and footrests stowed
5. Children/Infants restrained
6. Overhead bins/ compartments closed and locked
7. IVS stowed / strapped
8. Emergency equipment/exits/aisles/cross aisles clear of obstruction
9. Portable electronic devices switched off
10. Carry-on baggage stowed and secured

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.25 Cabin Checks Prior to Departure
chunks.text:
11. Curtains and partitions opened and secured
12. Lavatories unoccupied and locked
13. Galley equipment latched, locked and secured, galley electrics switched off
14. Waste bin flaps closed
15. Cabin lights adjusted appropriately
16. Ensure Flight Deck cleared
17. PED facility switched off from the FAP
18. Cabin Closets/Compartments/Dog Houses are Closed, Locked and Secured CCMs shall be responsible to check their designated area, and open door observation window for exter- nal visibility.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.26 Spraying of Aerosol
chunks.text: The Purser shall ensure the following announcement is made prior to spraying. CCMs should spray aer- osol towards the cabin ceiling working from AFT to FWD. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,

chunks.heading: WORLD HEALTH ORGANISATION STANDARDS WILL BE SPRAYED THROUGHOUT THE CABIN. WE KIND-
chunks.text:
LY REQUEST YOU TO REMAIN SEATED, AND RECOMMEND YOU KEEP YOUR NOSE, EYES AND MOUTH COVERED UNTIL THE SPRAYING IS COMPLETED. THANK YOU”. Flights to other countries - The spraying shall be carried out as specified, conforming to regulatory re- quirements of the destination country. Inbound flights to Sri Lanka - the following procedures shall be adhered.
1. For single sector flights into Sri Lanka, aerosol spraying shall be carried out prior to passenger boarding.
2. For multiple sector flights, spraying of aerosol shall be carried out at the last overseas port be- fore departure to Srilanka.
3. The spraying shall be carried out after the aircraft has been fully catered, the service doors closed and prior to passenger boarding. One main entry door may remain open for operational requirements.
4. Spray should be directed towards the open Overhead lockers, celling and galley areas. Ensure that the spray does not fall on the face of the operator while he or she is walking along the aisle

chunks.heading: WORLD HEALTH ORGANISATION STANDARDS WILL BE SPRAYED THROUGHOUT THE CABIN. WE KIND-
chunks.text:
at the rate of not more than one step or row of seats per second.
5. Aerosol shall be sprayed into all toilets and coat closets for 2sec each. Ensure the toilet seats and diaper changing boards are up and not sprayed.
6. Aerosol shall be sprayed in the flight deck for 3sec. Spray shall not be directed on aircraft equip- ment and on persons in the flight deck.

chunks.heading: WORLD HEALTH ORGANISATION STANDARDS WILL BE SPRAYED THROUGHOUT THE CABIN. WE KIND-
chunks.text: Upon arrival, the empty cans shall be handed over to the relevant authority. This shall be accompanied by a signed copy of the General Declaration / other destination specific documents, which must include all relevant information filled out as required.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.27 Push Back/Taxiing out/Runway
chunks.text:
Pushback - A procedure, to push back an aircraft from the gate using external power. Push back tugs - Special, low profile vehicle that pushes an aircraft back. Taxiing - Refers to the movement of an aircraft on the ground, under its own power to and from a run- way for a take-off or after a landing. Runway - A defined rectangular area on a land aerodrome prepared for the landing and take-off run of an aircraft along its length. CCM Responsibilities CCMs shall adhere to the following guidelines in preparation for take-off.
1. All service related duties should cease/class dividers opened and secured
2. Galley electrics switched off
3. CCMs shall sit and be restrained in preparation for departure
4. Cabin Supervisors shall check and report to the Purser individually that the respective areas are checked and ready for take-off CCMs shall not leave their seats except to attend to a critical safety related duty, and should be vigilant

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.27 Push Back/Taxiing out/Runway
chunks.text: to ensure that passengers remain seated until the seat belt sign is switched off. If required the CCM may initiate a PA announcement advising passengers to remain seated for safety reasons and shall not place themselves in danger in trying to seat passengers.

chunks.heading: 2.15.2.28 Confirmation of Cabin Ready to PIC
chunks.text: Purser shall indicate Cabin Ready to the PIC before take-off and landing using the FAP when available or via the inter-phone, once all CCMs are seated and restrained. The Purser may walk around prior to confirmation.

chunks.heading: 2.15.3 Take Off
chunks.text: Take off is the phase of flight in which an aircraft moves through a transition from taxiing (moving to the runway) to flying in the air, starting from the runway until airborne. Purser may initiate the following announcement as a reminder to the passengers if the duration be- tween the completion of the passenger safety briefing and the time of departure is over 20 minutes. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, AS WE SHALL BE AIRBORNE SHORTLY, PLEASE MAKE SURE, YOUR SEAT BELTS FASTENED, CHAIR BACKS ADJUSTED UPRIGHT, WINDOW BLIND OPENED, TRAY TABLE, VIDEO SCREENS AND FOOT REST STOWED. YOU ARE REMINDED TO SWITCH-OFF ALL ELECTRONIC DEVICES. THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.1 Night-Take Off
chunks.text: The cabin/galley and entry lights should be in the ‘DIM’ position and the window lights in the ‘OFF’ po- sition for night take-off. This is to acclimatise passenger and CCM vision for an unprepared evacuation. Note: Cabin/Galley must never be in total darkness during the flight. The Purser shall initiate the following announcement: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, CABIN SAFETY REGULATIONS REQUIRE THAT WE DIM THE CABIN LIGHTS IN PREPARATION FOR TAKE OFF. PASSENGERS WHO WISH TO CONTINUE READING MAY USE THEIR PERSONAL READING LIGHTS.

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.2 Imminent Take Off
chunks.text: The PIC shall advice CCMs to sit for take-off through the PA system. “CABIN CREW, BE SEATED FOR TAKE-OFF”. (Cabin crew are required to sit at their stations and restrain themselves once all checks are completed prior to Purser informing PIC, ‘CABIN READY’ via FAP or inter phone. C/S’s to ensure compliance of the aforementioned to the Purser)

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.3 Cabin Crew Seating Stations
chunks.text: It is mandatory that CCMs be in uniform for every take-off and landing for identification in an emergen- cy. Window blinds on the doors shall be opened for take-off and landing. The CCM shall observe STS and be vigilant for abnormalities. Crew Stations A330 – ALT Aircraft 51H – Reserved for Cabin Crew Seating Pur

chunks.text: Crew Stations A330 – ALH Aircraft 63C – Reserved for Cabin Crew Seating Crew Stations A330-300 Aircraft A330 -300 L2A Crew seat shall be occupied by FSS 4 when an interpreter is not on duty. Crew Stations 4R ALS Aircraft Pur

chunks.text: Demonstration Positions A330-200 CS1 shall demonstrate if S1 is not detailed. Demonstration Positions A330-300 FSS 1 shall demonstrate on the right side positioning at row 4 as the view to the passengers are limited.

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.4 Silent Thirty Seconds Review (STS)
chunks.text: When secured for take-off, CCMs shall observe STS – (BDEEP) Brace for impact Door operation Evacuation commands Evacuation route Passenger control

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.5 Climb (Ascent)
chunks.text: Ascent - climbing to a higher altitude after take-off. Flight Crew shall not be disturbed until the aircraft reaches cruise altitude and the seat belt sign is switched off, unless in an emergency that needs immediate attention.

chunks.heading: 2.15.3.6 Safety Announcement after Seat Belt Sign Off (A330-300 A320/321Neo)
chunks.text: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, PASSENGERS MAY USE YOUR SMART DEVICES TO ACCESS THE INTERNET THROUGH THE ONBOARD WIFI NETWORK OR GSM NETWORK, TO ENSURE YOU DO NOT DISTURB THE PASSENGERS AROUND YOU, PLEASE SWITCH YOUR PHONES TO SILENT MODE.

chunks.heading: “MOBILE PHONES MAY BE USED ONLY ON FLIGHT MODE DURING CRUISE”
chunks.text: WE RECOMMEND THAT YOU HAVE YOUR SEATBELT SECURELY FASTENED AT ALL TIMES WHEN SEAT- ED. PASSENGERS WHO DO NOT WISH TO BE DISTURBED, SHOULD FASTEN THEIR SEATBELT OVER THE BLANKET, VISIBLE TO THE CREW. IF THE “FASTEN SEATBELT” SIGN IS SWITCHED ON DURING FLIGHT, REFRAIN FROM USING THE TOILETS, RETURN TO YOUR SEAT IMMEDIATELY AND FASTEN YOUR SEAT- BELT. AS A SAFETY MEASURE, ALL TOILETS ARE FITTED WITH SMOKE DETECTORS. THE USE OF MOBILE PHONES IN THE TOILET IS PROHIBITED. OUR CREW WILL ENDEAVOUR TO MAKE YOUR FLIGHT WITH US A TRULY PLEASANT EXPERIENCE.

chunks.heading: 2.15.4 Cruise
chunks.text:
A level maintained during a significant portion of the flight and when the aircraft flies most fuel effi- ciently between the ascent and descent phases. During cruise, the CCMs shall check the following in the cabin/lavatories and galleys but not limited to,
1. Overhead stowage compartments to remain closed at all times
2. Infants in bassinets checked periodically
3. Passengers sleeping have their seat belts fastened

chunks.heading: 2.15.4 Cruise
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
4. Passengers not sleeping on the floor (inclusive of children/ infants)
5. Conduct regular check on lavatories/ waste bins, flaps for prevention of fire
6. Carts /trolleys shall be manned and locked when in the cabin
7. Containers in galleys to be locked and latched
8. Carts /trolleys to be secured at all times in the galleys
9. Be Vigilant for fire hazards
10. Waste management carried out for safety and hygiene conditions
11. Passengers and crew shall not sit, place feet or any items on the slide pack.
12. Revenue passengers shall not sit on jump seats.

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.1 Turbulence
chunks.text: Definition - Turbulence is the result of atmospheric and environmental effects, which can be light/mod- erate/severe. The degree of turbulence can vary for many reasons. It is important to be aware that clear air turbulence may occur without warning. Passenger Announcement - The CCMs shall initiate the following PA announcement to advice the pas- sengers.Ref 4.1

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.2 Hygiene in lavatories
chunks.text: During cruise, the CCMs should check the lavatories at regular intervals to maintain safety and hygienic conditions and address the following: Waste bins not over filled(Waste bin flap closed)/Paper towels and tissues not piled on the lavatory floor The sink is dry and the drain system functioning. In the event water is shut off in the lavatory, the power to the water heater shall be switched off. Unserviceable lavatories shall be locked and placarded.

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.3 Waste Management in galleys
chunks.text: CCMs should be concerned of waste management in galleys. The waste bins shall not be over filled due to health/ hygiene condition and safety hazards. All waste bin flaps shall be closed during flight. Methodical waste management and stowage should be addressed depending on the aircraft type and available resources. If waste is to be stowed in lavatories for landing, it shall be in transparent bags in order to identify any fire hazards. The bags shall be stowed once the “fasten seat belt” sign has been switched on for landing. The waste bags shall be removed after all passenger have disembarked.

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.4 Stowing of used blankets in lavatories
chunks.text:
Used blankets may be stowed in lavatories provided the following conditions are strictly adhered to,
1. The lavatories shall be used to stow blankets as a last resort (only after all other means of stow- age has been utilized)
2. Blankets shall be stowed only in transparent bags

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.4 Stowing of used blankets in lavatories
chunks.text:
3. A maximum of 25 blankets shall be stowed in each bag
4. A maximum of 3 such bags shall be stowed in each lavatory
5. Lavatories shall be checked for fire hazards prior to stowing the blankets
6. Lavatories next to CCM stations shall be used for this purpose
7. The bags shall be stowed once the “fasten seat belt” sign has been switched on for landing, (ap- proximately 20 minutes prior to landing)
8. The bags shall not surpass the height of the lavatory sink
9. The lavatory door shall be locked to prevent passenger access
10. The Crew shall monitor the lavatories after stowage of the bags
11. The blankets shall be removed after all passenger have disembarked and shall not be positioned blocking direct access to exits. The following technical conditions shall be applicable in the lavatories to stow blankets/Waste,
1. An operational smoke detector (Refer NOTE below)
2. An operative door locking mechanism

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.4 Stowing of used blankets in lavatories
chunks.text:
3. Can be locked and unlocked externally
4. Not used for the stowage of any other items Note : An aircraft may be dispatched with an inoperative smoke detector if blanket collection bags are not placed in the lavatory, therefore minimum equipment list (MEL) relief shall not be applica- ble if such bags are to be placed in the lavatory.

chunks.heading: 2.15.4.5 Smoking Regulation
