chunks.text: Smoking of any form is not permitted on all Civil Aircraft registered in Sri Lanka or operated within Sri Lanka’s airspace, SLCAIS 74, CCMs shall ensure the observation of the ’No smoking regulation’. Ref 2.20

chunks.heading: 2.15.5 Descent
chunks.text: Descent is the phase where an aircraft decreases altitude in preparation for landing. The fasten seat belt and no smoking signs (330-300 not applicable) shall be switched on and should be observed. Unless in an emergency, CCMs are advised to refrain from interrupting the Flight Crew until the aircraft is parked and the fasten seat belt sign is switched off. The PIC shall initiate a PA announcement on top of descent to advice CCMs to prepare cabin for landing. “CABIN CREW PREPARE CABIN FOR LANDING”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.1 Cease Cabin Services
chunks.text: CCMs shall cease service related duties on top of descent and commence pre-landing safety duties. The cabin lights shall be at full intensity to carry out the cabin checks. Initiate the following announcement prior to the collection of headsets.

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.1 Cease Cabin Services
chunks.text: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, IN PREPARATION FOR LANDING THE HEADSETS AND BLANKETS PROVIDED TO YOU WILL BE COLLECT- ED BY THE CABIN CREW. WE TRUST YOU ENJOYED THE ENTERTAINMENT PROVIDED. PLEASE NOTE THE REMOVAL OF BLANKETS FROM THE AIRCRAFT IS PROHIBITED AND THE TOILETS WILL BE LOCKED SHORTLY,

chunks.heading: THANK YOU”
chunks.text: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, IN PREPARATION FOR LANDING, WE SHALL BE LOCKING ALL TOILETS AND SECURING THE CABIN. PLEASE RETURN TO YOUR SEAT, ADJUST YOUR SEAT BACK TO THE UPRIGHT POSITION, STOW AWAY

chunks.heading: YOUR TRAY TABLE/VIDEO SCREEN/RETRACT THE FOOTREST/FASTEN YOUR SEATBELT, AND HAVE THE
chunks.text: WINDOW BLINDS OPEN FOR LANDING. ALL HAND LUGGAGE TO BE STORED IN THE OVERHEAD BIN OR UNDER THE SEAT IN FRONT OF YOU, FOR SAFETY REASONS, IT IS MANDATORY THAT WE CLEAR THE CABIN OF ALL DISPOSABLE ITEMS. PLEASE HAND OVER ALL SUCH ITEMS TO THE CREW WHO WILL BE IN THE CABIN SHORTLY. YOU ARE REMINDED TO SWITCH OFF ALL ELETRONIC DEVICES, YOU ARE REQUIRED TO REMAIN SEATED UNTIL THE SEATBELT SIGN IS SWITCHED OFF.

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.2 Before Landing Announcement on Flights Exceeding 4 Hours
chunks.text: The CCMs shall carry out a manual demonstration to advice passengers of the locations of exits as a reminder on flights exceeding 4 hours. Ref 2.15.3.3.1 “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, THE CREW IN FRONT OF YOU WILL ONCE AGAIN DEMONSTRATE THE CLOSEST AND ALTERNATE EXITS. IT HAS BEEN OUR PLEASURE HAVING YOU WITH US AND WE LOOK FORWARD TO BEING OF SERVICE TO YOU AGAIN IN THE NEAR FUTURE. THANK YOU FOR FLYING SRILANKAN AIRLINES, A MEMBER OF THE ONEWORLD ALLIANCE. AYUBOWAN”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.3 Sterile Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text: CCMs shall observe and enforce Sterile Flight Deck Policy when the seat belt sign is switched on in preparation for landing. Ref 2.12.9

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.4 Cabin Checks Prior To Landing
chunks.text: CCMs shall carry out the following checks in preparation for landing,(Checks similar to pre departure checks) Ref 2.15.2.25

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.5 Confirmation of Secured Cabin to the PIC
chunks.text: The Flight Crew shall initiate a PA announcement advising CCMs to sit for landing “CABIN CREW BE SEATED FOR LANDING”. All CCMs shall sit at their stations with their seat belts and shoulder harness fastened. CCMs shall

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.5 Confirmation of Secured Cabin to the PIC
chunks.text: ensure the blind on the viewing window is opened. It is mandatory that CCMs be in uniform for every take-off and landing and shall be vigilant to observe any abnormalities. The Purser may carry out a walk around prior to confirming cabin ready to the PIC . It is mandatory that the cabin is secured and con- firmed to the PIC prior to the announcement The facility to inform PIC is available on the FAP or via the inter-phone. It is mandatory that cabin secure is confirmed to the PIC 10 minutes prior to landing. The Purser shall ensure the cabin is prepared for landing as required/on time and if not inform the PIC of the delay.

chunks.heading: 2.15.5.6 Night Landing
chunks.text: The cabin/galley and entry lights should be in the dim position & window lights switched off for night landing. This is to acclimatize passenger and CCM vision for an unprepared evacuation. Note - Cabin/Gally must never be in total darkness during the flight. The Purser shall initiate the following announcement prior to adjusting the lights.

chunks.heading: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN’
chunks.text: CABIN SAFETY REGULATIONS REQUIRE THAT WE DIM THE CABIN LIGHTS IN PREPARATION FOR LAND- ING. THOSE WHO WISH TO CONTINUE READING MAY USE THEIR PERSONAL READING LIGHTS. THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.6 Approach
chunks.text: Approach is, when an aircraft leaves its cruise altitude and commences to descend in preparation for landing. 2.15.6 .1 Silent Thirty Second Review (STS) When seated for landing CCMs shall observe “STS” – (BDEEP) Ref 4.6.2/2.15.3.4

chunks.heading: 2.15.7 Landing/Taxiing In
chunks.text: CCMs shall remain seated and ensure passengers remain seated until the aircraft comes to a complete stop and the fasten seat belt sign is switched off. CCMs shall leave their seats only to perform safety related duties. Purser/Door assists are permitted to leave their seats once the aircraft leaves the active runway.

chunks.heading: 2.15.8 After Landing Safety Announcement
chunks.text: The under mentioned announcements shall be carried out having taxied out of the active runway at Transit/Terminating stations. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, WE HAVE ARRIVED AT OUR DESTINATION. PLEASE REMAIN SEATED UNTIL THE SEATBELT SIGN IS SWITCHED OFF. WE AT SRILANKAN AIRLINES WOULD LIKE TO MAKE EVERY EFFORT TO ENSURE

chunks.heading: BLOCK THE AISLES FROM FREE MOVEMENT, PLEASE BE MINDFUL WHEN RETRIEVING BELONG-
chunks.text: INGS FROM THE OVERHEAD COMPARTMENTS AS ITEMS MAY FALL OUT AND CAUSE INJURY TO THOSE AROUND YOU.MAY WE ALSO REMIND YOU TO KINDLY TAKE ALL YOUR BELONGINGS WITH YOU, WHEN LEAVING THE AIRCRAFT. SHOULD YOU REQUIRE ASSISTANCE PLEASE INFORM A MEM- BER OF THE CABIN CREW.

chunks.heading: SEATED UNTIL ALL OTHER PASSENGERS HAVE DISEMBARKED. AIRPORT STAFF WILL ASSIST YOU
chunks.text: AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. SHOULD YOU NEED ANY ASSISTANCE AT THE TERMINAL, PLEASE PROCEED TO THE TRANSFER DESK OR CONTACT A MEMBER OF THE GROUND STAFF OF SRILANKAN AIRLINES. WE INVITE YOU TO LOG ON TO SRILANKAN.COM, FOR THE LATEST DISCOUNTS AND SPECIAL OFFERS ON TRAVEL AND HOLIDAYS WITH SRILANKAN AIRLINES. IT HAS BEEN ENTIRELY OUR PLEASURE TO SERVE YOU AND WE HOPE TO SEE YOU AGAIN SOON. THANK YOU FOR FLYING SRILANKAN AIRLINES, A MEMBER OF THE ONEWORLD ALLIANCE. (AND OUR CODE SHARE PARTNER” …if applicable)”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.8.2 Delayed arrival
chunks.text: “ONCE AGAIN, WE SINCERELY APOLOGISE FOR THE DELAY AND THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE AND UNDERSTANDING. IT HAS BEEN A PLEASURE LOOKING AFTER YOU AND WE HOPE TO SEE YOU AGAIN SOON. THANK YOU FOR FLYING SRI LANKAN AIRLINES, A MEMBER OF THE ONE WORLD ALLIANCE (AND OUR CODE SHARE PARTNER” …if applicable)”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.8.3 Transit Stations
chunks.text: Ref 2.15.8 “THOSE WHO ARE CONTINUING THEIR JOURNEY WITH US ON THIS AIRCRAFT, PLEASE REMAIN SEAT-

chunks.heading: ED.”
chunks.text: If facilities are provided for smokers at the arrival airport, the relevant information should be included in the announcement. 2.15.8.4 Park in a remote bay. Note: CCMs stationed at the passenger disembarking doors should mention “mind your step and hold on to the railing”. If a passenger is carrying multiple bags/items, caution the passenger to have a free hand to hold on to the railing.

chunks.heading: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN
chunks.text: WE AT SRILANKAN AIRLINES WOULD LIKE TO MAKE EVERY EFFORT TO ENSURE YOUR SAFETY AND WELL-BEING. PLEASE REMAIN AT YOUR DESIGNATED SEAT AND AWAIT YOUR TURN. REFRAIN FROM RETRIEVING YOUR CARRY-ON BAGGAGE FROM THE OVERHEAD BINS UNTIL THE SEAT ROW IN FRONT

chunks.heading: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN
chunks.text: OF YOU HAS BEEN CLEARED. DO NOT STAND ALTOGETHER AND BLOCK THE AISLES FROM FREE MOVE- MENT. ON ARRIVAL AT << NAME OF AIRPORT>> THIS AIR-CRAFT HAS BEEN ALLOCATED TO A REMOTE PARKING BAY. WE ADVISE YOU TO BE CAUTIOUS WHEN DISEMBARKING THE AIRCRAFT USING THE PROVIDED STEPS. PLEASE BE MINDFUL OF THE PERSON IN FRONT OF YOU WHILST USING THE STEPS. WE RECOMMEND THAT YOU GRIP AND USE THE HAND RAILING WITH YOUR FREE HAND, ON THE MOBILE STEPS, TO ASSIST YOU IN DISEMBARKING SAFELY. PASSENGER COACHES WILL TRANSPORT YOU TO THE ARRIVAL TERMINAL. SHOULD YOU REQUIRE ASSISTANCE PLEASE INFORM A MEMBER OF THE CABIN CREW.

chunks.heading: 2.15.8.5 Delay in Parking
chunks.text: Flight Crew or CCMs should prevent disorder by initiating a brief PA announcement-advising passenger to remain seated until the aircraft approaches the gate/ parked and the seat belt sign is switched off. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY, WE ADVICE ALL PASSENGERS TO REMAIN SEATED UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT COMES TO A COMPLETE STOP AND THE SEATBELT SIGN IS SWITCHED OFF”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.8.6 Delayed arrival
chunks.text: “WE SINCERELY APOLOGISE FOR THE DELAY AND THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE AND UNDER- STANDING. IT HAS BEEN A PLEASURE LOOKING AFTER YOU AND WE HOPE TO SEE YOU AGAIN SOON. THANK YOU FOR FLYING SRILANKAN AIRLINES, A MEMBER OF THE ONE WORLD ALLIANCE (AND OUR CODE SHARE PARTNER” ….if applicable)”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.9 Arrival
chunks.text: Arrival is the conclusion of a sector when the aircraft is parked/engines are shut down/fasten seat belt sign is switched off.

chunks.heading: 2.15.9.1 Disarming of Slides
chunks.text: When the seat belt sign is switched off, the Purser shall advice CCMs to disarm the slides and cross check by initiating the following PA announcement:

chunks.heading: “CREW DISARM SLIDES AND CROSS CHECK”
chunks.text:
The slides on the right shall be disarmed first. Prior to disarming the slides on the right, door primaries on the left shall cross over to the right. The following disarming procedure shall be carried out. (PIN/LEVER/PIN verbally stated by the CCM whilst disarming the slide)
1. Remove safety Pin.

chunks.heading: “CREW DISARM SLIDES AND CROSS CHECK”
chunks.text:
2. Move door arming lever to disarm position.
3. Insert safety pin. The slides on the left shall be disarmed next, Once the right-side slides are disarmed, both door primaries shall cross over to the left and the left side door primary shall disarm the slide observed by the opposite door primary. The following disarming procedure shall be carried out. (PIN/LEVER/PIN verbally stated by the CCM whilst disarming the slide)
1. Remove safety Pin.
2. Move door arming lever to disarm position.
3. Insert safety pin. The above procedure shall be carried out on all types of aircraft in the fleet. Routine door operations shall be carried out only by the door primaries. Purser shall initiate an “ALL STATION” call to obtain confirmation by the door primaries and shall check for slides disarmed indication on the FAP.

chunks.heading: 2.15.10 Opening Doors
chunks.text: Once the slides are disarmed the PIC shall give the confirmation by making the following an- nouncement:

chunks.heading: “CABIN CREW YOU MAY OPEN DOORS WHEN REQUIRED”
chunks.text: In the event the above command is not received, Purser shall check with PIC and advice CCMs accordingly. NOTE: In the event the opposite door is unmanned (CCM not assigned), the door primary shall be responsible for disarming both slides and shall be extra cautious when doing so. CCMs shall await the confirmation by ground staff to open the doors with two knocks and thumbs up prior to opening doors. Exception would be at airports where the door has to be opened to position steps. The Purser shall obtain permission from the PIC prior to opening the door at such stations. CCMs shall man half the doors until completion of passenger disembarkation

chunks.heading: 2.15.11 Conclusion of Sterile Flight Deck Policy
chunks.text: Sterile flight deck policy ceases when the aircraft comes to a complete stop after completing a flight leg and the fasten seat belt sign is switched off. CAUTION: CARRYING OUT SERVICE RELATED DUTIES SHALL ONLY BE AFTER THE SEAT BELT SIGN HAS BEEN SWITCHED OFF AND THE SLIDES ARE DISARMED. CAUTION: DO NOT LEAVE AN OPEN DOOR UNATTENDED AS THE SAFETY STRAP PULLED ACROSS THE DOOR WILL NOT PREVENT PASSENGERS/CREW MEMBERS FROM FALLING OUT.

chunks.heading: 2.15.12 Aerodrome Restrictions Announcement
chunks.text: The following announcement should be initiated advising passengers of the local restrictions when the aircraft is on ground.

chunks.heading: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN
chunks.text: PLEASE BE INFORMED THAT ANY FORM OF PHOTOGRAPHY IS PROHIBITED BY THE AIRPORT AUTHORI- TIES, VIOLATION OF THIS LAW COULD LEAD TO PROSECUTION, THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: 2.15.13 Steps/Aerobridges
chunks.text: CCM in charge of the door shall ensure safe positioning of steps/aerobridges prior to passengers disem- barking. The gap between the aircraft threshold and the steps shall not exceed 6”(inches). If reposition is required passenger boarding/disembarking shall be stopped immediately and same communicated to the ground staff through the Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.15.14 Passenger Boarding/Disembarking During Transit
chunks.text: The Purser shall ensure that half the doors are manned at transit stations when passengers are disem- barking. CCMs shall remain at the respective stations until the joining CCMs take over duties.

chunks.heading: 2.15.14.1 Passenger count/Baggage Identification at a Transit Station
chunks.text: The disembarking Purser shall ensure a transit passenger count is carried out and confirmed with the load sheet. CCMs should ensure the passengers remain seated prior to the commencement of the pas- senger count. Purser shall initiate the following PA announcement, “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, TO ENABLE US TO CARRY OUT AN ACCURATE PASSENGER COUNT WE REQUEST YOU TO REFRAIN FROM USING THE TOILETS AND REMAIN SEATED. THANK YOU”. On completion of the passenger count, the lavatories shall be unlocked for cleaning. The joining crew shall carry out transit passenger carryon baggage identification and check all seats, including seat pock- ets, that were occupied by disembarking passengers. The Purser shall initiate a PA announcement prior to the baggage identification. In the event of a delay of the joining crew boarding the aircraft, the dis- embarking crew shall carry out the baggage identification and seat check . Unclaimed items must be

chunks.heading: 2.15.14.1 Passenger count/Baggage Identification at a Transit Station
chunks.text: reported to ground staff immediately. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,

chunks.heading: INFORMED THAT ALL UNIDENTIFIED BAGGAGE WILL BE OFFLOADED. PLEASE ASSIST THE CREW
chunks.text: BY IDENTIFYING YOUR BAGS. THANK YOU” .

chunks.heading: 2.15.15 Post Landing Duties
chunks.text:
The following duties shall be performed by CCMs after all passengers have disembarked, Purser Duties
1. Ensure deportees and INADS handed over to ground staff and documentation completed.
2. UMs/YPs handed over including special handling passengers.

chunks.heading: 2.15.15 Post Landing Duties
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
3. Cabin Defects logged in the cabin defects logbook.
4. IFE system switched off.
5. Ensure all kangaroo belts collected stored and in correct numbers.
6. A mandatory walk around the cabin needs to be performed to ensure all after landing duties are completed by CCMs. CCM Duties
1. Ensure all passengers have disembarked from the aircraft. This includes passengers with special requirements.
2. Security check shall be carried out from AFT to the FWD of the aircraft ensuring all passengers have disembarked the aircraft and items have not been left behind in overhead compartments, under seats, on seats, refrigerators and chillers, stowage compartments and coat closets. Such items shall be handed over to the security personnel on board.
3. Ensure all lavatories are unlocked and checked.
4. Ensure all overhead compartments are kept opened during above checks.

chunks.heading: 2.15.15 Post Landing Duties
chunks.text:
5. Kangaroo belts shall be collected, stowed and accounted for. Soiled/unserviceable kangaroo belts shall be entered in the defect’s logbook.
6. Safety equipment used during flight shall be handed over to engineering personnel and indicat- ed in the cabin defects logbook.
7. Soiled bassinettes are handed over to AIC staff for replacement.
8. Inform support service staff the location of the used First aid kit for replacement

chunks.heading: 2.16.1 Load Sheet
chunks.text:
Weight and balance is referred to as Load Control and is part of each airlines operational responsibility. The primary function of Load Control is to prepare the Load Sheet/Trim Sheet. It shows the number of passengers on board and baggage/cargo/Mail figures. The Trim Sheet also shows the centre of gravity of the aircraft is within limits, and the maximum aircraft weights are within limits. The load sheet shall carry the following information,
1. Total passenger weight
2. Total Cargo weight
3. Total fuel weight
4. Total take-off weight
5. Total number of passengers on board
6. Number of passengers disembarking at various stations
7. Number of Adults/Children/Infants
8. Last minute changes – referred to as LMC

chunks.heading: 2.16.2 Trim balance
chunks.text:
Prior to departure, Load Control staff will present the load sheet to the PIC for his verification, approval and signature. The PIC will retain the original and a copy shall be handed over to the Purser by Load Control staff. A weight and balance document (manual/EDP or ACARS) shall be calculated for every flight. EDP weight and balance documentation shall be produced with EDP systems approved by Colombo load control. Standard masses, including hand baggage, of
• 85 kg for a Flight Crew member
• 75 kg for a Cabin Crew member RESEATING OF PASSENGERS IN LARGE NUMBERS SHALL NOT BE PERMITTED FOR TAKE OFF/LANDING IN THE EVENT THE AIRCRAFT IS NOT FULL.

chunks.heading: 2.16.3 Passenger Count
chunks.text: The Purser shall be responsible for the final head count and ensure the total number of passengers on board the aircraft confirms to the total number stated on the Load Sheet. Once established that the head count tallies with the Load Sheet/Trim Sheet, the Purser shall confirm it to the PIC. Confirmation of the number of passengers against the load sheet is a mandatory safety and security requirement.

chunks.heading: 2.17.1 Individual Video System
chunks.text: Use of individual video screens are permitted when the aircraft is on ground/transit.

chunks.heading: 2.17.2 Meal Service on Ground
chunks.text:
The decision to carry out a meal service on ground during a delay shall be at the discretion of the Purser in consultation with the PIC under the following conditions: Purser responsibilities
1. Minimum delay should exceed 2 hours or as decided by the Purser
2. Purser should determine the time required and inform the PIC and ground staff
3. Obtain permission from the local Air Port Authority (through ground staff)
4. Refuelling shall not be carried out during the service
5. One FWD exit shall be opened with an aero bridge or steps positioned
6. One Aft exit may be opened with steps positioned or the door could be kept closed with the ground area clear of obstruction CCM Responsibilities
1. Alcohol and Tea/Coffee shall not be a part of the service
2. Loose items shall not be carried on top of the carts
3. Only one meal cart on each aisle is permitted for a twin aisle cabin
4. Each cart should be manned by two CCMs when in the cabin

chunks.heading: 2.17.2 Meal Service on Ground
chunks.text:
5. Meal carts shall not be permitted in the cabin for a single aisle cabin, service shall be carried out by hand
6. Curtains and class dividers shall be opened during the service

chunks.heading: 2.17.3 Seal Verification Process
chunks.text:
In compliance with CAASL regulations, the verification of catering seals is the responsibility of the oper- ating crew. This procedure is mandatory and shall be strictly followed on all flight’s ex CMB. For wide-body aircraft, the seal verification form will include three carbonized copies, distributed as follows:
• Forward Galley, Mid Galley, Aft Galley – 1 copy each Narrow-body aircraft will receive a single seal verification form by the catering office. Crew members shall:
• Verify all seals on carts and containers against the corresponding seal form.
• Sign the form once verification is complete.
• During seal verification of carts and containers against the catering seal form, any discrepancy in the seal number shall require the crew to summon security to verify the contents and record the details in the VR. Crew Responsibilities
• Wide-body aircraft:
• Forward Galley – Cabin Supervisor 1

chunks.heading: 2.17.3 Seal Verification Process
chunks.text:
• Mid Galley – Cabin Supervisor 2
• Aft Galley – Cabin Supervisor 3 Narrow-body aircraft:
• FSS2 and Cabin Supervisor

chunks.heading: 2.18 Apron Safety/Security Procedures
chunks.text:
Apron is a defined area, a part of an aerodrome intended to accommodate loading and unloading of passengers /cargo / fuelling/ servicing or parking for maintenance. Safety The ramp could be dangerous due to movements of ground support equipment (vehicles, tugs etc.). CCMs shall be alert and exercise caution, be aware of the circle of safety of an aircraft, and follow the guidelines given below:
1. Walk out and around the wing tips
2. Never walk under the wings even when engines are not running
3. Never pass directly in front or behind, operating aircraft engines
4. Walk only on cleared areas when ice or snow is observed on the ramp,
5. Be cautious as rain could cause the ramp to be slippery
6. Do not throw trash on the ramp
7. Ensure passengers do not smoke when boarding or disembarking Vehicles that should observe the circle of safety Vehicles when parking should adhere to the circle of safety regulations.

chunks.heading: 2.18 Apron Safety/Security Procedures
chunks.text: Vehicles transporting staff to service the aircraft shall be parked outside the circle of safety. Direct contact vehicles Vehicles that need direct contact with the aircraft are Ambu-lift/aircraft step/ cargo loading trucks/ high loaders etc. Persons Walking Across Tarmac/ Safety Attire All persons shall observe the circle of safety and don a reflective tabard (safety attire) when walking on the tarmac/ramp. CCMs shall wear the tabard when on the ramp for baggage identification or other- wise. Photography Photography will not be permitted as per the regulations in force at the respective airports.

chunks.heading: 2.19 ETOPS/EDTO
chunks.text: Extended Range Operations with Two-Engine Aircraft./Extended Diversion Time Operation ETOPS/EDTO is an acronym from International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), a rule permitting new- er twin-engine commercial aircraft to fly routes that, at some points are further than a distance of 60 minutes flying time from an emergency or diversion airport. Authorisation for ETOPS/ times are 120,180 minutes from a suitable aerodrome available subject to the operator showing compliance with the laid down operational criteria, and the aircraft airframe/engine combination has the appropriate Type Design approval. EDTO is an acronym from ICAO for any operation by an aeroplane with two or more turbines where the diversion time to an En-route alternate aerodrome is greater than the threshold time established by the state of the operator. Shall comply with SLCAIS 062

chunks.heading: 2.20 Regulation on Smoking/Consumption of Alcohol/Psychoactive Substances
chunks.text:
Smoking - Smoking is prohibited on any Civil Aircraft registered in Sri Lanka. Ref SLCAIS 74 E- cigarettes and Vape are permitted only in crew and passengers carryon baggage. Recharging and use of E-cigarettes and Vape shall not be permitted inflight. Cabin Crew member Responsibility for non-Compliance CCM shall ensure passengers adhere to the regulation, if not follow the below mentioned procedure,
1. Carry out a verbal warning ( if it fails to achieve compliance)
2. The Purser shall be guided by the disruptive passenger policy, Ref 2.24.2.1
3. Purser to hand over a final warning authorised by PIC, stating it is the final warning
4. Purser to fill in an DPIR Ref 2.36.8 In addition to the above, CCMs should be vigilant and ensure no smoking regulation is adhered to when,
1. Administering oxygen
2. In a Decompression

chunks.heading: 2.20.1 Regulation on Alcohol/Psychoactive Substances
chunks.text: A person who appears to be intoxicated or who demonstrates by manner or physical indications that the individual is under the influence of psychoactive substances shall not be permitted to enter the aircraft. On observation, the Purser shall infom the PIC and Ground staff for necessary action.

chunks.heading: 2.20.1.1 Procedure for Serving Alcohol
chunks.text: Passengers are prohibited to consume alcohol on board an aircraft unless served by the airline. Hence they are not permitted to consume alcohol from their personal possession. The Purser is empowered to refuse serving alcohol if a passenger exhibits signs of intoxication.

chunks.heading: 2.20.1.1 Procedure for Serving Alcohol
chunks.text:
Alcoholic beverages shall not be served to the following:
1. Passenger who appears to be intoxicated
2. An escorted Prisoner/ Escorted Deportee/ Deportee Escort/ INAD
3. Anyone under the age of 18
4. Any person occupying a Flight Deck or Cabin Crew assist seat If a passenger does not follow instructions and continues to consume alcohol off a personal bottle, Purser shall deliver a verbal warning and keep the PIC informed. If he continues, the PIC should be informed and the final warning document signed by the PIC shall be handed over to the passenger. The bottle should be confiscated,the content measured,kept in the custody of the Purser and handed over to the Security Personnel at the arrival airport. The Disruptive Passenger Incident Report (DPIR) with witness reports should be forwarded to the Cor- porate Safety along with the VR. Ref 2.36 Note : It is mandatory to complete a DPIR form for every incident of unruly/disruptive behaviour

chunks.heading: 2.20.1.1 Procedure for Serving Alcohol
chunks.text: that may threaten the safety of the aircraft or its occupants

chunks.heading: 2.21.1 Incident
chunks.text: An occurrence, other than an accident, associated with the operation of an aircraft which could affect the safe operation such as, Jeopardises the safety of crew, passengers or aircraft.Cause trauma to the crew or passengers.Cause damage to any major components.

chunks.heading: 2.21.2 Accident
chunks.text: An occurrence associated with the operation of an aircraft that takes place between the time any per- son boards the aircraft with the intention of flight and such time as all persons have disembarked there from, which Any person suffers death or serious injury, Except when the injuries are self-inflicted or inflicted by other persons or when the injuries caused due to stowaways hiding outside the areas availa- ble to the passengers and Crew. The aircraft incurs damage or structural failure, The aircraft is missing or completely inaccessible. Reporting: In the event of an incident/ accident during flight, the Purser shall forward a duly completed report bearing in mind that the reader should be able to obtain an overall view of the incident stating the specific details, timings and locations. The report shall state the occurrences in the sequence that took place, and shall include additional

chunks.heading: 2.21.2 Accident
chunks.text: information helpful for an investigation.

chunks.heading: 2.21.3 Reporting To Authority
chunks.text: The Accident/Serious Incident must be notified immediately by the aircraft commander to the compa- ny. The commander or Flight Safety Manger or Operations Control Manager at Airlines Operations Con- trol Centre (AOCC) must raise the Accident/Serious Incident Reports Immediately with the minimum of delay and by expeditious means to Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka and all other official agencies concerned, with a copy to AOCC and the original to Corporate Safety. The Purser shall inform the PIC and forward a completed report to the Manager Group Safety on arrival at base or on electronic format at overseas stations, in keeping with the policy. In the event the Inci- dent/Accident is pertaining to the Purser, or the Purser is injured, the next most suitable Cabin Supervi- sor shall be responsible to ensure compliance. The report shall be submitted to the DGCA by the Coop- erate Safety Section.

chunks.heading: 2.21.4 Follow-Up Action/Selection of Witnesses
chunks.text: If a CCM/Passenger is required to be a witness in an incident/accident, Purser should ensure the wit- nesses of incident/accident fill up the witness form. The following are the guidelines but not restricted to when selecting a witness. Crew/passengers who witnessed the incident/part of the incident or accident A witness (passenger) who is a resident or employed in the country of prosecution

chunks.heading: 2.22 Hazardous Material Information System
chunks.text: Srilankan Airlines sets and enforces occupational safety and health standards in the work place. The objective is to ensure a safe and healthy working environment is maintained for all employees and crew. The company further encourages voluntary compliance through consultation/partnerships and promotes training and education on safety for its employees.

chunks.heading: 2.22.1 Voluntary Disclosure of Safety or Security Matters
chunks.text: The CAASL requires employees to voluntarily disclose hazardous occurrences/accidents/ security sen- sitive or any other malpractices which takes place in the airline which will result in an unsafe working environment. The reporting is encouraged to identify cause of the events to ensure that suitable corrective action is taken and not apportion blame to any individual/s involved. An Air/Ground Safety Report (AGSR) is available for voluntary disclosure on incidents/accidents/fatigue or any other matters relating to safety. When an AGSR is raised, it should be addressed and forwarded to the Senior Manager Group Safety and shall be signed prior to submitting.

chunks.heading: 2.22.2 Discomfort on Board
chunks.text: The crew shall inform the Purser regarding any passengers or crew feeling dizzy/ faintish/ difficulty in breathing or vomiting. The Purser in turn will inform the PIC for any remedial action and documentation on the Technical Defects logbook. The Purser shall enter it in the Cabin Defects Logbook giving specific details for rectification prior to the next departure.

chunks.heading: 2.22.3 Non Punitive Reporting
chunks.text:
Voluntary disclosure is a method of non-punitive information expected from staff to implement and maintain safer working methods. Establishing a reporting system is to encourage a proactive safety culture system wide. It is not recommended to report on behalf of another. Reporting may include the under mentioned but not restricted to:
1. Using wrong procedures or deviating from standard operating procedures
2. Ignoring procedures
3. Lack of knowledge/ comprehension or skills to perform tasks
4. Use of improper equipment or tools
5. Lack of facilities or inadequate facilities for maximum performance
6. Giving or obeying wrong orders
7. Disobeying orders
8. Carelessness /Negligence
9. Hurrying to finish a task
10. Lack of concentration due to overwork or inadequate rest
11. Habitually undertaking risks
12. Improper management or lack of awareness
13. Lack of training or inadequate training

chunks.heading: 2.22.3 Non Punitive Reporting
chunks.text:
14. Lack of supervision
15. Excessive workload
16. Lack of fitness to work/lethargy-laziness
17. Lack or inadequate two way communication
18. Misunderstanding/Misguidance
19. Misinterpretation or ambiguity
20. Low alertness due to direct or accumulated fatigue

chunks.heading: 2.23 Refuelling and De-fuelling (fuelling) Procedures
chunks.text:
Subject to any local airport regulation and/or restrictions, minimum required CCM’s are on-board. Ref 2.13.1. Fuelling is permitted with passengers on board the aircraft or while embarkation and disembar- kation is taking place. The following precautions must be observed.
1. One qualified person shall remain in the Flight deck during fuelling and be capable of using emergency procedures for fire protection and fire fighting, communications, as well as for initiat- ing and directing an evacuation
2. Two-way communication shall be established and remain available through the aircraft’s inter- communications system, or other suitable means, between the ground crew that supervises the refuelling and the qualified personnel on board the aircraft. When designation of exits for rapid de-planing or an evacuation, the following factors should be consid- ered: Aircraft type (Eg; some aircraft might require to designate over wing hatches), Number of CCMs

chunks.heading: 2.23 Refuelling and De-fuelling (fuelling) Procedures
chunks.text:
on board, the method utilized for de-planing passengers (steps/aero-bridges), Exterior obstructions (parked service vehicles) that might block one or more exits. Cabin crew procedures to ensure a method of two-way communication is established,
1. Among CCMs positioned throughout the cabin for coordination should an evacuation be re- quired
2. Between CCMs and passengers (one-way) for the purpose of providing instructions for an emer- gency evacuation
3. Between CCMs and Flight crew (when on board) for notification of refuelling commencement and when an evacuation is required
4. Between Cabin crew/Flight crew/Engineering/Ground handling personnel for the purpose of ensuring notification, if fuelling needs to be discontinued for any reason

chunks.heading: 2.23.2 Flight Crew Responsibilities
chunks.text: Shall Advice the Purser when fuelling commences and ensure the fasten seat belt sign is switched off and the no smoking signs are illuminated (if applicable).

chunks.heading: 2.23.3 Engineering Staff Responsibilities
chunks.text: The engineer-in-charge/technician shall be responsible in keeping the Purser/In charge CCM informed when fuelling commences.

chunks.heading: 2.23.4 CCM Responsibilities, When fuelling with Passengers
chunks.text: On receiving the information, the Purser shall initiate the following announcement: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, AS THE AIRCRAFT IS BEEN FUELLED, WE ADVICE ALL PASSENGERS TO KEEP YOUR SEAT BELTS OPENED AND SWITCH-OFF MOBILE PHONES UNTIL THE SEAT BELT SIGN IS SWITCHED ON, THANK YOU”.

chunks.heading: 2.23.4 CCM Responsibilities, When fuelling with Passengers
chunks.text:
CCMs shall ensure the following while fuelling is in progress:
1. One cabin crew member is positioned by the boarding door (s).
2. Passengers open their seat belts, Prepared for an emergency evacuation
3. Cabin lighting selected to bright
4. Passengers do not smoke/strike matches/use cigarette lighters/ use mobile phones In case of an emergency, passengers shall be evacuated using at least two main exits. To fulfil this re- quirement, the following shall be adhered to:
1. One FWD passenger exit shall be opened with an aero-bridge or steps positioned and
2. One AFT passenger exit should be opened with steps positioned,
3. If the AFT passenger exit is kept closed, the area below shall be clear of obstruction including catering/service trucks or boarding steps. This shall enable the deployment of the slide safely.
4. All aisles / cross aisles and exits are free of obstruction
5. Half the number of exits shall be manned. (Each CCM is responsible for the opposite door)

chunks.heading: 2.23.4 CCM Responsibilities, When fuelling with Passengers
chunks.text:
6. Should any condition arise during fuelling, which may constitute a potential hazard (detection of fuel vapour in the cabin etc.) notify the Flight Crew/Ground Engineer and prepare for a deplan- ing
7. No meal services to be carried out If deplaning of passengers is required steps/aerobridge is preferred, than the use of escape slides

chunks.heading: 2.24 Carriage of Special Handling Passengers (Passengers with Alerts)
chunks.text:
The PIC/Purser shall be notified when the above passengers are traveling. The seat allocation and type of service will vary depending on the category of passengers. Allocation of seats is the responsibility of the reservations/ground handling departments. However, CCMs shall ensure the seat allocation regula- tions are adhered to whilst the passenger is on board.
1. Passengers with a Security Alert
2. Passenger with a Medical Alert
3. Passengers with Assistance Alert

chunks.heading: 2.24.1 Armed Passengers
chunks.text: Whenever armed guards on official VIP’s escort duties or other authorised state officials are travelling on SriLankan Airlines flights, the laid down procedures shall be followed (Security Handling). Ref 8.5

chunks.heading: CAUTION: NO PASSENGER IS ALLOWED TO CARRY WEAPONS AND/OR AMMUNITION IN THE
chunks.text: CABIN. IF A PASSENGER DECLARES OR IS DETECTED WITH SUCH ITEMS, INFORM PIC, CHECK

chunks.heading: FOR REQUIRED AUTHORISATION/PERMITS AND ADVISE THE PASSENGER SUCH CAN BE CAR -
chunks.text: RIED ONLY IN CHECKED IN BAGGAGE. SUCH ITEMS SHALL BE RETRIEVED BY AIRPORT SECURI- TY AND WOULD BE LOADED IN THE DESIGNATED LOCATION .

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.1 Disruptive passenger
chunks.text:
Type of Disruptive Behaviour, A disruptive passenger is a person who may, but not limited to;
1. Use threatening/abusive or suggestive language
2. Imperil the safety of the aircraft/passengers or crew
3. Suffer from a mental/physical state and the conduct may cause discomfort or make him objec- tionable to other passengers
4. Involving in any hazard or risk to the passengers/crew or property
5. Refusing to observe/comply with the instructions of SriLankan Airlines staff
6. Indecent exposure
7. Assault of a Crew Member/passenger The Disruptive Passenger Policy SriLankan Airlines has a zero tolerance policy for abusive/disruptive passengers. The Company shall take reasonable steps to ensure a safe and secure environment for its customers and employees on board its aircraft. The following shall be considered when transporting such passengers
i. The risk on other passengers, crew and aircraft

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.1 Disruptive passenger
chunks.text:
ii. The type of the aircraft and the number of such passengers
iii. The risk evaluation on the special category passenger (Prisoner, Deportee & Inadmissible) If the passenger is considered a potential risk, a minimum of two escorts shall be provided. The number to transport and the potential threat should be determined by the airline (security man- agement) and agreed by the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.2 Inadmissible Passenger (INAD)
chunks.text: An “inadmissible passenger” (INAD) is a passenger, who is refused admission to a country by authori- ties of that country eg. due invalid visa, expired passport etc. Alcoholic beverages shall not be served to

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.3 Deportee with Escorts
chunks.text: A deportee is a passenger, who has legally arrived in a country, or who entered a country illegally and who at some later time is ordered by the authorities to leave the State and if considered dangerous, Deportee should be escorted by two or more security officers, they shall be seated on either side of the deportee. Wide body aircraft maxium of 04 DEPA/DEPU passengers and narrow body aircraft maxium of

chunks.heading: 02 DEPA/DEPU passengers
chunks.text:
1. The escorting officers shall identify themselves to the Purser/PIC.
2. Service of meals to such a deportee shall be with plastic cutlery.
3. Alcoholic beverages shall not be served to the escorting officers or the deportee.
4. Deportee shall be escorted to the toilet

chunks.heading: 02 DEPA/DEPU passengers
chunks.text: 5. DEPA/DEPU shall be indicated on the PIL. Note : A deportee passenger (DEPU) unescorted and (DEPA) escorted

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.4 Prisoners in custody with Escorts
chunks.text: Prisoners and passengers in Custody are handled by the SriLankan Airlines Security and Investigation Department who are the authorised personnel to determine the maximum number allowed and the number of escort Security officers required. They shall be accepted with authorised escorts and be seat- ed at the rear end of the aircraft and never at an emergency exit. Prisoners and passengers in custody must be boarded first and disembarked last. The ground/security staff shall inform the PIC/Purser prior to boarding a Prisoner/Escort. Service of meals to the prisoner should be with plastic cutlery. Alcoholic beverages shall not be served to the escorting officers or the prisoner. At transit stations, the Purser shall ensure the disembarking crew introduces the escorts and identifies the deportee/prisoner to the joining crew, and handover the necessary documents for onward carriage. On arrival, the deportee/prisoner should remain seated (unless specified) until the Purser introduces

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.4 Prisoners in custody with Escorts
chunks.text: the escorts and identifies the deportee/prisoner and hand over documents to the ground staff or rele- vant authorities. In certain countries they shall be disembarked first. Prisoner should be escorted by two or more security officers, they shall be seated on either side of the Prisoner.

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.5 Boarding /Seating Passengers With a Security Alert
chunks.text:
The ground staff shall inform the PIC/Purser prior to boarding a passenger with a security alert.
1. Purser shall ensure the alert passenger is identified by all CCMs
2. The CS in charge shall not allow the passenger to disembark at transit stations
3. The local immigration or relevant authority at the departure/arrival stations shall be notified in accordance with local laws and regulations They should board the aircraft prior to other passengers and disembark (unless specified) last. The seats at the rear of the aircraft shall be allocated to escorting officers and the alert passenger. CCMs shall ensure the passenger does not have the opportunity to gain access to offensive or dangerous articles during flight. The passenger if escorted should be under surveillance by the escorting officers, right throughout the journey (i.e. visiting the lavatory etc.).

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.6 Refusal of Carriage
chunks.text:
CCMs shall be vigilant during boarding for following passengers, who may be unfit to travel,
1. Passengers who appears to be under the influence of alcohol and/or psychoactive drugs at a level that may risk the safety of the aircraft, other passengers and himself during an emergency,

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.6 Refusal of Carriage
chunks.text:
2. Passengers who have sustained serious injury prior to boarding,
3. Passengers who are medically unfit due to illness/injury,
4. Passengers who have been detected to have an infectious diseases and/or within the incubation period of any infectious diseases (e.g. chicken pox, measles etc…)
5. Unruly passengers, Non adherence to crew instructions Inform PIC/Dispatcher and off load passenger if required

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.7 Off-Loading
chunks.text:
The PIC or ground staff may use their authority to off-load a disruptive passenger if there is reasonable doubt that his presence may jeopardise the safety of the aircraft or its occupants and/or but not re- stricted to the following:
1. If the disruptive behaviour takes place prior to passenger boarding or at the point of boarding, the ground staff should deny boarding.
2. If the disruptive behaviour takes place whilst taxiing the Purser shall inform the PIC and he may decide to return to the parking bay and off-load the passenger.
3. If the disruptive behaviour takes place during flight, the PIC may decide to off-load the passen- ger at the next scheduled destination or in extreme situations, divert the aircraft to the nearest airport to off load the passenger/s.

chunks.heading: 2.24.2.8 Handling a Disruptive Passenger
chunks.text: The PIC may delegate to the Purser, his authority to deal with any disruptive situation that occurs in the aircraft. The Purser shall take charge of the situation and request those witnessing the incident (passengers) to assist in restraining the passenger/complete a witness report form with names/seat numbers and any other personal details as required. The Purser shall report all details to the PIC and submit a completed Disruptive Passenger Incident Re- port form (DPIR) to the Cooprate Safety along with the witness reports etc. A copy will be forwarded to the Manager Security and Investigations and the Authority. The Purser shall be guided by the following procedures when handling a disruptive passenger:

chunks.heading: 2.24.3 Warning
chunks.text:
1. Formally warned (verbal warning) carried out
2. Final warning notice read to passenger and handed over
3. Seek authorisation from the PIC to use the restraints
4. Use the restraints with the assistance of passengers if required
5. Reseat the passenger in the AFT with the permission of the PIC (if possible)

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.1 Formal Warning
chunks.text: The Purser shall carry out a formal (Verbal) warning to a passenger who exhibits disruptive behaviour.

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.2 Final warning
chunks.text: If the formal warning fails to achieve compliance, the Purser shall read out and hand over the final warning document authorised by the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.3 Police Assistance
chunks.text: In the event a disruptive passenger is off loaded, the PIC may request Police/Security assistance. Any carry on/checked-in baggage of the passenger should be off loaded. (Passengers may be required to remain in their seats until the disruptive passenger/ passengers are off loaded)

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.4 Use of Restraining Ties
chunks.text:
The following procedure shall be followed, prior to and during restraining a passenger. Any measures to restrain a passenger shall be with the authorisation of the PIC. Briefing - in the event of a decompression, the passenger seated next to the restrained passenger shall be briefed to assist the disruptive passenger with the oxygen mask. Subject to restraining CCMs shall,Check on blood circulation regularly,
1. Brief the passengers adjacent on the (procedure) in case of a decompression
2. Sit at a CCM seat, adjacent to the passenger seat for landing with a pair of scissors kept in the vicinity,
3. Cut the restraints in a planned emergency with the PIC’s permission,
4. Allocate a centre seat at the rear of the cabin,
5. If escorted, brief them on the procedure in the event of a decompression or an emergency.
6. Removing the restraints for any other reason is at the sole discretion of the PIC.

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.4 Use of Restraining Ties
chunks.text: A passenger once restrained shall be handed over to the relevant authorities on arrival.

chunks.heading: 2.24.3.5 Legal Action by the Company
chunks.text: In the event a CCM is subjected to physical assault, a report must be submitted to the company without delay and the company may in accordance with applicable laws and regulations initiate a civil or Crimi- nal complaint against the passenger. At overseas stations, the Station Manager or a senior member of its staff shall assist the PIC, Purser and the CCMs involved when dealing with the Police and/or relevant authorities. The In-flight Services man- agement shall be informed at the earliest.

chunks.heading: 2.24.4 Passenger with a Medical Alert
chunks.text: Passengers under medication and or on the way for treatment / after treatment is categorised as pas- sengers with a Medical alert.

chunks.heading: 2.24.4 Passenger with a Medical Alert
chunks.text: Cabin Crew training is limited to handle injuries and illness on board.

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.1 Medical Clearance
chunks.text:
Not all incapacitated passengers require medical clearance before being accepted for travel. However, passengers with the following incapacities and/or disabilities such as Alzheimer’s, Downs Syndrome, Autism, Dementia, Learning difficulties (other) and cognitive impairment must be subject to medical clearance by the UL GMO/CMO before being accepted for travel. In addition:
1. Those who, because of certain diseases or incapacitations, may have or may develop unusual behaviour or physical conditions which could have an adverse effect on the welfare and comfort of other passengers and/or crew members
2. Those who can be considered to be a potential hazard to the safety or punctuality of the flight, including possible diversion and unscheduled landing
3. Those who would require medical attention/constant monitoring and/or special equipment to maintain their health during the flight
4. Those who may have their medical condition aggravated during or because of the flight

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.1 Medical Clearance
chunks.text: 5. Those suffering from a disease, which is believed to be actively contagious and communicable. In order to facilitate acceptance of a passenger with a disability for travel by air, the passenger’s person- al doctor shall complete the SriLankan Airlines Medical Information Form (MEDIF).

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.2 Passenger with Disabilities (PWD)
chunks.text: The category of passenger with disabilities is as, Ambulatory Able to board/disembark/move about unassisted. Non-ambulatory Unable to board/disembark/move about unassisted. A PWD is a person whose physical/medical or mental condition requires assistance when embarking/ during flight/disembarking/on ground and in an emergency. The Purser shall inform the PIC of PWDs after referring the passenger information list. When the above passengers travel, depending on the category and disability, they shall board prior to other passengers with the escort (if available) to be briefed on safety/emergency procedures. If appli- cable, briefed on securing and opening seatbelts, donning of life jackets for a ditching and oxygen mask during a decompression. Allocation of seats/stretcher as per regulations is the responsibility of the Reservations/Ground Handling Departments. However, CCMs shall ensure the seat/stretcher allocation

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.2 Passenger with Disabilities (PWD)
chunks.text:
regulations are adhered to whilst the passenger is on the aircraft. The number of PWDs accepted on a flight shall not exceed the number of ABPs capable of assisting them in an emergency evacuation. Accepting a PWD on board,
• PWDs shall board the aircraft first for departure and the relevant safety briefing shall be con- ducted by the relevant CCM.
• Frequent checks shall be carried out during flight to ensure safety and comfort of the PWD.
• CCM to brief PWDs prior to landing to remain seated until assistance is provided. Handing Over a PWD, The PWD shall be handed over to the relevant station staff by the Purser or Cabin Supervisor 2 by ensuring they disembark in an orderly manner once all other passengers have disembarked to prevent injury/discomfort. Passenger In A Wheelchair Is a person who requires assistance when boarding/during flight/disembarking and on ground. Such passengers are categorised as follows,

chunks.heading: WCHR
chunks.text: Passengers who can ascend/descend steps and make own way to/from cabin seat but cannot manage long distances (wheel chair Ramp)

chunks.heading: WCHS
chunks.text: Passengers who cannot ascend/descend steps but is able to make own way to/ from the cabin seat to the exit (wheel chair Steps)

chunks.heading: WCHC
chunks.text: Passengers completely immobile and requires wheel chair to/from cabin seat (wheelchair Cabin) MEDA Passenger Is a person who may travel for/after medical attention and requires assistance when boarding/during flight/disembarking and on ground. Approval by the GMO/CMO is required for clearance to travel cate-

chunks.heading: WCHC
chunks.text:
gorising the level of assistance. CCMs shall be guided by the following precautions when allocating seats for the passenger
1. Seats shall not be allocated at emergency exit seat/seat rows
2. Two non-ambulatory passengers should not be seated across the aisle (e.g. Seat C and D)
3. Accompanying escorts should be allocated the relevant aisle seat
4. Passenger with a plaster cast should not be seated obstructing the aisle

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.2.1 Reassurance Briefing
chunks.text:
CCMs shall conduct a briefing to PWDs as follows,
1. CCMs would be assigned to assist during an emergency
2. In an emergency, remain seated until assisted by the crew
3. Mobility Aids shall not be used in an evacuation, but assisted by the crew

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.3 Passenger on a Stretcher
chunks.text: May be paralytic or severely ill person categorised as: Quadriplegic Passenger Paralysed from the neck or shoulder down Paraplegic Passenger Paralysed from the legs and/or some part of the body Hemiplegics Passenger Paralysed on either side of the body Qualified medical personnel shall accompany the above stated passengers. The stretcher locations are pre-determined and a maximum of two stretcher passengers could be accommodated on an aircraft. For carriage, medical clearance by the GMO/CMO and a completed MEDA form is required. The stretch- er positions Ref 2.35

chunks.heading: 2.24.4.3.1 Briefing for an escort accompanying a stretcher passenger
chunks.text:
Cabin Supervisor shall carry out a briefing to the escort as follows:
1. To remain in the vicinity of the stretcher passenger
2. In an emergency, the exits and alternates which would be used
3. Discuss details and precautions when evacuating the passenger without the stretcher
4. The escort shall be briefed to place the drop-down oxygen mask on the stretcher passenger in the event of a decompression after donning their personal mask
5. Fit the life vest to the stretcher passenger in case of a ditching evacuation

chunks.heading: 2.24.5 Passengers with Assistance Alert
chunks.text:
• A passenger with assistance alert is a person who is stable but needs assistance when boarding/ during flight/disembarking/on ground and in an emergency.
• Even though they may have their own doctor’s certificates of fitness for travel, medical clear-

chunks.heading: 2.24.5 Passengers with Assistance Alert
chunks.text:
ance shall be referred to UL Medical Centre and the SriLankan Airlines Medical Information Form (MEDIF) has to be completed for travel.
• Persons who are reduced in mobility due to age (between 75 - 85 years of age need to provide a copy of the Passport data page at the time of booking). A form of Indemnity to be signed by the- passenger at the time of acceptance to prove that s/he can fend themselves, have meals without any assistance and manage the toilet needs on board the aircraft on their own without any assis- tance.
• Seating shall be assigned as per SriLankan Airlines policy, which is most suited to meet the pas- senger’s need.
• In order to meet safety requirements, such passengers shall not be allocated seats where they would obstruct emergency exits, impede the crew in their duties, obstruct access to emergency equipment or hinder an evacuation.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.1 Blind Passenger
chunks.text: A Service Animal may accompany a blind passenger who is mobile with /without assistance. (Ref 2.29.2) A passenger, with a guide dog, should be assigned a window seat at a bulkhead, non- emergency exit row so the dog has enough floor space to lie on and other passengers do not step on it.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.1.1 Briefing a blind Passenger (SOLE B)
chunks.text: CCMs shall conduct a briefing using the demo kit as follows: Seat belt Fastening adjusting and opening the seat belt Oxygen mask Location and Usage Life Vest Location & Usage Exits Closest and alternate exits / number of seats rows from the exits Bracing How to brace and pay attention to all the announcements The passenger seated next to the blind passenger (buddy), shall be briefed to assist the said passenger to don the oxygen mask in the event of a decompression. Reservations code: BLND Blind Passengers do not require a medical certificate for clearance to travel by air. They will be provided assistance by the ground staff during the process of boarding and disembarkation. Two blind passengers shall not be seated across the aisle. If blind passengers travel with escorts, the escorts shall be seated at an aisle seats next to the blind passenger. A Blind passenger is not permitted to be seated at any emergency exit. SriLankan Airlines will not provide passengers with any assistance

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.1.1 Briefing a blind Passenger (SOLE B)
chunks.text: for personal care needs on board the aircraft such as:consumption of food and drink, administration of medication, elimination functions including assistance inside the lavatory or other personal care needs. If such assistance is required during flight, the blind passenger shall travel with a personal care atten- dant or make alternative arrangements. A Service Animal may accompany them. Ref 2.29.2

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.2 Differently Able Passenger (Deaf)
chunks.text: Passengers who need less help but may communicate mainly through sign language/ lip reading or writ- ing. A Hearing dog may accompany them. Ref 2.29.2

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.2 Differently Able Passenger (Deaf)
chunks.text: Reservations code: DEAF Deaf passengers are considered ambulatory/mobile and therefore they do not require any special assis- tance. No restrictions to the numbers that may be carried. In the event of a large group of deaf pas- sengers (e.g. 20 Deaf students), they must be accompanied by able-bodied passenger at a ratio of 1:4. When a group of deaf passengers are booked to travel, they must be seated together as a group with their escort(s). Briefing CCMs shall conduct a briefing advising the passenger the importance of observing signs to brace and to evacuate when required.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.3 Expectant Mother
chunks.text: Expectant mothers are required to visit the medical practitioner prior to travel , in order to inquire about their fitness to fly the length of the trip.Expectant mothers without any complications traveling after their 28 th week of pregnancy are required to provide a medical certificate from a qualified medical practitioner issued within 7 days of travel, confirming the pregnancy is free of complications, Fitness to travel and the estimate date of delivery. Expectant mothers with multiple and /or complicated pregnan- cy shall carry a medical certificate at all times from a qualified medical practitioner issued within 7 days of travel, confirming fitness to travel and the estimate date of delivery During an evacuation, the appointed ABP shall assist by blocking other passengers and helping the ex- pectant mother to open the seat belt and evacuate. Single Uncomplicated Pregnancy Up to 36 weeks of pregnancy For flights up to 4 hours only

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.3 Expectant Mother
chunks.text: Up to 35 weeks of pregnancy No restriction Multiple, Complicated Pregnancies (twins/triplets etc.) Up to 32 weeks of pregnancy For flight up to 4 hours Up to 28 weeks of pregnancy No restriction Air travel is not recommended within the last 7 days prior to the confinement and within the first 7 days after delivery. At the time of passenger boarding if the CCMs observe any doubt regarding the above guidelines they should inform the Purser.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.4 Briefing an Expectant Mother
chunks.text: An expectant mother shall be advised to place and secure the belt over the hips and below the abdo- men and avoid placing any pillows between the seat belt and abdomen.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.5 Carriage of New-born Babies
chunks.text: New-born babies cannot be accepted for air travel within the first 7 days of birth. Prematurely born

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.5 Carriage of New-born Babies
chunks.text: babies, babies born with delivery complications who require immediate medical treatment, who are below 7 days old can be accepted only with medical clearance. A qualified escort eg. Doctor, Specialized Medical Nurse shall escort the baby. An indemnity to be signed by the parent and/or guardian who accompanies the baby. Passenger Infor- mation List (PIL) to be handed over to Purser. At the time of passenger boarding if the CCMs observe any doubt regarding the above guidelines they should inform the Purser. Recommended travel to be practiced for new born babies/infants

chunks.heading: REMARKS
chunks.text: Normal Healthy Babies From 7 days up to the age not exceeding 02 years

chunks.heading: NO
chunks.text: Accompanied by parents or an adult over 18 yrs. or suitable es- cort e.g. Qualified Nurse New Born Babies Below 7 days YES Accompanied by parents or suita- ble escort e.g. Qualified Nurse Premature babies with or without complications Babies with delivery complica- tions Babies who require immediate medical treatment depending on the severity of the illness From birth up to the age not exceeding 02 years

chunks.heading: YES
chunks.text: Escort needed: e.g. Medical Practitioner, Qualified nurse and/or Attendant

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.6 Adults with Infants
chunks.text: Briefing for adults with infants (SLOB Briefing) Ref 2.25.5 Elderly/Frail passenger Is a person who may require assistance when boarding/during flight /disembarking/ on ground and in an emergency. They may be under medication. Assistance to and from the lavatory may be required and should be advised how to lock /unlock the lavatory door and the use of the attendant call button in the lavatory. If they are elderly and frail, they shall not occupy a seat next to an emergency exit.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.7 Un-Accompanied Minors (U/M)
chunks.text: A child between the ages of 5 - 11 years, and not accompanied by an adult over 18 years is defined as a U/M. A U/M accepted for travel is in the custody of SriLankan Airlines until handed over to the parent/ guardian. When accepting a U/M/s, all required documents shall be completed and handed over to the

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.7 Un-Accompanied Minors (U/M)
chunks.text: Purser by the ground staff. The Purser shall ensure the following is received in the UM pouch; name and address of the U/M, name and phone number of the person authorised to accept the U/M, special instructions (Medicine/ Food/Allergies), ticket/boarding passes/passport/baggage claim tags, accepting and handing over booklet with details. A female CCM from the operating crew shall be nominated to be responsible for the U/M. During a change of crew, the taking over Purser shall accept the UM, complete documentation and introduce the UM to the rest of the CCMs. In the event, a CCM is dedicated for the U/M/s, the said CCM shall not disembark at any transit point and shall continue the duration of the journey with the U/M/s. Allocation of seats is the responsibility of the Reservations/Ground Handling Departments. However, CCMs shall ensure U/M’s are not seated next to an adult male passenger whilst in the aircraft.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.7.1 Briefing a UM/YP
chunks.text:
1. Inform the unaccompanied minor which adult will assist with the operation of the seat belt and the fitting of the oxygen if the situation requires it.
2. The content of the passenger briefing card and in case of evacuation to seek assistance of adult passenger in contacting a crew member.
3. Inform the passenger sitting next to the unaccompanied minor to assist with, providing the mi- nor with an oxygen mask in case of a decompression after fitting one’s own mask
4. Securing/releasing the minor’s seatbelt, if necessary and calling a cabin crew member in all oth- er in flight situations. Note - A child under the age of 12 years separated from the accompanying adult, who is travelling in another cabin class, shall be considered a UM in order to ensure that the child is assisted in case of an emergency and appropriate briefing carried out. The adult and child should be informed that in the

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.7.1 Briefing a UM/YP
chunks.text: event of an emergency they should follow the instructions of cabin crew and not try to reunite inside the cabin as this would slow down the overall evacuation.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.8 The pre-determined seats for U/M/s
chunks.text:
1. B/C - any seat
2. E/Y – Outboard left rows (A/C) as stipulated according to the aircraft type

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.9 Dedicated CCM for special handling of U/M’s
chunks.text:
An additional (dedicated) CCM shall be assigned to take care of U/Ms. The specified duties for the CCM shall be limited to being responsible for them.
1. A child between ages of 2 - 5 yrs, up to a maximum of 3 children are accepted for travel provid- ed the services of an Escort (Flight Stewardess) is obtained by the parent/guardian.
2. As per SriLankan Airlines policy, maximum number of U/M’s (5 -11 years)allowed on-board an aircraft is 15 numbers. Whenever there are more than 15 U/M’s travelling on any one flight, it is UL’s policy to assign an additional stewardess to care for the children on board.
3. If a U/M is a PWD, the dedicated CCM shall be responsible for only for 01 child.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.9 Dedicated CCM for special handling of U/M’s
chunks.text:
4. Children below the age of 5 but over 2 years of age or those who require special attention (i.e. Differently able) may be accepted as an UM provided the services of an Escort (Flight Steward- ess) is obtained by the parent/guardian.
5. The dedicated CCM shall sit adjacent to the U/M.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.10 Young Passengers (YP)
chunks.text: Passengers between the ages of 12 - 15 years are categorised as Y/P’s Assistance would be offered according to the request/requirement. A young passenger from the age of 12 to 15 may request to travel as an U/M.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.11 Intellectual Disability
chunks.text: SriLankan Airlines will assist individuals with cognitive and developmental disabilities in boarding and disembarking, and in making flight connections between gates when applicable. An escort will not be available to remain with or supervise the passenger whilst in the terminal building or in-flight, to en- sure that the passenger’s travel needs are met. It is important that passengers requiring such assistance state their needs at the time of reservation.

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.12 Travelling with an assistant/attendant
chunks.text: For safety reasons, SriLankan Airlines require some passengers with cognitive or development disa- bilities to travel with a safety assistant that can provide them with assistance in comprehending and responding appropriately to safety instructions from cabin crew and/or assist them to evacuate the air- craft in the event of an emergency. The safety assistant or personal care attendant must be self-reliant and mentally and physically able to provide the passenger with the assistance required. If such passen- gers are identified it shall be brought to the attention of Purser/PIC immediately

chunks.heading: 2.24.5.13 Assistance on Board for Passengers with assistant and medical alert
chunks.text: SriLankan Airlines will not provide passengers with any assistance for personal care needs on board the aircraft such as: consumption of food/drink, administration of medication, elimination functions includ- ing assistance inside the lavatory, or other personal care needs. If such assistance is required inflight, it is recommended that the passenger travel with a personal care attendant or make alternative arrange- ments.

chunks.heading: 2.25 Passenger Seat
chunks.text:
It is a regulatory requirement that each passenger on board has a fully functioning seat. The safety feature of a passenger seat shall consist of, Functional Seat belt/adjustable seat back/passenger service unit- (Drop down Oxygen masks)/life vest and a relevant safety card/disruptive passenger leaflet. A passenger seat shall be allocated to each adult and child - (2 years and above). Each passenger shall occupy a fully functional seat with the seat belt securely fastened during:
1. Taxiing / Take-off/ Landing (TTOL)
2. In an emergency when required
3. When the seat belt sign is switched on

chunks.heading: 2.25 Passenger Seat
chunks.text: Multiple occupancy of a passenger seat is permitted when an infant is lap carried by an adult, secured by a kangaroo belt to the adult’s seat belt.

chunks.heading: 2.25.1 Emergency Exit Row Seating
chunks.text:
Occupancy of emergency exit row seating is restricted as per SriLankan airline’s policy which is also approved by the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (CAASL). Seats adjacent to emergency exits shall be allocated only to able-bodied adults (above 18 years) who appear to be capable of operating or assist- ing with the operation of the exit. Such seats will not be pre-assigned and check-in agents must physi- cally ascertain the suitability of the passengers before allocating these seats. Emergency exit row seats shall not be allocated to the following category of passengers:
1. Children and infants ( accompanied/unaccompanied )
2. Incapacitated Passengers (including blind and deaf)/Passengers with disabilities (MEDA and non-MEDA/Passengers with intellectual disabilities), Pregnant Passengers
3. Passengers who are elderly and frail (crew to use their best judgment)
4. Disruptive passengers, INAD, Deportees or prisoners in custody

chunks.heading: 2.25.1 Emergency Exit Row Seating
chunks.text: 5. Obese passengers, Passengers with plaster casts

chunks.heading: 2.25.2 Briefing Pax seated at the emergency exits
chunks.text:
The Passengers occupying seats adjacent to the emergency exits shall be briefed as stated below:
• CCM shall introduce self to pax
• State that the passengers are seated next to an emergency exit (point to the exit)
• Inquire the willingness to help in an emergency
• Act on command of CCM
• Inform pax to refer the safety card for door operation (show safety card)
• Check for any clarifications

chunks.heading: 2.25.3 Unserviceable Passenger Seat
chunks.text: If a seat is identified as unserviceable prior to take off, PIC shall be informed and immediate action shall be taken to rectify the defect. In the event a passenger seat remains unserviceable, an alternate seat with all safety features should be provided. A defective seat shall not be occupied.

chunks.heading: 2.25.4 Seat belts
chunks.text: The seat belts should be used as a restraint at all times when seated and when the fasten seat belt sign is switched on. Passengers shall be briefed of the usage of the seat belts prior to departure. Ref: 3.5.1

chunks.heading: 2.25.4.1 Extension Seat Belts
chunks.text: The extension seat belt is a standard seat belt but with extra length to restrain expectant mothers or obese passengers.

chunks.heading: 2.25.4.2 Kangaroo belt
chunks.text: It shall be used with the purpose of securing an infant under the age of 02 years who are lap carried by an adult.

chunks.heading: 2.25.4.3 Infant/Child Restraint System
chunks.text:
The maximum number of infants on any type of aircraft are limited by the number of infant life vests and the kangaroo belts available on board the aircraft which is limited as follows: A330 Aircraft 20 infants A321 Aircraft 16 infants A320 Aircraft 14 infants (MRE 10 infants) If extra infants are to be transported, sufficient infant life vests and kangaroo belts shall be up-lifted from base. 7 days - 6 months Kangaroo belt (accompanied and lap carried by an adult) 6 months - 2 years Kangaroo belt/Car seat (accompanied by an adult) 2 years - 5 years Seat belt (accompanied by an adult)
1. If one adult is traveling with two infants, One infant must be seated on the adult’s lap and secured with an approved infant seat belt (kangaroo belt), The second infant shall be above 6 months old, secured in an approved child car seat installed on an adjacent passenger seat (Reve- nue Seat)
2. The passenger with the infant shall be seated in compliance with additional drop-down oxygen

chunks.heading: 2.25.4.3 Infant/Child Restraint System
chunks.text:
mask and shall be informed regarding the use. No two (2) infants should occupy the same seat row, due to oxygen mask limitation unless there are sufficient oxygen masks available (example: Bassinet point seats). There must be an additional oxygen mask in each PSU for infant in the event of a decompression.
3. A mother with a gestational period (pregnant) up to 16 weeks (4 Months) may lap carry an infant. It is mandatory that each infant is accompanied by an able-bodied adult over 18 years of age

chunks.heading: 2.25.5 Briefing for Adults carrying Infants
chunks.text: CCMs shall carry out a safety briefing to the passenger with the infant as follows,

chunks.heading: 2.25.5.1 S.L.O.B. - Briefing
chunks.text: Seatbelt Instruct the adult to secure the infant with a Kangaroo belt for take-off, landing and whenever the seat belt sign is switched on during flight Life Vest The availability of infant life vests, floatation cots, and the distribution in the event of a ditching Oxygen If decompression occurs, to don the oxygen mask first and place a spare mask on the infant Bracing Bracing with an infant or the infant may remain in a car seat for Impact.

chunks.heading: 2.26 Car Seat
chunks.text: An approved child car seat may be fitted to an aircraft seat and the manufacturer’s instructions/weight restrictions shall be followed. All safety and installation instructions shall be followed by the responsible adult accompanying the infant/child. The child car seat shall be marked with an associated qualification sign, which shows the name of the qualification organisation and a specific identification number and/ or a label which states it is acceptable for use on an aircraft. The child car seat shall be secured to the assigned seat (Revenue seat) by the aircraft seat belt. The seat shall preferably be a window seat or a seat that does not obstruct a passenger’s direct access to an exit. The seat shall not be secured in an aisle seat or a cross-aisle seat that forms part of the evacuation route to exits. No part of the child car seat shall obstruct passenger movement, and the lower part of

chunks.heading: 2.26 Car Seat
chunks.text: the shell (under structure) should not prominently extend beyond the passenger seat. The child car seat shall not be secured in any rows leading to an emergency exit nor in a row immediately forward or aft of an emergency exit, where it may hinder evacuation for any passenger. The child car seat should be secured so as the nearest exit for evacuation is a floor level exit. A forward-facing child car seat shall only be fitted in the same direction as the passenger seat on which they are secured. Rear-facing child car seats shall only be installed on forward-facing passenger seats. If a forward-facing child car seat with a rigid backrest is to be secured, it should be done with the passen- ger seat in the reclined position, then positioned upright once the child car seat has been secured. This would ensure better tightening of the child car seat onto the passenger seat. The child car seat shall not

chunks.heading: 2.26 Car Seat
chunks.text: be installed on a seat that is equipped with an airbag unless it is obvious that the airbag is de-activated. The child car seat shall be secured to the passenger seat for the entire duration of the flight, even if not occupied by an infant or stored away when not in use. If stored away, the adult shall be provided with a kangaroo belt to secure the infant when the seat belt sign is switched on. More than one child car seat per seat row is allowed, provided the responsible adult for each infant occupies the adjacent seat. The child car seat shall not obstruct access of neighbour passengers to the nearest aisle. If the child car seat could be reclined, it shall be re-adjusted upright, and tables used with the child car seat shall be removed when the seat belt sign is switched on and in preparation for an emergency. The infant shall be secured using only the child car seat restraining device and always restrained when

chunks.heading: 2.26 Car Seat
chunks.text: in the child car seat. The passenger seat belt shall not be used over the child car seat to secure the infant at any time. The infant shall be secured in the child car seat for taxi, take off, landing and any time the seat belt sign is switched on. During an evacuation, only the infant shall be removed and evacuated without the child car seat.

chunks.heading: 2.26.1 Aviation Approved Car Seat
chunks.text: Devices meeting the following requirements are acceptable on board. Ref GD 006/Doc 10049 Australian/New Zealand Standards - AS/NZS 1754. USA Standards - FMVSS213 European Standards - ECE-R44 Figure 02 FWD facing car seat Figure 03 - AFT facing car seat Figure 01. Example of labeling requirements This child restraint system meets the standards for use in aircraft as recommended by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority of Australia and the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand. Only to be used on aircraft with the permission of the aircraft operator, pilot and crew.

chunks.heading: SUITABLE FOR FORWARD OR REAR-FACING USE
chunks.text: The top tether strap is not required to be used on board aircraft and should be stowed securely.

chunks.heading: CONFORMS TO ALL APPLICABLE FEDERAL
chunks.text: MOTOR VEHICLE SAFETY STANDARDS.

chunks.heading: CERTIFIED FOR USE IN MOTOR VEHICLES
chunks.text: AND AIRCRAFT.

chunks.heading: 2.26.1.1 Briefing on usage of Bassinet
chunks.text:
CCMs should be responsible to use their best judgment when offering bassinets.
1. Check the function of bassinet points on the bulk head (Pre Flight Checks)
2. Fix bassinet/s and ensure it is secured prior to placing the infant
3. Do not provide a bassinet for infants who could sit up un-assisted
4. The maximum weight of an infant shall not exceed the specified limit if stated on the bassinet
5. Bassinet shall not be fixed, prior to take-off/landing or during transit The guidelines for the adult briefing;
1. The infant to be removed from the bassinet when the fasten seat belt sign is switched on
2. Bassinets shall be removed, for take-off/ landing and for an emergency preparation
3. Pillows and covers shall be placed below shoulder level
4. To constantly check on the infant
5. Not to leave the infant unattendant at any time
6. If assistance is required to use the call bell
7. The infant to be restrained by the bassinet restraints (Flaps) all times

chunks.heading: 2.27 Carry-On Baggage
chunks.text: A crew member/passenger may carry a maximum of 7 kg as carryon baggage. Hand baggage brought into the cabin shall be stowed securely.

chunks.heading: 2.27.1 Acceptance and Stowage
chunks.text:
Carryon baggage should be stowed under the seat or in an overhead bin. The use of the stowage space under the seat shall be only if the seat is equipped with a restraint bar and the baggage is secure. The weight restriction on stowage bins shall be adhered to. The stowage bins should have functioning hinges and slam locks. Mobility aids shall be stowed in overhead bins or coat closets with lockable doors. Restrictions Carryon baggage shall not be stowed,
1. In lavatories
2. Behind the last row of seats
3. On the aisle or adjacent to exits
4. On top of emergency equipment
5. In the 1 st row against the bulkhead in each cabin
6. Strapped onto empty seats unless approved

chunks.heading: 2.27.2 Excess Baggage
