chunks.text: Excess/Extra/Large baggage that does not fit in to the designated stowages shall be removed from the cabin and referred to the ground staff for loading in the cargo hold.

chunks.heading: 2.28 Cargo in Passenger Seat/Cabin
chunks.text:
‘Cabin Seat Baggage’ on passenger seats which is also known as Bulky Baggage on passenger seats, which is not usually suitable for loading in the aircraft hold due to its nature and or specifications. Such baggage may include:
1. Musical instruments
2. Works of art
3. Electronic equipment
4. Diplomatic baggage
5. Valuable baggage If such baggage is not accepted in the cabin on a seat due to certain restrictions and/or limitations, it can travel as hold checked baggage provided packaging is appropriate. As per SriLankan Airlines policy, only a maximum weight of 75 kgs can be carried as ‘cabin seat baggage’. There is no change to the passenger’s FBA (Free Baggage Allowance) as a result of cabin seat baggage. In other words, the FBA shall not be used to account for cabin seat baggage in excess of 75 kgs. Ensure a window seat(away from the Emergency Exits) is blocked unless specified. Booking has to be made prior.

chunks.heading: 2.28.1 Loading and Securing Cabin Seat Baggage
chunks.text:
CCMs shall ensure that the ‘cabin seat baggage’ i.e. , bulky, oversized, fragile or valuable baggage on a cabin seat is;
1. Properly secured by a passenger seat belt/and or a Kangaroo belt having enough strength to eliminate the possibility of shifting under all normal anticipated flight and ground conditions.
2. The Item should be packed or covered in a manner to avoid possible injury to passengers and cabin crew members.(If not it can be denied acceptance)
3. Ensure load limitation of the seat is maintained. (75 kgs.)
4. Does not restrict access to use of any emergency or regular exit, or aisle(s).
5. Does not obstruct any passenger’s view of the seat belt sign, no-smoking sign or required exit signs. Cabin crew shall not be responsible for any damages to the item and or musical instrument during flight.

chunks.heading: 2.29.1 Domestic Pets
chunks.text: Carriage of pets in the passenger cabin shall not be permitted. Unless special approval is obtained from

chunks.heading: 2.29.2 Service Animal
chunks.text:
Service Animal can only accompany passenger whose vision or hearing is impaired and the passenger is actually dependant on the Service Animal
1. Such a service Animal is permitted in the Business Class or Economy Class cabin
2. The Service Animal is not allowed to move in the cabin and is expected to be seated near the passenger
3. Service Animal must be well behaved, clean and odourless
4. A suitable restraint harness shall be provided by the owner to secure and restrain the Service Animal during taxi, take off, landing turbulence or whenever the “Fasten seat belt” sign is illumi- nated. In cruise, it is acceptable for the Service Animal to be less restrained
5. The passenger shall be allocated a bulkhead window seat Note - Advise passenger how to evacuate Service Animal by holding the it and sliding. Designated Seat numbers for passengers escorted with Service Animals, Aircraft Type Business Class Economy Class

chunks.heading: 2.29.2 Service Animal
chunks.text: A 320 1A or 1F 5/6A or 5/6F A 321 1A or 1F 6A or 6F A 330 1A or 1K 20A or 20K

chunks.heading: 2.29.3 Administrative guidelines/restrictions and conditions
chunks.text:
1. Only one service animal per aircraft shall be permitted.
2. If a service animal is confirmed to travel at a bassinet row window seat, allocating a bassinet shall not be permitted.
3. Passengers having onward connections should obtain the onward airline confirmation for their onward travel.
4. The Service Animal, however, cannot be seated where it may obstruct aisle or affect leg space of the passenger seated adjoining. if the Service Animal cannot be accommodated at the seat location along with the passenger due to Service Animal is disruptive or too large to fit at the passenger’s feet without encroaching on another passenger’s space or protruding into the aisle, It will need to travel in a kennel (provided by the passenger) in the cargo hold

chunks.heading: 2.29.3 Administrative guidelines/restrictions and conditions
chunks.text:
5. Srilankan Airlines cannot accommodate a service animal in the cargo hold when it is a narrow body operation
6. There is no charge for Service Animals used by passengers with disabilities.
7. The passenger must ensure that the accompanying Service Animal will not need to relieve itself during the flight or that he can adequately manage the dog’s waste without creating any health and sanitation issues on the flight. The passenger must bring whatever absorbent or other mate- rial required for this purpose. The passenger shall ensure the Service Animal is prepared for the flight by exercising and limiting its fluid intake before the flight.
8. The Service Service Animal needs to be properly harnessed, and the leash of the Service Animal must be secured to the owner’s seatbelt at all times during flight.
9. SriLankan Airlines will not be responsible for the health and well-being of the Service Animal

chunks.heading: 2.29.3 Administrative guidelines/restrictions and conditions
chunks.text: whilst accompanying the passenger in the cabin.

chunks.heading: 2.30 Carriage/Restrictions on Portable Electronic Devices (PED)
chunks.text: Use of PEDs on board are restricted as they could affect the aircraft navigation and two way communi- cation systems. PEDs may be used on flight mode during flight. Mobile phones for two way communica- tion are permitted once the aircraft has landed and taxied out of the active runway on completion of a sector. An announcement shall be carried out advising passengers on the regulations. On aircrafts with satellite two way communication facilities for passengers, the use of PEDs shall be restricted during the critical phases of the flight. CCMs shall monitor for passenger compliance.

chunks.heading: 2.30.1 Devices Permitted without restrictions
chunks.text: Medical prescribed instruments such as hearing aids/ pacemakers. Cameras/calculators.

chunks.heading: 2.30.2 Devices Permitted During Cruise
chunks.text: Personal Electronic Devices,

chunks.heading: 2.30.3 Devices Not Permitted at Anytime
chunks.text: Devices transmitting and/or receiving signals other than stated above e.g. Portable radios, Televisions

chunks.heading: 2.30.4 Interference to Aircraft Navigation Systems
chunks.text: If abnormal interference to two way communication and navigation equipment is detected or suspect- ed, the Flight Crew shall alert the Cabin crew who shall check for compliance. If any abnormal occur- rence takes place, it should be recorded in the Cabin Defects Log book with the passenger seat number and the type of device used.

chunks.heading: 2.30.5 Use of Devices on Open Ramps during Boarding/Disembarking
chunks.text: Certain airport regulations may restrict the use of PEDs while boarding/ disembarking or during transit. A PA announcement shall be initiated informing the passengers of such regulations. “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, IN KEEPING WITH THE AIRPORT REGULATIONS, WE REQUEST PASSENGERS TO SWITCH OFF MOBILE PHONES AND ALL OTHER ELECTRONIC DEVICES WHILST THE AIRCRAFT IS ON GROUND. THANK YOU”. The use of PEDs while re fuelling shall not be permitted and the appropriate announcement shall be carried out.

chunks.heading: 2.31 Cabin Crew Seat
chunks.text: Seats for the minimum required CCMs shall be located near required floor level emergency exits. Such seats shall be forward-or rearward-facing. Each CCM assigned emergency evacuation duties shall occu- py a designated seat for take-off, landing and whenever the PIC so directs.

chunks.heading: 2.31.1 Seat Belt/Seat Harness
chunks.text: The seat belt and the shoulder harness on a CCM seat are equipped with a single point release mech- anism. During pre-flight checks, CCMs shall ensure the release mechanism is functioning and the re- straining belts are not damaged. The seat pan shall have a spring loaded function to restore it back to stowed position. The harness should be adjusted to sit tight but does not pull the lap strap upward. The webbing of the seat belt and shoulder harness shall lie flat against the body and the single point release buckle facing outwards for quick release. The device, will automatically restrain the occupant’s torso in the event of sudden movement, (Jerk). Under certain circumstances additional CCM’s (above the required minimum number) may sit at passenger seats (with lap belts only).

chunks.heading: 2.31.3 When should a Crew member Occupy a Seat
chunks.text: CCMs shall be seated and secured with the seat belt and shoulder harness, only at their assigned cabin crew seats, during take-off/landing and when ever deemed necessary by the PIC in the interest of safety

chunks.heading: 2.31.4 Requirements to Occupy Assigned Seats/Stations
chunks.text: The minimum number of CCM required for each type of aircraft is based on the seating capacity/num- ber of passengers carried, or the number of exits in order to effectively carry out a safe evacuation of passengers from the aircraft.

chunks.heading: 2.31.5 Persons Authorised To Occupy Crew Seats
chunks.text: The PIC may permit a non-revenue passenger to occupy a door assist CCM seat. Ref 2.12.5

chunks.heading: 2.31.6 Primary Cabin Crew member Seating
chunks.text: A CCM on a familiarization flight shall not occupy a Primary/Assist cabin crew seat.

chunks.heading: 2.31.7 Unserviceable CCM Seat
chunks.text:
A CCM seat is considered unserviceable if the seat belt/shoulder harness the stowing of the seat pan is not functioning. If the seat is unserviceable, the Purser shall be guided by the following,
1. Allocate a cabin seat at an exit row closest to the CCMs allocated exit
2. Inform the PIC and all CCMs of the alternate seat allocation
3. The passenger seat should be designated and marked as a crew seat

chunks.heading: 2.31.7 Unserviceable CCM Seat
chunks.text: 4. The defective crew seat shall be stowed, secured or removed

chunks.heading: 2.32 Dispatch of an Air Craft with an In-Operative Door
chunks.text:
The aircraft may be dispatched with one door inoperative as required by the MEL. CCMs shall communicate to the Purser when a door is observed inoperative. The Purser shall inform the PIC at the earliest for two way communication and rectification by the Engineers. Dispatching an aircraft with a door inoperative shall be under the following conditions,
1. All other doors are operational.
2. Exit light/floor path lighting associated with the inoperative exit is covered and marked “NO EXIT” by approved placards prior to passenger boarding.
3. The affected door is not used for passenger boarding/disembarking and is not used for any oth- er purpose whilst passengers are on board.
4. Passengers in the location are advised regarding the defective door.
5. Manual safety demonstration carried out, not pointing to the defective door as an exit.
6. All Cabin crew shall be aware that evacuation procedure shall not include the affected door. (The

chunks.heading: 2.32 Dispatch of an Air Craft with an In-Operative Door
chunks.text:
opposite door may be used).
7. In an evacuation, a CCM shall remain at the defective door to redirect the passengers to usable exits.
8. The aircraft may continue the flight or a series of flights but shall not depart an airport where repairs or replacements can be carried out. 2.32.1 The specific seats to be blocked shall be as specified in the MEL. Ref: A330 aircraft 5.24, A320 aircraft 6.39, A321 aircraft 6A.23 and 6A.46

chunks.heading: 2.32.1.1 Blocking identified seats
chunks.text: Identified seats in the vicinity of the inoperative door should be placard as ‘Do Not Occupy’ and the CCMs shall ensure that these seats remain vacant for taxi, take-off and landing.

chunks.heading: 2.32.1.2 No Exit Cards
chunks.text: 04 NO EXIT cards are provided to be used in case of an in-operative door. Relevant EXIT signs should be covered and NO EXIT stickers shall be placed on the inoperative door and other pathways to the exit.

chunks.heading: 2.33 Unserviceable Equipment
chunks.text:
Purser shall check the cabin defects log book prior to passenger boarding and coordinate with the main- tenance personnel to rectify any unattended defects.
1. Purser shall brief CCMs to identify defects/ shortcomings as per the MEL and inform same at their earliest to report it in the cabin defects log book for rectification prior to departure.
2. Inform the CCMs of any pending defects as per the cabin defects logbook.

chunks.heading: 2.33 Unserviceable Equipment
chunks.text:
CCMs shall carry out the following serviceability checks on the equipment but not limited to:
1. Heaters - (Coffee makers/Ovens/Hot Cups/Water Boilers)
2. Chillers – Bins/drawers and units
3. Vacuum Systems - In lavatories
4. Electrical System - Circuit breakers
5. Water shut off valves - In lavatories and galleys
6. Locks and Latches - In galleys
7. Containers with lockable doors
8. Carts with lockable doors
9. Carts with functioning locking/braking and releasing mechanisms
10. Waste carts/containers with spring loaded flaps or other covers

chunks.heading: 2.33.1 Procedure for Unserviceable Equipment
chunks.text:
An unserviceable sticker (U/S) shall be pasted on all unserviceable equipment, which have been en- tered in the cabin defects logbook and on the VR. In the event equipment is identified to be unserviceable, CCMs shall be guided by the following,
1. Ex base - Containers not fitting in to the slot/ trolley and cart not locking / equipment not latch- ing shall be offloaded.
2. Ex other stations - The defective equipment could remain on board provided such equipment could be safely secured and remain in the galley.
3. During flight - The equipment shall remain secured in the galley Galley restraining devices(locks/latches) Do not use the stowage space Containers with lockable doors Off load container Carts with lockable doors Off load cart Carts with brake/release mechanism Off load cart Circuit breaker popped out Do not reset/ do not use Waste carts/ containers without flaps/covers Off load cart

chunks.heading: 2.33.1.1 Unserviceable Aircraft Waste Carts and Fixed Waste Bins
chunks.text:
Ex-Base (CMB), CCMs in charge of galleys shall check the waste cart and fixed waste bins for the following before depar- ture and confirm with the cabin supervisor in charge,
1. Waste cart locking devices (Breaks) are serviceable and the waste bin flap is not bent or dam- aged and seals the waste cart opening securely. If not inform the Purser/cabin supervisor and

chunks.heading: 2.33.1.1 Unserviceable Aircraft Waste Carts and Fixed Waste Bins
chunks.text:
the cart shall be replaced.
2. Fixed waste bin in the galleys - The waste bin flap is not damaged or bent and seals the waste container in the closed position. This shall ensure if a waste bin fire occurs it shall cut-off the supply of oxygen. During Flight,
1. CCMs shall ensure the waste collected is managed and distributed evenly into the waste carts & waste bins. When available, use the trash compactor/s initially to dispose waste.
2. If the waste cart/bin flap is found damaged and cannot be secured the waste cart /bin shall not be used to dispose waste.
3. In case of a defective waste bin flap, which is bent or damaged and cannot be secured properly, it shall be entered in the cabin defects logbook before landing and the Purser shall enter same in the voyage report for follow-up action. Before /After landing, Cabin Supervisor/s shall ensure all waste carts are not over-filled and the waste bin flaps are closed and

chunks.heading: 2.33.2 Primary And Secondary Locking devices
chunks.text: All carts and trolleys utilised for passenger services on board shall be equipped with primary locking de- vices and shall be checked by CCMs in charge prior to departure. Carts and trolleys with unserviceable locking devices shall be off loaded or used as per Ref 2.33.1 Carts and trolleys shall be secured by using the primary and secondary locking devices available in galleys during taxi, take-off, landing, turbulent weather, and all other emergencies as declared by the Flight crew. If a primary or secondary locking device is unserviceable, such position shall not be used to stow carts and trolleys. All carts and trolleys shall be attended by cabin crew at all times when in use, when stationary the braking device must be engaged and attended. Carts and trolleys must be properly stowed when not in use.

chunks.heading: 2.33.2.1 Securing and Locking
chunks.text: CCM designated and the area supervisors shall ensure, prior to push back/landing and during turbu- lence all moveable equipment are stowed/secured/ latched and locked. All loose service equipment shall be securely stowed /locked when in the cabin or in the galley.

chunks.heading: 2.34.1 Description of Surface Contamination
chunks.text: Ice formation on ground may be expected when air temperature drops below freezing (0 ºC /32 ºF) and when moisture or ice forms due to condensation. The aircraft is vulnerable to ice build-up when ex- posed to any form of moisture after the surfaces have been cold soaked during the previous cruise and when fuelled with cold fuel or after an overnight parking at low temperatures. Critical surfaces of the aircraft (wings, vertical & horizontal stabilisers, control surfaces slats, flaps, and ailerons) must be clear of snow, frost and ice before take-off. Thin hoarfrost is acceptable on the surface of the fuselage but not on the primary control’s surfaces. CCMs Responsibility and Duties CCMs shall be always vigilant for any type of ice (hoarfrost) and shall report to the PIC immediately. CCM shall convey to the PIC any concerns raised by a passenger relating to an observation made on ice contamination. Observation by a CCM or a passenger regarding contamination or any other concerns

chunks.heading: 2.34.1 Description of Surface Contamination
chunks.text: shall be reported to the PIC immediately prior to the take-off roll. De Icing/Anti Icing When the aircraft is on ground in sub-zero conditions and ice accumulates on the wings or primary control surfaces, it has to be de-iced by spraying de-icing liquid. This prevents ice formation for a con- siderable period. During taxiing in icing conditions, the anti-icing system would be switched on by the flight crew to pre- vent further ice formation.

chunks.heading: 2.34.1 Description of Surface Contamination
chunks.text: Emergency during de icing In the event of an evacuation during de-icing, crew shall be mindful of checking on outside conditions, to be clear of obstructions prior to deploying the slides.

chunks.heading: 3.0.1 Introduction
chunks.text: Safety equipment carried on Sri Lankan airlines aircraft shall conform to the Air-Navigation Regulations of Sri Lanka and as a requirement by SLCAIS 15. This chapter describes all general items of portable safety equipment provided for use on Sri Lankan airlines aircraft. The pre-flight check of safety equip- ment is a mandatory duty of every CCM. If there is any discrepancy, CCMs shall inform the Purser who will notify the PIC and Ground Engineer/Maintenance staff and/or carry out an entry in the Cabin Defects Log book. Specific information shall be entered in the Cabin Defects log book for the Engineer to confirm the airworthiness of the aircraft. The Purser shall ensure the replacements are (if required) received prior to departure CCMs shall use the Quick Reference Card (QRC) for guidance for checking of safety equipment in the relevant area

chunks.heading: 3.0.2 Pre-Flight Checks/Serviceability checks
chunks.text:
CCMs shall carry out a pre-flight serviceability check and confirm by signing the Voyage Report when:
1. Boarding an aircraft for duty,
2. In the event of a crew change,
3. An aircraft has been left unattended,
4. On completion of maintenance work carried out in the cabin. When carrying out the above checks, CCMs shall ensure, Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/ clear of obstruction. Pre-Flight Checks/Serviceability checks shall be carried out on, but not limited to,
1. All safety equipment
2. Demonstration equipment
3. Passenger seats/ belts/life vest
4. Crew seat-belt and harness/life vest
5. PA/Interphone system
6. Lavatories-smoke detectors/ waste bin door and the flap/extinguishers/ call lights
7. Safety cards (relevant to the operating aircraft)/ passenger information leaflet
8. Emergency exit signs/doors
9. All restraining devices- locking and latching

chunks.heading: 3.1.1 Halon - KIDDE
chunks.text:
Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/ correct num- ber/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. Needle on the pressure gauge is in the green zone
3. Safety pin is placed through the handle and lever/not bent or damaged
4. Seal intact Precautions - Do not tilt more than 45° (this will stop the flow)/do not dis- charge at a person Operation - Break the seal/pull the safety pin/hold the extinguisher up- right and aim the nozzle at the base of the fire/squeeze both levers together. Limitations - Used on all types of fires/ the effective range is 10 ft. and the duration is 9 seconds.

chunks.heading: 3.1.2 Halon - Maip
chunks.text: Refer 3.1.1

chunks.heading: 3.1.3 Halon - Airtotal
chunks.text:
Pre-flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. Needle on the pressure gauge is in the green zone
3. Safety catch is in the lock position (up position)
4. Seal is intact Precautions - Do not tilt more than 45° (this will stop the flow)/do not discharge at a person. Operation - Break the seal/push the safety catch down/hold extinguisher upright and aim the nozzle at the base of the fire/squeeze both levers together. Limitations - Used on all types of fires/effective range is 10 ft. and the duration is 9 seconds.

chunks.heading: 3.1.4 BCF
chunks.text:
Colour of Extinguishers – Red or Green Pre Flight Check/Serviceability checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. RED Disk marked ‘FULL’ intact
3. Needle on the pressure gauge at the bottom of the extinguisher is in the green zone.(On certain extinguishers only) Precaution - Do not tilt more than 45° (this will stop the flow) do not discharge at a person. Operation - Flip the red safety catch up/hold the extinguisher upright and aim the nozzle at the base of the fire/squeeze the palm lever. As BCF is heavier than air, it is capable of seeping and penetrating through small openings and cracks. Limitations - Used on all types of fires/effective range is 10 ft. and the duration is 9 seconds.

chunks.heading: 3.1.5 Halotron (Halon Free extinguisher)
chunks.text:
Is a proven clean fire extinguishing agent designed for streaming applications in portable and handheld fire extinguishers. It is the world’s most widely distributed halocarbon-based clean fire extinguishing agent for such applications. Gross weight 2.3 kg with the bracket. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
1. Needle on the pressure gauge is in the green zone
2. Safety pin is placed through the handle and lever/not bent or damaged
3. Seal/Collar intact Precautions - Do not tilt more than 45° (this will stop the flow)/do not discharge at a person. Operation - pull the safety pin to release the seal/hold the extinguisher upright and aim the nozzle at the base of the fire/squeeze both levers together. Limitations - Used on all types of fires/the effective range is 10 ft and the duration is 9 seconds.

chunks.heading: 3.1.6 Waste Bin Fire Extinguisher
chunks.text:
Description - An automatic fire extinguisher containing 120 grams of Halon/Freon gas is in- stalled in the compartment below the sink /ad- jacent to the waste bin When exposed to heat in excess of approximately 77° C, the Halon/Fre- on gas is discharged within 60 seconds through a single nozzle into the waste bin below Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Clear of obstructions.
2. The needle of the pressure gauge is in the green zone

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.1 PBE (Oxy crew)
chunks.text: Description - Each CCMs seat location shall be provided with a PBE. A chemical reaction generates oxygen and the process releases heat. While supplying oxygen, it’s capable of protecting the fire fighter from the fire and heat. If inhalation resistance increases, it may be depleted source of oxygen or defective equipment. Breath- ing will still be possible for a short while. The mask is equipped with a speech diaphragm and a body belt.

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.1 PBE (Oxy crew)
chunks.text:
Revision No 02 Revision Date 15 August 2024 Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. White security seal on the locking clamp is intact
3. Yellow serviceability sticker on the foil bag is not broken (visible through the viewing window)
4. Box is not damaged
5. Foil bag is not pressed against the viewing window Precautions Remove all makeup Remove sharp objects-(Chains and earrings) Neck seal should be air tight (Long hair pushed into the hood/ neck seal not damaged) Ensure oxygen is flowing before tying the body belt. Note: Do not smoke or expose self to fire or flames after removing the PBE as hair may be saturated with oxygen Operation Open the container by pushing up the locking clamp Remove the foil bag, tear open by using the red tear strip Take the smoke hood out Insert both hands through the neck seal into the hood and widen using the back of your hands and Pull

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.1 PBE (Oxy crew)
chunks.text:
the hood over the head from back to forward (do not remove the hands until the neck seal is secure), Adjust the inner mask to fit over the nose and mouth Pull the activation tab in front to activate the generator and take 4-5 deep breaths to ensure oxygen is flowing Fasten the body belt around the waist and tie a knot on to a side, breathe normally If resistance in breathing is experienced remove the PBE immediately and inform Purser of the location of PBE After Use
1. Release the body belt
2. Seize the top of the hood and pull it off the head

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.1 PBE (Oxy crew)
chunks.text: 3. Place/store in safe area away from heat as the chemical reaction heats up the generator Limitations – Provides oxygen for approximately for 15 Minutes Note: If the inner mask does not fit the nose and mouth, CO2 exhaled will be inhaled again causing dizziness to the user.

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.2 Air Liquide
chunks.text:
Description- It protects the head and supplies gaseous oxygen stowed in a cylinder at the neck seal The visor is trea ted with an anti-fogging compound. The internal hood is manufactured with self-extinguish- ing material. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. Security seal is intact
3. The green condition indicator disc is visible Precautions
1. Remove all makeup
2. Remove sharp objects-(Chains and earrings)
3. Neck seal should be air tight (Long hair pushed into the hood/ neck seal not damaged)
4. Ensure oxygen is flowing by breathing comfortably, if not replace with another Operation
1. Hold the box handle in one hand and with the other hand firmly pull the grey part of the lid marked “PULL”: the stick breaks, the lid opens. Hold the vacuum-packed hood in one hand hold in position by the two yellow squares then take it out of the packing box by pulling it towards

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.2 Air Liquide
chunks.text:
you
2. Or Hold the case in one hand and with the other lift the part of the green security latch marked “SEAL” to break it, Push sharply on the part of the cover marked “PUSH” to open the cover. Hold the vacuum-packed hood in one hand (held in position by the two yellow clips) and take it out of he packing box by pulling it
3. Remove the foil bag and pull on the red tear tab, the cover tears easily. Take out the hood pulling on the compressed oxygen container (do not insert the hand in the packaging to pull the

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.2 Air Liquide
chunks.text:
hood by the fabric or the sealing collar. this can damage the oxygen activation system and affect its operation)
4. With the orange marks visible and towards you, place your hands on the orange marks and using your thumbs, open the black neck seal at the base of the hood, Don the hood from rear to front and ensure the neck seal is not damaged (you must only grab the black neck seal and not internal components or the white fabric, if you grab the white fabric or the internal compo- nents, you can damage the activation of the oxygen system)
5. Holding the oxygen container tightly with both hands with the black neck seal open, flick the hood down in a sharp movement to deploy it
6. Put the hood over your head, from back to front. After donning the hood, you will hear a slight click caused by the activation of the oxygen system. You will then hear a noise caused by the oxygen flow in the PBE.

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.2 Air Liquide
chunks.text:
After Use
1. To remove the mask - Insert both thumbs into the neck seal at the front of the hood and remove the hood backwards
2. Store in a dry, fire protected area, away from heat.
3. Inform Purser of the location after use. Limitation - Oxygen supply will last for approximately 15 Minutes WARNING: WHEN DONNING THE PBE OR DURING ITS FIRST SECONDS OF USE, IF YOU DO NOT HEAR THE NOISE PRODUCED BY THE OXYGEN FLOW, OR EXPERIENCE BREATHING RESISTANCE, YOU MUST IMMEDIATELY REMOVE THE PBE AND EQUIP WITH ANOTHER PBE. Note: Do not smoke or expose self to fire or flames after removing the PBE as hair may be saturated with oxygen

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.3 Scott Protective Breathing Equipment
chunks.text:
Description - The Scott PBE (Protective Breathing Equipment) is a portable, self-contained, personal smoke hood designed to safeguard cabin crewmembers from the effects of smoke, carbon dioxide, harmful gases and oxygen deficiency while managing in-flight fire, smoke or fume emergencies. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. Check if the humidity indicator is blue in colour (If pink the unit is unserviceable)
3. The box should not be damaged Operation
1. Remove the unit from the fixture and open the container after lifting the catch marked lift.
2. Open the container and remove the transparent bag
3. Tear open the transparent bag by using the red strip
4. Remove the PBE and unfold
5. Activate the oxygen flow by pulling the red pull tab on the life support pack in the direction indi-

chunks.heading: 3.1.7.3 Scott Protective Breathing Equipment
chunks.text:
cated (hissing sound indicates the flow of oxygen, if not do not use, replace with another unit)
6. Insert both hands in to the neck seal and enlarge ensuring the life support pack fits at the back of the head
7. Bend forward and don the PBE front to the back and ensure the neck seal is not damaged
8. Stay up-right and pull the mask down until the head band inside the hood fits firmly on the fore- head
9. Insert two finger in to the neck seal and check it is free of obstructions and pull the hood down fully to cover the neck seal completely Limitations The oxygen flow shall last for 15 Mins WARNING: IF BREATHING RESISTANCE IS EXPERIENCED, REMOVE THE HOOD IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT TOUCH THE LIFE SUPPORT PACK DUE TO HEATING WHEN IN USE Note: Do not smoke or expose self to fire or flames after removing the BPE as hair may be saturat- ed with oxygen.

chunks.heading: 3.1.8 Fire Protection Gloves
chunks.text:
Description/Use - Protective gloves are used to grasp hot or burning parts and smother minor fires. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number
2. Stowed in a sealed transparent cover
3. Not damaged or torn

chunks.heading: 3.1.9 Fire/Crash Axe
chunks.text: The Crash Axe is available in the flight deck and/or galley compartment. It is used in an emergency, es- pecially when fighting an onboard fire. Pre Flight-Checks Correct location/correct number /correctly secured/clear of obstructions Description/Use Cutting Edge – Used to open panels and cutting the fuselage or other obstructions during a fire or emergency. It is also used to enlarge an opening or to cut electrical wiring up to 24,000 volts. Pointed Edge – Used to start an opening on panels during a fire to insert the nozzle of the extinguisher. It is also used to disperse embers during a fire.

chunks.heading: 3.2.1 ELT ADT 406 AP
chunks.text:
Description - The ADT 406 AP is a bright coloured water sealed /compact/ buoyant/ manually activated transmitter, secured to a metal bracket with a Velcro strap. A wire harness is attached (optional) to the metal bracket. It’s equipped with a lanyard for attachment in a ditching. The toggle switch has ARM/OFF/ON positions. The beacon transmits distress signals on three frequencies simultaneously:
- 121.5 MHz (civil distress frequency)
- 243 MHz (military distress frequency)
- 406.025 MHz (COSPAS-SARSAT frequency).

chunks.heading: 3.2.1 ELT ADT 406 AP
chunks.text:
Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction.
2. The toggle switch is in the OFF position.
3. Testing of the ELT shall be carried out by the Engineering staff. Operation On Land
• Unfasten the Velcro straps to remove the ELT from its bracket.
• Pull firmly to break the wire harness(optional feature).
• Take it to a high elevation clear of obstructions, remove transparent cover and erect the flexible antenna manually and move the toggle switch to the “ON” position (lift and slide the switch). In Water -
• All of the above
• Tie it to the lifeline diagonally opposite the sea anchor using the lanyard
• Place the transmitter in water and ensure the transmitter floats away from the raft. Transmission begins with a visual and aural indicator
• To stop transmission, move the toggle switch to the OFF position. Limitations Civil/Military 60 hours

chunks.heading: 3.2.1 ELT ADT 406 AP
chunks.text: Satellite 24 hours

chunks.heading: 3.2.2 ELT Kannad 406 AS
chunks.text:
Description - KANNAD 406 AS is yellow in colour and the housing is made of aluminium alloy coated with paint. It is a compact buoyant transmitter and has to be activated manually. A toggle switch with three positions is located on top of the ELT. (ARM/ON/OFF) An antenna is fastened to the ELT. It’s equipped with a lanyard for attachment in a ditching. The beacon transmits distress signals on three frequencies simultaneously:
- 121.5 MHz (civil distress frequency)
- 243 MHz (military distress frequency)
- 406.025 MHz (COSPAS-SARSAT frequency). Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured and clear of obstruction
2. The toggle switch is in the “OFF” position
3. Testing of the ELT shall be carried out by the Engineering staff. Operation On Land -
• Unfasten the Velcro strap to remove the ELT from its bracket.
• Take it to an elevation clear of obstruction.

chunks.heading: 3.2.2 ELT Kannad 406 AS
chunks.text:
• Erect the antenna, move the toggle switch to the “ON” position. In Water -
• All of the above
• Tie it to the life line diagonally opposite the sea anchor using the lanyard
• Place the transmitter in water and ensure the transmitter floats away from the raft. Transmission begins with a visual and aural indicator as given below
• To stop transmission move the toggle switch to the “OFF” position. Limitations Civil/Military 48 hours - Satellite 24 hours -

chunks.heading: 3.2.3 ELT Rescue – 406S
chunks.text: Description - The Rescue 406 S is a portable Emergency Locator Transmitter which is powered by a water activated battery. A pouch of salt is provided to be dissolved to create an electrolyte solution for enhanced activation when used on land.

chunks.heading: 3.2.3 ELT Rescue – 406S
chunks.text: The beacon transmits distress signals on three frequencies simultaneously:

chunks.heading: 243 MHz (military distress frequency)
chunks.text:
406.025 MHz (COSPAS-SARSAT frequency). Pre-flight Check/Serviceability Check
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstructions
2. Stowed in a sealed transparent cover and the pouch of salt is available Precautions - Do not tilt the transmitter more than 60° as transmission may be suspended by draining the liquid out from the vent holes. Operation On land -
• Remove from quick release bracket and take it out of the aircraft to a higher elevation free of obstructions.
• Erect the antenna manually and unwind the lanyard to remove the plastic bag.
• Fill the plastic bag with a liquid up to the indicated line (do not use alcohol/oil).
• Empty the pouch of salt in to the liquid and immerse the transmitter until the liquid penetrates the vent openings

chunks.heading: 243 MHz (military distress frequency)
chunks.text:
In water -
• Unroll the free end of the cord at the top of the beacon
• tie the cord to the life line of the raft diagonally opposite to the sea anchor.
• place the transmitter in water and ensure the transmitter floats away from the raft. Transmission could be stopped by
• Draining the liquid from the transmitter/by holding it horizontally.
• By folding the antenna
• Immersing the transmitter under water. Limitations Civil/Military 48 hours Satellite 24 hours Note: It is recommended to operate one ELT at a time as direction trading on one transmitter pro- duces better results.

chunks.heading: 3.2.4 Heliograph (Signaling Mirror)
chunks.text: Description- Is a reflective plate which has a high capability of reflection and has an opening in the centre Operation- The mirror should be held a few inches away from the face against the sun and point a fin- ger towards the object. Look through the opening and direct the reflection on to the object. Precautions - Do not continue to flash the mirror at passing aircraft after response by performing the roll action.

chunks.heading: 3.2.5 Sea Dye marker
chunks.text: Description- It is a water-soluble luminous dye that is packed in a pouch with an attachment cord to be dropped into the water The trail is visible during the day and in the night when searchlights are used The sea dye marker is stowed in the survival pack of the slide raft. Operation - Tear open one pack/tie to the trailing edge of the lifeline and throw it over board. Same side of the sea anchor

chunks.heading: 3.2.5 Sea Dye marker
chunks.text: Limitations - The duration is approximately 30 to 40 minutes. If the dye is used in rough waters the trail may be displaced.

chunks.heading: 3.2.6 Whistle
chunks.text: Description/Use - It is brightly coloured and used to attract attention

chunks.heading: 3.2.7 Orion Sky blazer – Aerial Flare
chunks.text:
Description – It is a cylindrical plastic canister signalling device used to attract attention when Search and Rescue (SAR) are seen or heard. Operation –
• Hold the flare by the arrow facing upwards.
• Press the top centre down, the flare tube will drop.
• Pull the centre tube down until locked in position.
• Unscrew the bottom part to expose the metal chain.
• Hold upright and pull the metal chain firmly downwards.
• The flare fires a red torch which rises up and lasts for 10 seconds. Precautions - If the flare fails to ignite do not examine but cool by dipping in water and dispose.

chunks.heading: 3.2.8 Mini Flare
chunks.text:
Description - It is a water-resistant light weight signalling device. The pack stows eight flare stars and a penjector with a trigger mechanism. Operation -
• Open the flap on the pouch to expose the flare stars.
• Remove the penjector and engage a flare by inserting and turning clockwise.
• Pull the flare from the pouch.
• Hold at arm’s length at 45°.
• Pull the trigger and fire the flare into the sky.
• Dip the used flare in water to cool.
• Remove and dispose the used flare.
• Stow the penjector in the pouch for reuse Limitations - Each flare will burn for approximately 6 seconds at 3000 candlelight Precautions - If the flare fails to ignite do not examine but cool by dipping in water and dispose. Both types of flares can be used during day and night.

chunks.heading: 3.3 Emergency Torch
chunks.text: Type 1 Description - It is water resistant, equipped with a battery and a lanyard. A magnetic switch is activat- ed when the flashlight is removed from the bracket. There is no ON/OFF switch, and the light can be turned off by unscrewing and disconnecting the base. A torch shall be located within reach at every crew seat Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number /correctly secured/clear of obstruction Secured with a plastic security seal.

chunks.heading: 3.3 Emergency Torch
chunks.text: The red light flashing every 4 to 6 seconds. Operation - Pull the torch to break the plastic strap the light will illuminate automatically To Switch off place it back into the retention backet. To prolong usage, unscrew the bottom cover and disconnect the wire harness. Limitations- The battery power would last for 04 hours. Emergency Torch Type 2 (ALS Aircraft) Is a normal battery-operated device. Secure strap is not available Pre-Flight / Serviceable checks – Pull it from the bracket, Slide the switch to ON position and check illumination. Operation- Pull it from the bracket, Slide the switch to ON position

chunks.heading: 3.4 Power Megaphone
chunks.text: A megaphone is voice amplifying device. The purpose of the megaphone For crew to give instructions to passengers during an emergency or as emergency means of communi- cation inside the aircraft if the PA system fails. Type 1 Description - It is equipped with a microphone/press to talk switch. It is powered by self-contained batteries.

chunks.heading: 3.4 Power Megaphone
chunks.text: Pre Flight-Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number /correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Use the press to talk switch to check serviceability, a click sound will be heard. Type 2 Operation - Press to talk and speak into the microphone. Description - It is equipped with a microphone/squeeze handle / volume control / alarm pin and powered by self-contained batteries. Pre Flight-Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number /correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Squeeze the handle to check serviceability after increasing the volume, a click sound will be heard, and a flashing green light is visible. Operation: Squeeze the handle and speak into the microphone. Adjust volume accordingly. Precaution - Avoid dropping in water as this would short circuit the batteries.

chunks.heading: 3.5.1 Passenger Seat Belts
chunks.text:
Description- It is attached to the seat structure with an adjustable metal buckle on one side and a metal fitting on the other. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location /correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. Both ends of the seat belts are available and can be fastened Ref: 2.25.4 Operation - To open the seat belt lift the upper portion of the buckle. Precautions - Ensure straps are not twisted or damaged. Limitation - Only one passenger shall be secured by a seat belt. NOTE: On certain aircraft “Y” seat belts are available at bulkhead row seats with double attachment points to the seats.

chunks.heading: 3.5.2 Cabin Crewmember Seat Belt/Shoulder Harness
chunks.text: Description - The Cabin crew seats are equipped with a lap strap and a shoulder harness. The seat-belt and the self-locking shoulder harness have a single point release. The base of the self folding seat pan, a cavity is located to stow the lap strap. It is mandatory for CCMs to use the seat belt and shoulder har- ness during taxi/take-off/turbulence/ landing and when instructed by the PIC.

chunks.heading: 3.5.2 Cabin Crewmember Seat Belt/Shoulder Harness
chunks.text:
Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks
1. Serviceability of the locking device
2. Lap strap can be adjusted
3. The self-locking device on the shoulder harness is functioning
4. The straps are not twisted or damaged
5. The base of the seat pan is self-folding Operation - Place the lap straps first and insert the metal fitting of the shoulder harness and adjust. The seat belt can be opened from the single point release. The seat belt once removed must be stowed in the cavity at the back of the seat pan NOTE: On the A 330-300 aircraft the crew seat belts needs to be fastened when not in use. Precautions - Ensure straps are not twisted or damaged. The lap strap should be locked and adjusted and the buckle should be positioned under the abdomen and above the hips. Limitation - CCM shall occupy only a fully functional crew seat.

chunks.heading: 3.5.3 Infant Seat Belt (kangaroo-belt)
chunks.text: Description - It is equipped with a loop in the centre To secure lap carried infants. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Usage – Pass the passenger seat belt through the loop of the kangaroo belt Secure the infant seatbelt around the waist of the infant NOTE: For Seat belt equipped with an airbag, the loop on the kangaroo belt should be inserted on to the side that does not contain the airbag.

chunks.heading: 3.5.4 Extension Seat Belt
chunks.text: Description - A kangaroo belt may be used as an extension seat belt. Pre Flight Check/Serviceability Checks

chunks.heading: 3.5.4 Extension Seat Belt
chunks.text: Correct location/correct number/ correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Usage - It is used to restrain expectant mothers, obese passengers, cargo in passenger seats and when securing medical oxygen cylinders. NOTE: For seat belts equipped with airbags special extension seat belts are available

chunks.heading: 3.6 Portable Oxygen System
chunks.text: Single outlet Dual Outlet Single outlet with flow selector

chunks.heading: 3.6 Portable Oxygen System
chunks.text:
Description - Green coloured cylinders and contains 310 litres of oxygen. It is equipped with a pressure gauge/refill- ing valve/carry strap/ON/OFF rotator knob and a safety valve It has a flexible mask with an elastic strap and a re-breather bag connected to a tube. The re-breather bag has a green indicator, indicating inflation. Three types of 310 Litre oxygen bottles are available on board.
1. Single outlet.- Rate of Flow 4 Litres for 75 Minutes.
2. Dual outlets. - Rate of Flow 2 Litres for 150 mins/4 Litres for 75 Minutes.
3. Single outlet with a flow selector on top of the bottle. - Rate of Flow 2 Litres for 150 mins/4 Litres for 75 Minutes. Pre-Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/ correctly secured/clear of obstruction
2. All bottles shall be over 1500 PSI ex-base
3. Mask shall be fitted to the high outlet and in a pouch
4. Tubing is not damaged Operation

chunks.heading: 3.6 Portable Oxygen System
chunks.text:
1. Remove mask from plastic bag
2. Ensure mask and tubing is attached to the high outlet
3. Open valve by turning ON/OFF knob anti- clockwise
4. Check for the flow of oxygen by pinching mask end of the re-breather bag
5. Place mask over nose and mouth and adjust elastic band
6. Secure bottle on the safety bar using two kangaroo belts
7. Remove mask when the gauge reaches 500/250 PSI After Use
1. Close the valve by turning ON/OFF knob clockwise
2. Disconnect the tube from the bottle
3. Re-stow bottle of oxygen Precautions - After use, the tubing and mask shall be disconnected as a precautionary measure to stop the leakage of oxygen

chunks.heading: 3.6.1 Ex En-Route Station Minimums- 8 bottles
chunks.text:
• 6 bottles - at 1000 PSI
• 2 bottles - at 500 PSI Limitations - Bottles above the minimum requirement for dispatch may be used for first Aid to a mini- mum of 250 PSI. En-route if an aircraft is dispatched with the minimum requirement of bottles and oxygen is to be ad- ministered as first aid, the bottles with a 1000 PSI can be used up to 500 PSI. Administering of addition- al oxygen above this shall be at the discretion of the PIC

chunks.heading: 3.6.2 Procedure to secure a bottle of Oxygen during administration
chunks.text:
EY Seats
1. The bottle of Oxygen shall be secured as shown below with the two kangaroo belts on to the seat frame. (crew shall ensure the belts are tight around the bottle and the tubing is free from obstruction)
2. The standard procedure shall be followed to administer Oxygen.
3. Preferred location to secure the bottle of Oxygen, is an aisle seat.
4. The procedure may be applied during cruise and TTOL.
5. The procedure for securing shall be the same for stretcher passengers.

chunks.heading: 3.6.3 BC Seats/Stretcher Passenger
chunks.text: The preferred location is in an over head bin above an aisle seat. The bottle shall be stowed in the over head bin that can be locked and latched. The bottle of oxygen shall be stowed as shown below. A cabin bag shall be placed to ensure the bottle does not move for TTOL The tubing to be taken down between the separation of two over head bins. Open the valve and ensure the tubing is not crushed and the Oxygen is flowing The standard procedure shall be followed to administer Oxygen. Medical Centre shall inform Engineering department of the requirements of additional MEDA oxygen on flight, copying ground handling department who in turn will inform the Purser and the PIC. The duty Engineer will inform the Purser regarding the number of bottles and the location.

chunks.heading: 3.6.3 BC Seats/Stretcher Passenger
chunks.text: Crew Usage in post decompression Place the carry strap around neck and shoulder. The bottle should not obstruct CCM from assisting pas- sengers. During post decompression, oxygen from all bottles may be used until the gauge reads zero. Administering procedure, Ref 9.3 NOTE: In the event MEDA oxygen is pre-requested, CCMs to ensure spare oxygen masks shall be provided.

chunks.heading: 3.7 Manual Release Tool - (MRT)
chunks.text: Used to release the cabin oxygen system door Description The manual release tool is so designed that it has a flat end and a pin type end. The flat end is slightly curved and the pin end is folded inwards which requires to be rotated outward for use. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/ correctly secured/clear of obstruction Operation - The MRT is used to open the oxygen stowage compartment door manually. The pointed end is inserted into the pin hole to release the oxygen stowage compartment door lock (oxygen stow- age compartment). If the oxygen stowage compartment door is stuck the flat edge is used to release the door

chunks.heading: 3.8.1 Adult / Child Life Vest
chunks.text:
Description Every seat on the aircraft shall be equipped with a life vest easily accessible from the individu- al seating position. The life vest is made up of two separate buoyancy chambers. Two carbon dioxide cartridges are in- stalled for inflation. This can be activated by pulling the red tabs.
• Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks – Crew life vest

chunks.heading: 3.8.1 Adult / Child Life Vest
chunks.text:
Crew required to check on their personal life vest under each crew seat and if the overhauled due date is not expired
• Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks - Infants and passenger The infant life vest and the spare adult life vest - Correct location/correct number/ correctly secured/clear of obstruction A random check shall be carried out on the passenger life vest in the cabin Operation - Adult
1. Slip the life vests over the head and bring the strap around the waist
2. Attach the buckle and pull strap to tighten.
3. Pull the red tabs downwards sharply to inflate.
4. To manually inflate the vest, blow into the rubber tubes located on the side of the vest.
5. The protective plugs of the battery must be pulled to activate the locator light powered by a water activated battery. - last for 08 hours.
6. A whistle is available to attract attention. Precautions - Sharp objects should be removed prior to donning and precautions should be taken not to over tighten

chunks.heading: 3.8.1 Adult / Child Life Vest
chunks.text: buckle or keep it too loose

chunks.heading: 3.8.1 Adult / Child Life Vest
chunks.text:
Fitting an Adult Life Vest to a Child
1. Slip the life vest over the child’s head.
2. Pass the strap around the waist and secure using the buckle
3. Pull the strap to tighten and secure the vest.
4. Inflate one chamber of the life vest by blowing in to the rubber tubes. NOTE: Child life vests shall be fitted and inflated during Phase II

chunks.heading: 3.8.2 Infant Life Vest
chunks.text: Every infant on board shall be provided with a flotation device designed for them. The neck size is reduced when inflated to ensure the infant does not pass through. A lifting tape with a lifeline is attached to grasp and secure the infant to the adult. Description – The infant life vest is a single chamber flotation device. When activated the chamber inflates around the waist of the infant. A life line is attached for securing purpose. It consists of a manual inflation system by pulling the tab and an oral inflation tube for increase or decrease of pressure. A battery is connected to a light which activates when immersed in water. Light System Assembly: The system consists of a light and a battery attached to the harness. The light is automatically activated when the battery is immersed in water. Harness Assembly: The harness assembly consists of a harness and a buckle. The harness assembly secures the life vest to

chunks.heading: 3.8.2 Infant Life Vest
chunks.text: the wearer Oral Inflation System: The oral inflation system has a tube connected to the buoyancy cell. The end of the tube is fitted with a valve. The oral inflation system is used to add or remove pressure as necessary. Manual Inflation System: The manual inflation system consists of a carbon dioxide cylinder attached to an inflator mechanism and the inflator tag. When activated the compressed carbon dioxide gas is released and fills the cham- ber

chunks.heading: 3.8.2 Infant Life Vest
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024 Operation
1. Remove the life vest from its pouch.
2. Place the hands through the openings
3. Don the life vest around the infant’s chest.
4. Put the harness through the infant legs
5. Close the three locking points of the buckle at the back of the infant
6. Secure the life vest by the harness
7. To adjust the harness pull on the loose end
8. Pull the red inflator tag to inflate the life vest at the door sill. Use the oral inflation system if more or less pressure in the life vest is necessary:
1. Blow into the tube to inflate
2. Press the valve to deflate the life vest. Note: Oral inflation prior to gas inflation will cause excessive pressure which may burst the life vest. Limitations - The infant life vest will support an infant up to approximately 16 KGS.

chunks.heading: 3.8.3 Survival Cots - Infant
chunks.text:
Description – The baby-survival cot are for babies:
1. from 07 days to 18 months
2. up to a length of 838 mm.
3. up to a weight of 16.0 kgs The baby-survival cots have these main components:
1. Buoyancy and arch assembly.
2. Restrainer with 2 air apertures and 4 transparent windows The cover part of the restrainer is opened/closed with a sliding fastener across the middle from one side to the other side. The sliding fastener is covered by strips of clear PVC to make it water resistant, With the following features,
1. Strap with whistle and tether 3 meters.
2. Thermal waistcoat.
3. Gas inflation system (CO cylinder).

chunks.heading: 3.8.3 Survival Cots - Infant
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
4. Oral inflation system is available to inflate the cot.
5. A water-activated light that is powered by a battery is attached to the cover of the restrainer.
6. When the baby-survival cot is in the water, the water pocket fills with water to give the cot more stability and float upright. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/ correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Operation - Each baby-survival cot shows the instruction for its use:
1. Carefully remove the baby-survival cot from its fabric container, then unroll it. Get access to the inflation system.
2. Pull the red tab to inflate, this inflates the buoyancy chambers with gas from the attached infla- tion system.

chunks.heading: CAUTION: ORAL INFLATION PRIOR TO GAS INFLATION WILL CAUSE EXCESSIVE PRESSURE AND
chunks.text:
MAY BURST THE COT.
3. If more or less pressure in the cot is necessary, use the oral inflation system.
4. If necessary, inflate the floor of the cot with the attached oral inflation tube, to give the baby more protection.
5. Lay the baby on its side with its head at the air aperture in the waistcoat
6. Make sure that the baby lays correctly in the waistcoat and close the waistcoat
7. Carefully tighten the adjustable strap and secure the buckle.
8. Close the cover of the restrainer with the sliding fastener
9. Make sure that the strips cover the sliding fastener. This makes the sliding fastener water resist- ant
10. Place the cot on the floor with infants head pointing AFT.
11. To prevent the cot from moving pass the adults feet through the carrying strap.
12. Use the strap to carry the cot by hand or over the shoulder
13. Carry the cot to the exit and use the life line to lower the cot into the water

chunks.heading: CAUTION: ORAL INFLATION PRIOR TO GAS INFLATION WILL CAUSE EXCESSIVE PRESSURE AND
chunks.text: Note: The life line of the Survival Cot/infant life jacket can be tied around the waist of an adult once out side the aircraft Ground Evacuation- It provides maximum protection when sent down the slide. Ditching - The infant has a better chance of survival in a floatation cot, than any other standard floatation device on board Precautions - The cot should be inflated out of sight of the passengers. Ensure it is not damaged and fully inflated and rigid prior placing the infant

chunks.heading: 3.8.4 The Slide/Raft
chunks.text:
Description - The Slide/Raft is a floating device which is designed for protection under extreme conditions. It inflates automatically when the door is opened in the ARMED mode. The Slide/Raft includes,
• Boarding Handle - The boarding handles support passengers to climb into the slide raft.

chunks.heading: 3.8.4 The Slide/Raft
chunks.text:
Revision No 01 Revision Date 01 April 2024
• Boarding Ladder - The boarding ladder is installed for passengers to climb into the slide raft.
• Life Line - Is a tape located above the water level between the two buoyancy tubes of the Slide/ Raft. It continues lengthwise on both sides and provides assistance for survivors to hold on. It also could be used as an attachment point for signalling devices.
• Heaving line/Ring - A cord with a rubber ring attached used to retrieve survivors from the water. The line may be used to secure rafts together.
• Ditching line/Re-Entry Strap - It is also referred as the mooring line and avoids free fall of the slide when disconnected from the aircraft and its is attached to one of the upper tubes It can be used as a re-entry strap in the event of a land evacuation.
• Manual inflation handle - A red handle located at the right side at floor level, used for manual

chunks.heading: 3.8.4 The Slide/Raft
chunks.text:
inflation of the slide raft.
• Release handle - A white handle located at the centre of the girt bar used to detach the slide raft from the door sill.
• Safety Hook Knife - A sharp metal device used to cut the ditching line when disconnecting the raft from the aircraft. Located in a pouch on the top buoyancy chamber.
• No Fail Handles - Four brightly coloured canvas tape handles located at the bottom of the slide raft. It shall be used to hold the raft to evacuate passengers when used as a hand held slide.
• Lighting strip - Is a strip illuminated to hi-light the sliding path located along the sliding path on both sides. It activates when the slide raft is deployed and would last as long as emergency lights last and the power line remains connected to the aircraft.
• Locator lights - Located on top of the canopy support tubes and powered by water activated batteries. It illuminates automatically when the raft is in contact with water and last for 8 hours.

chunks.heading: 3.8.4 The Slide/Raft
chunks.text:
• Top up/off Valve - It is a screw type valve located on both chambers to connect the hand pump.
• Sea Anchor - Made of nylon fabric attached with a cord and is located in a pouch at the doorsill end between the two buoyancy tubes. It minimizes the drift and improves raft stability. The length could be adjusted for stability and manoeuvring.

chunks.heading: 3.8.5 Slide/Raft Variance
chunks.text: The slide rafts at L2 /R2 are equipped with a boarding ramp to angle away from the aircraft engines.

chunks.heading: 3.8.6 Survival Equipment (Survival Kit)
chunks.text: Description - It is a bright coloured zipper type canvas container installed in each slide-raft. The contents are as fol- lows: Mirror/Heliograph Bailing bucket First aid kit Whistle Sponge Desalting kits Signals/Mini flares Hand pump Food rations Sea dye markers Repair plugs Plastic water bags Flash light Canopy Survival Manual Center Masts

chunks.heading: 3.8.7 Supplementary Raft Accessory Kit (SRAK)
chunks.text: Description - It is a bright yellow coloured bag. Contents as follows: Water Storage Bag 05 Reverse Osmosis Pump 01 Flashlight (Alkaline) 01 Flares 04 Emergency Rations (2000 Calories) 05

chunks.heading: 3.8.8 Reverse Osmosis Pump
chunks.text:
Is a simple hand activated fresh water-supplier with a suction and pump action. There are two tubes attached. The inlet tube is for salt water and outlet tube is for fresh water. It is able to convert over six gallons of sea water to drinking water Operation -
1. Pull back intake strainer, and attach the double hose.
2. Lower the strainer tube fully into the saltwater and place one hand under the end of the cap, the other hand over the end of the handle
3. Pump up and down as far as it will go in each direction at a speed of 40 strokes per minute.

chunks.heading: 3.9 No Exit Cards
chunks.text:
Description - It is a self-adhesive sign with red luminous lettering. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks Correct number/correct location/correctly secured/clear of obstructions. Operation - 1.04 ‘NO EXIT’ cards are provided and should be pasted as follows,
2. On the inoperative door
3. On the EXIT sign above the inoperative door

chunks.heading: 3.9 No Exit Cards
chunks.text: 4. On all EXIT signs leading to the inoperative door

chunks.heading: 3.10 Emergency Response Kit
chunks.text: Description - It is used to handle a dangerous goods incident on board and contains, A sponge/thick plastic bag/rubber bands/protective rubber gloves/blotting paper. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstructions. Operation- Ref 10.18.4

chunks.heading: 3.11 Restraint Tie kit
chunks.text:
Restraint Ties kit 1.2 thick restrain straps 2.4 thin restrain straps 3.1 pair of scissors Description (thick strap) two items. It is a hard plastic tape with a serrated side and a smooth side Operation - (thick strap)
1. Place one hand through the loop up to the wrist and draw down the thick strap
2. Take the arms behind the passenger and insert the other hand and tighten.
3. The straps are self-locking and have to be cut for removal.
4. Care should be taken when tightening and removing to prevent injury. Description - (thin strap)
1. four items. It is a hard plastic type with a serrated side and a smooth side. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks Correct number/correct location/correctly secured/clear of obstructions and the scissors included. Precautions- Do not use the ties as a tourniquet. Once restraint straps are drawn down they cannot be loosened

chunks.heading: 3.11 Restraint Tie kit
chunks.text:
Usage
1. The pair of thick restraints to be used to secure the hands behind (seat belt to be fastened mak- ing the passenger further unmovable)
2. The other restraints could be used for legs if necessary
3. It may be required to obtain assistance from an able bodied passenger when restraining an un- ruly passenger CAUTION : DO NOT USE THE TIES AS A TOURNIQUET. ONCE RESTRAINT STRAPS ARE DRAWN

chunks.heading: DOWN, THEY CANNOT BE LOOSENED
chunks.text: Location - A330 R4 Stowage Compartment

chunks.heading: 3.12 Aisle Chair
chunks.text: Description - It is a foldable wheel chair which can be manoeuvered in the aisle to transport a person to the lavatory or to an exit during boarding/disembarking.

chunks.heading: TYPE “A” - OPERATION
chunks.text:
1. Pull the chair upright until locked in position
2. Adjust the foot rest
3. Two braking devices are located at the rear of the aisle chair
4. To Stow the aisle chair
5. Pull the black release cord across at the bottom of the chair

chunks.heading: TYPE “B” - OPERATION
chunks.text:
1. Pull the chair upright until locked, if not push the orange handle located at the bottom of the chair
2. Adjust the foot rest and secure seat belts
3. Two braking device are located above the rear wheels
4. To Stow the aisle chair,
5. Pull the orange pull handle until the chair collapses

chunks.heading: 3.13 Cabin Defects Log Book
chunks.text: Description - Cabin Defects Log book is retained on board to record unserviceable/used or missing equipment in the aircraft cabin, galleys and lavatories but not limited to. Above observations shall be recorded/signed and dated in the cabin defects log book by the CCMs. All CCMs are responsible to inform the Purser of any observations that are detected pre-flight, during flight and post flight. Discrepancies on the quantity as per the MEL, of safety and survival equipment shall also be recorded as soon as observed. The Engineer on duty shall comment on all entries prior to signing of the aircraft for airworthiness Differed Defects (D/D) - D/D is when a defect is permitted to be differed and the aircraft is permitted to fly with the defect for a pre-determined period. Procedure for entering cabin defects log The Purser shall record all cabin defects with the date and signature Entries shall be precise with the nature of the defect, factual and detailed information shall be stated

chunks.heading: 3.13 Cabin Defects Log Book
chunks.text: when making an entry. Engineers shall review the cabin defects log at the end of each flight in order to rectify the defect. Those defects classified in the MEL as “NO GO” shall be rectified prior to departure. Whenever safety equipment is used it shall be logged in the cabin defects log with details and location for replacements. When the cabin defects log book is changed, the new log book shall carry forward the pending defects.

chunks.heading: 3.14.1 First Aid Kit
chunks.text: Description - Carried on the aircraft for First Aid and minor medical ailments. Requirement - 01 First Aid kit for every 100 passengers Pre-Flight Check/Serviceability Checks Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstructions/seal intact. Contents Ref 9.14

chunks.heading: 3.14.2 Emergency Medical Kit (A10)
chunks.text: Description - Carried on the aircraft for Major Medical Emergencies and is under the purview of the PIC. It can be used only by a qualified, Medical Practitioner/Paramedic or a Nurse. Contents Ref 9.15

chunks.heading: 3.14.3 Automated External Defibrillator (AED)
chunks.text:
Description – Carried on the aircraft to revive persons with a cardiac arrest. A battery operated electronic defibrillator with an automated voice command for usage . Pre-Flight Check Correct location/correctly secured/clear of obstruction. Serviceability Checks Check on the status indicator - flashing (hour glass) or Green LED flashing Items included.
1. AED battery / 01
2. AED memory card / 01
3. Heart pad adult / 01
4. Heart pad child & infant / 01
5. ECG leads (03 cables) / 01 set
6. ECG electrodes / 03 / 01 set
7. Red box Precautions Ensure the patient is placed on a dry surface and no part of the first aider is in contact with the patient when the shock is delivered Operation Ref 9.12

chunks.heading: 3.14.4 Resuscitator Vent Aid Kit (RVAK)
chunks.text:
Description - It is designed for mouth-to mask ventilation for adult/child or infant. It is a heart shaped flexible trans- parent mask designed to fit the nose and mouth. It has a detachable one-way valve and should be used by a trained person A pair of rubber gloves are stowed with it Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks
1. Correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstructions.
2. Instructions leaflet placed in the packing. Operation- Administering procedure, Ref 9.4

chunks.heading: 3.14.5 AMBU Resuscitator
chunks.text:
Air-Shields Manual Breathing Unit/Resuscitator (Ambu Bag) Description – The Ambu bag is a F/Aid equipment held and operated by hand to provide continuous oxygen to a per- son. It is a hollow bag with a transparent re-breather bag. A detachable mask and oxygen tubing with one free end attached to the Ambu bag. Pre Flight Checks/Serviceability Checks correct location/correct number/correctly secured/clear of obstructions Precaution
• Page for a medical practitioner
• Don protective gloves

chunks.heading: 3.14.5 AMBU Resuscitator
chunks.text:
• Ensure the face mask is connected to the bag and the bag is connected to the oxygen tube.
• If patient vomits, remove mask and clear patient’s airway
• Clear the mask assembly of foreign material
• Re-apply mask to the patient and continue ventilation. Operation- Administering procedure, Ref 9.5

chunks.heading: 3.15.2 Hand Set (With the PA system functioning)
chunks.text: Required for dispatch 8 - One each at every exits. One or more hand sets may be inoperative provided that one hand set is operative at each pair of exit doors. Alternate, normal and emergency procedures shall be established in consultation with the PIC for the use of one hand set per pair of exits if required. In the event L1 PA system is inoperative – The Purser shall define the hand set used when required and communicate to the PIC/ Cabin crew and document same. chunks.heading: 3.15.3 Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL)
chunks.text: Established by the aircraft manufacturer for the specific aircraft type. A list established for a particu- lar aircraft type by the manufacturer with the approval of the state of manufacturer containing items, which is permitted to be unserviceable at the commencement of a flight. The MMEL may be associated with special operating conditions, limitations or procedures. The MMEL is located in the flight deck. In the event an item/s on the MMEL malfunctions or not limited to, during flight the PIC shall be informed for guidance

chunks.heading: 3.15.4 Minimum Equipment List (MEL)
chunks.text: MEL provides information for the operation of an aircraft, subject to specified conditions with particular equipment inoperative. It is compiled by the operator and approved by CAASL (Authority) in conformity with or more restrictive than the MMEL. The MEL contains the items or components, the repair category, the quantity per aircraft, the dispatch minimum, the qualifying conditions and the operational procedure. The PIC shall use the MEL when required to confirm the dispatching minimum, the qualifying conditions and operating procedures. The PIC may over ride the minimums depicted in the CCM SEP Manual for dispatch guided by the MEL within the regulatory requirements. The MEL is located in the flight deck.
