chunks.heading: 6.5.7 Type 1 door Escape Slides/Rafts
chunks.text: Each type “1” door is equipped with a dual-lane slide. They are stowed in a container hinged on the lower part of the door. When the door is opened in the “ARMED” mode, automatic slide/raft deploy- ment and inflation will occur. The disconnection procedure is clearly marked on the slide. If the slide is Inflated and Deflates, Instruct four ABPs who have evacuated to hold the no fail handles and direct one passenger at a time to evacuate. Passengers shall be directed to useable exits to expe- dite the evacuation

chunks.heading: 6.6 Type “III” Exits (Hatches)
chunks.text: When the hatch is removed, you can see the SLIDE MANUAL INFLATION HANDLE. An awareness safety briefing shall be carried out for ABPs seated in the proximity of the hatches. The details of how to open the hatch is depicted on the back of the seat and between the hatches. The over wing emergency hatches are always in the “ARM MODE” and the slide would automatically inflate when one hatch is opened. Opening one of the hatches on each side will deploy the slide on the relevant side in three seconds. The off wing slides are equipped with a manual inflation system. The red manual inflation handle is located at the upper inner part of the hatch frame and is visible when the hatch is opened. Hatches are primary exits for a crash landing. In a ditching it will be opened only as a last resort.

chunks.heading: 6.6.1 Opening of Hatches
chunks.text:
1. Remove the flap cover
2. The slide armed white indicator should illuminate
3. Pull down the control handle, the hatch door should fall inwards
4. Lift the hatch frame by using the grip mould at the bottom of the hatch
5. Throw the hatch out of the leading edge of the wing, to prevent any damage to the slide
6. If it fails to inflate pull the manual inflation handle

chunks.heading: 6.6.2 Manual Inflation Handle
chunks.text: The red manual inflation handle located at the upper inner part of the hatch frame

chunks.heading: 6.6.3 Deployment of the Over Wing Slide
chunks.text:
It is equipped with dual lane slides.
1. Deceleration Strips
2. There are deceleration strips at the far end of the slide. These strips decrease the speed of evacu- ees, before touching the ground.
3. Sliding Surface
4. Side Rails, The rails prevents the passengers from falling off the slide .
5. Over Wing Ramp Barrier, The barrier provides a visual guide for the evacuees towards to the ramp and to the slide.
6. Ramp, The ramp provides a transition from the wing to the evacuation slide
7. Buoyancy Chambers, The inflated tubes stabilize the slide structure
8. No fail Handles
9. LED Lights, The LED lights provide lighting to the sliding surface and at the end of the slide.

chunks.heading: 6.6.4 Inflated and deflated Over-Wing Slide
chunks.text: If the Over-Wing slide is inflated and deflates due to a damage, it can still be used as a hand held escape slide. Locate the snap hook on the slide and attach it to the attachment point on the wing (D ring). Four ABPs shall hold the slide by using the two no fail handles installed on either side of the escape slide.

chunks.heading: 6.6.4 Inflated and deflated Over-Wing Slide
chunks.text: Shall evacuate one passenger at a time, instructing them to sit and slide.

chunks.heading: 6.6.5 Ditching Lines (Lifeline)
chunks.text:
The aircraft is equipped with 4 ditching lines which are used only in a ditching. The ditching lines are used to assist passengers moving on the wing during a ditching. The ditching lines are stowed in a nar- row compartment (Overhead bin) above the over wing hatches on either side. It will assist passenger to remain on the wing. Operation Instruct ABP to
1. Fix one snap hook of the lifeline to the attachment point located on the upper outer part of the hatch frame
2. Fix the other snap hook to the to the wing attachment point (B ring) located on the center of the wing surface
3. Once both snap hooks are securely connected, pull the Pull Tab to tighten the lifeline
4. The sliding buckle holds the lifeline tight for the correct length
5. Instruct passengers to evacuate use leg body leg, inflate life vest, hold on to the lifeline and remain on the wing.

chunks.heading: 6.7 Slide Raft Description
chunks.text:
The raft is designed in such a manner that it has two individual buoyancy chambers. Top chamber and a lower chamber. If one chamber is damaged the other chamber will keep the occupants a float. Both chambers are equipped with a facility to top up air and the locations for fixing the hand pump (inflation valves) are clearly marked. A hand pump is located in the survival kit.
1. Life Line, The life lines are installed along each side of the slideraft to enable passengers to hold onto the slideraft when in water.
2. Boarding Ladder,The boarding ladders are installed for passengers to climb into the slideraft.
3. Boarding Handle, The boarding handle support passengers to climb into the slideraft.
4. Heaving Ring, The heaving ring can be thrown to passengers in the water to pull them towards the slideraft.
5. Sea Anchor, The sea anchor is attached to the raft to stabilize the raft and act as a brake

chunks.heading: 6.7.2 Lighting Strip
chunks.text: The escape slides are equipped with an integral lighting system. The escape slide lights automatically illuminate when the escape slides are deployed. The escape slides are powered by the same power source as the cabin emergency lights and would last until the power supply cable remains connected to the air craft for a maximum period of 12 minutes.

chunks.heading: 6.7.3 Canopy
chunks.text: The canopy is located in the survival pack. It is water proof, wind resistant and bright orange/red in colour to attract attention. One end of the canopy is marked BOARD END. The outside surface is marked THIS SIDE UP.

chunks.heading: 6.7.4 Canopy Erection Instructions
chunks.text:
Canopy erection instructions are printed on the pouch in which the canopy is stowed. It is also con- tained in the slide raft management guide, which is located in the survival kit. Installing the canopy,
1. Remove canopy from the bag
2. Keep the canopy low to prevent it from being blown out of the raft
3. The markings on the canopy “Board End” should be on the girt bar end
4. The marking this side up should be the outer part of the canopy
5. Numbers are marked as even numbers on the right and odd on the left
6. Numbers on the canopy should correspond with the numbers on the raft support tubes.
7. Fix the rubber mount to the raft center attachment point (Rubber Pads)
8. Extend the center masts to a full length
9. Insert center mast into rubber mount and secure with tie down laces
10. Spread canopy lengthwise on the slide raft
11. Drape the canopy over the support tubes
12. Secure the canopy by tying it on to the attachment points on the main buoyancy tubes.

chunks.heading: 6.8.1 Viewing Windows
chunks.text: The windows installed in the flight deck are fixed windows and sliding windows. They are installed in front and each side of the flight deck

chunks.heading: 6.8.2 Sliding Windows
chunks.text:
Two of the flights deck windows can be used as secondary emergency escape routes. They are the second window located on both sides of the Pilots viewing windows. It has a locking and sliding mecha- nism. The windows can be opened only from inside, once opened it can be closed and locked back into its original position. To Operate the Sliding Window Opening
1. Press down the knob on the operating handle
2. Rotate rearwards until the windows moves inwards and slide window to the AFT until locked. Closing
1. Move forward the locking lever
2. Move the window with the forward window handle until it reaches the closed position
3. Push the operating handle forward to lock the window.

chunks.heading: 6.8.3 Escape Routes
chunks.text:
Escape routes from the flight deck are sliding windows using the escape rope and through the secure flight deck door. Descent Ropes Two knotted descent ropes are installed in a compartment above each sliding window. Each rope shall
1. Fixed Windows
2. Sliding Windows

chunks.heading: 6.8.3 Escape Routes
chunks.text: withstand a weight up to 180 Kgs. Throw the rope out from the sliding window. Use Leg, Body, Leg tech- nique to evacuate from the sliding window. Face the fuselage and lower body down to prevent injury.

chunks.heading: 6.9 Secure Flight Deck Door
chunks.text: SriLankan Airlines operated aircraft are equipped with a secure flight deck door, that separates the flight deck from the cabin. It is designed to resist penetration by small arms fire, grenade shrapnel and resist forcible intrusion by unauthorised persons. It is fully compliant with rapid decompression requirements. It has a digital keypad located on the door frame. It has an electrical control system, located in the flight deck. An emergency exit escape panel is located on the lower part of the door. The door when closed is locked at all times. In the event of a decompression or total electrical power failure, the door unlocks automatically. As the flight deck door is heavy, care should be taken to close the door gently. Emergency Exit escape Panel The emergency exit escape panel could be removed only from the flight deck. The two latches on the side of the panel should be moved to the centre and the panel pushed toward the cabin.

chunks.heading: 6.9 Secure Flight Deck Door
chunks.text: Digital Key Pad The keypad is located on the side of the forward attendant panel and equipped with two indicator lights (green and red) /numerical display. The keys are used to, request entry to the flight deck and the numbers are used to unlock the door. Key Pad Indicators GREEN light – steady- Indicates the Flight Crew has unlocked the door and it remains unlocked for 5 seconds. RED light - steady- Indicates the Flight Crew has denied access, the door remains locked and the emergency access keypad is inhibited for a pre-selected time

chunks.heading: 6.9.1 Controls on the Secure Flight Deck Door
chunks.text:
The toggle switch located in the flight deck has three positions ‘Unlock/Norm/Lock’ and an indicator light comes on when the door is opened. Opening the Secure Flight Deck Door from the cabin The door could be opened in,
1. Normal operation
2. Secondary operation

chunks.heading: 6.9.1 Controls on the Secure Flight Deck Door
chunks.text: 3. Emergency operation

chunks.heading: 6.9.2 Normal Operation
chunks.text:
Press “CALL CAPT” on the handset Establish contact with the Flight Crew and request access to the flight deck If entry is authorized by the Flight Crew:
1. The Flight Crew unlocks the door
2. A green light illuminates steady on the keypad, and kept unlocked for 5 seconds
3. CCM may gain entry by pushing open the door If entry is not authorized:
1. The door will be locked and red light comes on steady on the keypad
2. The keypad is locked for a pre-selected time

chunks.heading: 6.9.3 Secondary Operation
chunks.text:
3. Press 01 # on the key pad to request entry If entry is authorized
1. The Flight Crew unlocks the door
2. A green light illuminates steady, and door will be unlocked for 5 seconds
3. CCM may gain entry by pushing open the door

chunks.heading: 6.9.4 Emergency Operation
chunks.text:
PIC shall brief the Purser regarding the 2 to7 digit secret code at the pre-flight safety briefing to be used in the event of an emergency. The code shall be referred to as CODE RED. CCM shall adopt the follow- ing emergency procedure in the event of the Flight Crew does not respond to a call from the Cabin. Press “EMER CALL” on the handset to establish contact with the Flight Crew. If there is no response from the Flight Crew;
1. Enter code red
2. The green light on the key pad would start flashing
3. After a pre-selected time of (15 /120 seconds)
4. The door would unlock for 5 seconds/green light would illuminate steady
5. CCM should gain entry by pushing open the door Precautions Ref 2.10.8

chunks.heading: 6.10 Avionics Compartment
chunks.text: Access to the avionics compartment is not possible from the flight deck as an opening is not available.

chunks.heading: 6.11 Flight Deck Seats
chunks.text: Four seats are available in the flight deck of which two are column mounted and two foldable seats. The PIC’s and First Officer’s seats are column mounted seats and can be operated electrically and man- ually

chunks.heading: 6.11.1 Flight Deck Seats Description
chunks.text:
1. Column mounted seats
2. Electrically operated vertical and horizontal position with a manual back up
3. A manually operated recline lever
4. Equipped with shoulder harness, lap strap, fifth seat belt with a locking lever
5. An adjustable lumbar support
6. A life vest stowed at the back of the seat The first officer’s seat is identical to the PIC’s seat except that the controls are located on the left-hand side

chunks.heading: 6.11.2 First Observer Seat – Foldable Seat
chunks.text:
7. Located behind the center console
1. Equipped with a shoulder harness, lap strap and a fifth seat belt
2. Automatic seat pan folding facility
3. Releasing the lever located by the side of the seat to move it side ways
4. A life vest is located under the seat

chunks.heading: 6.11.3 Second Observer Seat – Foldable Seat
chunks.text:
1. Located behind the PIC’s seat
2. Equipped with a shoulder harness, lap strap and a fifth seat belt
3. Automatic seat pan folding facility
4. Fixed seat

chunks.text: The PIC may authorize a non-revenue passenger to occupy a Flight Deck observer seat with the follow- ing conditions: Ref:2.12.4

chunks.text: The forward attendant station accommodates seating for two attendants which are referred to as L1 &

chunks.heading: 6.12.2 Aft Attendant Seat
chunks.text: The seat belt must be stow correctly in the stowage cavity located at the rear of the seat pan, in order to avoid obstruction to the exit.

chunks.heading: 6.12.3 Swivel Seat
chunks.text: The attendant foldable swivel seat is installed in the aisle at the rear of the cabin. To install or to restore the seat, lift the lever to release the locking device (Type “A”) OR release the locking devices behind the seat and under the seat pan (Type “B”). In an emergency the first action of the CCM shall be to ensure the seat is in the stowed position before commencing evacuation commands.

chunks.heading: 6.13.1 Unaccompanied Minors
chunks.text: Second and third rows in BC & EY cabins are allocated (Window Seats)

chunks.heading: 6.13.2 Passenger with Disability
chunks.text: Second and third rows in BC & EY cabins are allocated (Window Seats)

chunks.heading: 6.13.4 Stretcher Positions
chunks.text: The last three rows (A,B,C / D,E,F) are allocated for stretcher passengers, with D,E,F as the primary loca- tion.

chunks.heading: 6.14 Briefing at the Hatches (Type “III” Exits)
chunks.text:
The Passengers occupying seats adjacent to the hatches shall be briefed as stated below.
1. ‘Greet the passenger”
3. ‘Are you aware that you are seated next to an emergency exit?’ (Point at hatchers on both sides/ point at the door)
4. ‘Are you willing to assist in case of emergency?’
5. ‘Thank you very much’
6. The hatch/door must be opened only on command’
7. ‘The steps to open hatch/door are shown on the hatch/door (point to decals) and in the safety card. please take a few minutes to go through it before take-off’
8. ‘Do you have any questions?, thank you once again for your willingness to help us” The Cabin Supervisor shall be responsible for conducting the briefing. The CCM conducting the briefing shall ensure the passengers have understood the procedure. If in doubt or if the passenger is not willing to assist, the Purser shall be informed, and passenger/s relocat- ed

chunks.heading: 6.15.1 Over Head stowage Compartment
chunks.text: Overhead compartments are located along the cabin sidewalls throughout the cabin. Stowage compart- ments have a load limit, which is indicated by a placard on the side. The compartment is locked with a slam lock. Once unlocked it will open automatically aided by the vacuum struts which holds the door open. An overhead compartment with a defective slam lock shall not be used for storage and shall be sealed to prevent usage.

chunks.heading: 6.15.2 Dog Houses
chunks.text: A doghouse is a stowage compartment with a drawer, fixed on the aircraft floor and are located behind the last row of the BC and EY cabins.

chunks.heading: 6.16 Galleys
chunks.text: The aircraft is equipped with two galleys. One in the forward identified as - G1 and the other at the rear identified as - G5

chunks.heading: 6.16.1 Water Shut-Off Valve
chunks.text: The water shut-off valves for the forward and aft galleys are located adjacent to the sink.

chunks.heading: 6.16.2 Waste Water
chunks.text: The waste water from the galley sinks are drained out of the aircraft through two heated drain masts in the forward and the aft of the aircraft located on the outer fuselage.

chunks.heading: 6.17 Lavatories
chunks.text: A 320 aircraft consist of three lavatories, one in the forward and two at the aft. Lavatory “A” in the for- ward is adjacent to the flight deck door, lavatory “D” and “E” are situated at the aft on either side of the aisle, forward of the aft galley. All three lavatories are equipped with diaper changing facilities and a handrail for PWD use and are fitted with smoke detectors. The handicap passenger sign is marked on the lavatory door together with the diaper changing board sign

chunks.heading: 6.17.1 Lavatory Waste Bin Fire Extinguisher
chunks.text: Description The lavatory waste bin fire extinguishers contain Halon and Freon gas. It is installed in the compartment below the sink of each lavatory. Pre Flight Check Ensure the needle is in the green zone

chunks.heading: 6.17.2 Smoke Detector
chunks.text: One smoke detector each is installed in all the lavatories. When smoke is detected, a warning signal is transmitted throughout the cabin and in the flight deck.

chunks.heading: 6.17.3 Smoke /Fire Warning Signal
chunks.text:
1. A repetitive triple low chime will sound every 30 seconds over the cabin loudspeakers
2. FAP SMOKE PAGE automatically comes on indicating the affected lavatory together with the location on aircrafts with touch screen FAPs
3. Red attention getter on all AIPs flashes, and text displaying the affected lavatory
4. The amber light will flash at the relevent ACPs
5. The amber light mounted on the exterior of the affected lavatory would flash
6. A steady red SMOKE LAV button on the Forward Attendant Panel (FAP) and the Additional Atten- dant Panels (AAP) will illuminate Re-setting the Warning System Once the smoke clears the system will reset automatically. By pressing the LAV SMOKE Indicator on the FAP or AAP’s audio and the visual signs on the AIP and ACP will be cancelled, but the following indica- tions will remain until the smoke clears
1. Amber flashing light on LAV exterior wall
2. SMOKE RESET (FAP) and SMOKE LAV (AAP) buttons illuminated red

chunks.heading: 6.17.3 Smoke /Fire Warning Signal
chunks.text: 3. On the touch screen FAP the smoke page indicator NOTE: On - 4R ABL aircraft the smoke reset switch is located outside each individual lavatory. Press the smoke reset push button outside the affected lavatory to cancel the audio and visual warnings.

chunks.heading: 6.17.4 Lavatory Water Shut off Valves
chunks.text: A manual water shut off valve is installed in each lavatory to cut off the water supply. It is located at floor level under the sink. The waste bin compartment door shall be open to gain access. CAUTION WHEN THE MANUAL WATER SHUT-OFF VALVE IS CLOSED THE WATER HEATER MUST

chunks.heading: BE OFF
chunks.text: Vacuum Release Valve The vacuum release valve is located under the sink to prevent air loss through the drain mast. If the float valve does not release water from the sink a manual pull ring is located on the float valve

chunks.heading: 6.18.9 Communication - PA /Interphone System
chunks.text: An interphone handset with integral push button for passenger address and crew calls are provided at all crew seats. The handset is easily accessible to a CCM when strapped into a crew seat. On 4R-ABM/N/O aircraft a push button must be used to release the hand set from the cradle. The PA system provides adequate sound levels to each row of passenger seats through loudspeakers. In addition, one loudspeaker is installed in each lavatory and each galley area. The PA can be operated from any handset and from the flight deck.

chunks.heading: 6.18.11 Passenger call System
chunks.text: A passenger call can be activated by pressing the attendant call push button located above each seat row. A HI chime is heard with the seat row indicator flashing on ground and during flight with the seat row indicator lighting up steady. To reset press the originating passenger call push button or by pressing CALL RESET on FAP/AAP on certain aircraft.

chunks.heading: 6.19.1 Ceiling Lights
chunks.text: Emergency ceiling lights are located on the ceiling panels throughout the cabin and are designed to provide downward lighting into the aisles. The cabin crew can turn ON the emergency light regardless of the position of the cockpit control

chunks.heading: 6.19.2 Escape Path Lighting System
chunks.text: Floor Escape Path Lighting System The floor escape path lighting system is photo luminescent. It requires a minimum of 15 minutes ex- posure to any light source or ambient daylight to illuminate the system. The Exit lights adjacent to the doors are controlled by the emergency light switches in the flight deck and the FAP.

Once activated the following pro- grams are available, Audio Channels Video Channels – As stipulated in the “On Board Entertainment” Guide Games The head sets for BC/EY are double pin head sets. Selection of movies and other programs are by using the touch screen. Audio & Video are on demand (AVOD System). The USB port is for charging an electronic device such as Mobile phones etc… Prior to screening of the safety demonstration, the IVS screens in business class ,row 6 and seats locat- ed near the hatches needs to be taken out of the stowage on ABM/N/O aircraft.

chunks.heading: 6.22.1 Fixed Oxygen
chunks.text: An oxygen generator is located above each row of seats. During a loss of cabin pressure the masks shall deploy automatically. If it fails to open, it can be opened by using the manual release tool. Once de- ployed one oxygen mask needs to be pulled down to activate the generator. Once activated oxygen will last for 15 minutes.

chunks.heading: 6.37.1 Aircraft Specific
chunks.text: Description The A320 NEO is a short to medium range, single aisle subsonic transport aircraft, powered by two tur- bofan engines. The fuselage has a circular cross section and is entirely pressurized with the exception of the nose and tail cone, the landing gear bays, the air conditioning compartments and the cargo com- partments. The flight deck is designed to accommodate a two operating crewmembers and two observ- ers. Any combination for cabin attendant seats may be provided with a minimum of 4 primary seats. Aircraft Specifics, Aircraft Registration - 4R ANA/B Model - A 320 - NEO Operating Range - 6,850km (3,700nm) Flight Deck Seats - 02 Flight Deck Observer Seats - 02 Cabin Crew Seats - 06 (L1, L1A, L2, L2A, R2, Swivel Seat) Minimum Crew - 4 (L1,L1A,L2,Swivel Seat) Configuration - Business Class 12, Economy Class 138

chunks.heading: 6A.0 A321 AIRCRAFT SPECIFIC
chunks.text:
6A.1 General Description The Airbus A321 is a short to medium range narrow body aircraft equipped with two turbofan engines. The A321 is a development of the A320, with an increased fuselage length of approximately 7.0 meters (22 feet).The A321 is the longest model of the A320 single aisle family. It’s a subsonic transport aircraft. The fuselage has a circular cross section and is entirely pressurized with the exception of the nose and tail cone, the landing gear bays and the air conditioning compartments. 6A.1.1 Aircraft Specifics, Model - A321 Operating Range - 3,000nm, 5,950 Km Flight Deck Seats - 02 Flight Deck Observer Seats - 02 6A.2 Doors/ Emergency Exits/Flight Deck Escape Route The A 321 is equipped with
• Type “I” Doors (04)
• Type “C” Exits (04)
• Two sliding windows in the flight deck for emergency escape Type “I” Doors are used for normal and emergency operation Type “C” Exits are used only during an emergency

chunks.text: The Type “C” emergency exits are located at L2, R2, L3, R3 which are located FWD and AFT of the wings. These exits do not consist of a raft but a single lane slide.

6A.6 Type “C” Exits Four type “C” exits are located at L2/R2, L3/R3 and shall be used only during an emergency evacuation. These doors which open outwards and forward in a staggered motion until locked and held in place by a “GUST” lock. A protective cover is on the door control handle to prevent inadvertent lifting of the handle. A single lane slide is stored in a compartment located underneath the door in the fuselage. The slides are canted slightly in order to deploy at a safe distance from the engines.

chunks.heading: 6A.0 A321 AIRCRAFT SPECIFIC
chunks.text:
6A.6.1 Serviceability Checks The inflation cylinder for each slide is stowed above each emergency exit in the overhead compart- ment. As a pre-flight check the needle on the gauge shall be in the green zone. 6A.6.2 Opening the door - Internal
1. Check door is disarmed
2. Check attention getters next to the viewing window
3. Check outside conditions
4. Open protective cover of the control handle
5. Hold assist handle and lift the door control handle
6. The door shall open in stages, do not force the opening process 6A.6.3 Closing the door - Internal
1. Grasp the assist handle on the door frame
2. Press the gust lock down firmly to release the door
3. Pull door rearwards in a semicircle until positioned in front of the door frame
4. Pull in and lower the door control handle until locked
5. Check the indicator reads “LOCKED” in green
6. Opening the door – External
7. Ensure the RED cabin pressure warning attention getter is not flashing

chunks.heading: 6A.0 A321 AIRCRAFT SPECIFIC
chunks.text:
8. Push the flap in and grasp the control handle
9. Lift up fully until the door is open (Above the green horizontal line)
10. Pull the door outwards and push forward until locked ( gust lock) Note: The slide would disarm automatically when opened from outside 6A.6.4 Closing of the door – External
1. Push the gust lock firmly down to release the door
2. Lift the door control handle above the green horizontal line
3. Move the door rearwards and into the frame
4. Lower the control handle and flush the control handle in to the door

chunks.heading: 6A.0 A321 AIRCRAFT SPECIFIC
chunks.text:
6A.6.5 Emergency Operation
1. Check out side conditions
2. Ensure lever is in the ARMED mode
3. Hold assist handle firmly
4. Open protective guard covering the door control handle
5. Pull the door control handle fully upwards and release
6. The door shall open and stay still for a few seconds to facilitate the slide deployment and gradu- ally open fully
7. Check correct slide deployment 6A.6.6 Manual Inflation Handle If the slide does not inflate automatically a RED manual inflation handle is stowed in upper right-hand side of the door frame. It is protected with a transparent cover. 6A.6.7 Operation Remove the transparent cover and pull the RED manual inflation handle firmly. 6A.6.8 Arming the slide on a Type “C” door Remove safety pin and stow in the pouch available under the, R2, R3, L3, crew seats. Move the arming/ disarming lever down until flushed in. At L2/R2 both safety pins shall be stored in the pouch under R2

chunks.text: 6A.9.2 Deploying the Portable Raft Position the raft at R2 exit, Check water level and open the door in disarmed mode Locate the activation line on the portable raft and secure to an anchor point on the aircraft. E.g. Assist handles, Launch raft and let it drift away, Pull sharply on the activation line to inflate the raft Pull raft towards the door sill and order passengers to board the raft In extreme conditions passengers may be advised to inflate life vest and jump into the water to board the raft, Cut the activation line attached to the aircraft using a hook knife available in the raft and move away 6A.9.3 Erecting the Canopy Open the accessory case and pull out the contents, 08 canopy support rods and the telescopic centre mast. Leave the rest of the accessories in the accessory case. Unfold the canopy (bright coloured) and position the openings above each boarding ramp, Locate 08 support rod webbing at each intersection

chunks.heading: 8.1.1 Aircraft and Flight Security
chunks.text: General Due to a serious build of aviation security threats the authorities has eagerly promoted awareness and made it mandatory a high level of security is established and maintained in the aviation sector. Taking

chunks.heading: 8.1.1 Aircraft and Flight Security
chunks.text: in to account the past incidents experienced Srilanakan airlines Security department has formulated a detailed chapter to successfully mitigate the security threats that might prevail. It is compiled in com- pliance to the CAASL requirements and approved by the DGCA. This section refers in general terms to the precautions and procedures applicable to Cabin Crew, and may be supplemented by information in the Flight Crew Notices or Cabin Crew Notices. Any incident which has a bearing on security is to be re- ported to the Head of Security / Senior Manager Security & Investigations, Station Manager & Manager In-flight Services, Delivery.

chunks.heading: 8.1.2 Purpose of security measures
chunks.text: To ensure the security and safety of the aircraft against unlawful interferences

chunks.heading: 8.1.2.2 Standard of searches and checks
chunks.text:
3. All service personnel boarding the aircraft with their carry-on items, shall be subjected to appro- priate security checks
4. Ensure that disembarking passengers do not leave items onboard the aircraft at transit stops and or turnarounds
5. During transit, stopovers and turnaround cabin crew / SriLankan Security staff / hired Security agents, would conduct appropriate aircraft inspection / search For obvious reasons, all reports and information on security matters shall be treated as confidential.

chunks.heading: 8.1.3 Control of access to aircraft
chunks.text:
1. Standard of access control
• Ensure unauthorized persons are being prevented from entering the aircraft, no person other than those listed below, would be permitted to board SriLankan aircraft
• Director General of the Civil Aviation Authority of Sri Lanka (DGCA) or his representative to per- form regulatory functions
• Representatives of Aviation Authorities of other countries at their relevant stations for the pur- pose of regulatory functions
• Customs/Immigration/Law Enforcement Officials according to perform official duties
• Bona fide passengers issued with boarding cards for the particular flight
• Authorized SriLankan staff
• Authorized staff of Handling Agents
2. During transit stopovers and turnaround, cabin crew/SriLankan Security staff/ hired Security agents shall be on duty on board to prevent unauthorized entry into aircraft
3. Any unidentified / suspicious person found within the aircraft, shall be immediately reported to

chunks.heading: 8.1.3 Control of access to aircraft
chunks.text: the Local Law Enforcement Authority/or Airport Authority

chunks.heading: 8.1.4 Co-operation with Airport Authorities
chunks.text: CCMs shall comply with security procedures required by airport authorities. At en-route stations the station manager or agent would ensure that procedures are compatible with local regulations. In the event of an aircraft diversion to any other airport, the PIC shall liaise with the local authorities to ensure the safety of the passengers and the aircraft.

chunks.heading: 8.1.5 Head of Security/Senior Manager Security and Investigations
chunks.text: The company has appointed a Head of Security/Senior Manager Security and Investigations who is responsible to liaise with national security authorities to evaluate levels of risk to SriLankan Airline’s and its area of Operations. In addition, he or his delegate (Duty Manager Security-ops) is responsible for informing the PIC/Purser of any security matter related to the current operations and/or duties.

chunks.heading: 8.1.6 PIC/Purser Responsibilities
chunks.text: The PIC is responsible for ensuring that security procedures at the aircraft that are pertinent to that particular flight have been completed prior to departure and before leaving the aircraft after the flight. Purser must report to the PIC that a Cabin Security checks such as galley compartments/Toilets/Meal Carts/Overhead Bins, have been completed before passengers’ board, before departure. Advice on non standard requirements and procedures at particular stations will be provided by the Sen- ior Manager Security & Investigations.

chunks.heading: 8.1.7 Identity Cards
chunks.text: CCMs shall wear their ID cards clearly visible on the outside of their clothing when on duty within the restricted zone at an airport (except when traveling on duty as a passenger) and remove/securely stow their cards after boarding the aircraft. It is the individual’s responsibility to ensure that his/her identity card remains valid and that he/she is familiar with its conditions of issue and use. All reasonable care shall to be taken to prevent loss or theft of ID cards, particularly when off duty, due to the security implications of misuse. It is even more serious if other identifying documents such as passports and licenses are lost or stolen at the same time.

chunks.heading: 8.1.7.1 Loss/Theft of ID card
chunks.text: Loss/Theft of ID card shall be reported to the Police in the area concerned immediately at the base or en-route station. Subsequently the loss/theft shall be reported to the Purser/PIC/Station Manager/In-flight Services De- partment/Security & Investigations Department and the Human Resources Department (As applicable).

chunks.heading: 8.1.8.1 Standards of screening and searching
chunks.text: 1. To ensure that crew, cabin and hold baggage intended for carriage onboard an aircraft engaged

chunks.heading: 8.1.8.1 Standards of screening and searching
chunks.text:
in an International Civil Aviation operation, is x-ray screened in order to prevent security risk articles or prohibited items or any item which can be used in an act of sabotage or other forms of unlawful interference. In the event of failure of x-ray equipment same shall be subjected to manual search
2. At destinations other than Sri Lanka, screening duties will be performed by an agency authorized by the Aviation Authority of that state to screen crew, hold and cabin baggage
3. Flight Deck Crew and Cabin Crewmembers are to safeguard personal baggage against possible interference or substitution, from the time it is packed until handed over for loading. Suitcases shall be locked at all times when unattended
4. If hotel or airport arrangements are such that Airline crew bags are left unattended at any time, a Crewmember shall be delegated to supervise them
5. All crew hold baggage & crew hand baggage must carry a Crew label

chunks.heading: 8.1.8.1 Standards of screening and searching
chunks.text: 6. All items labelled as Crew Baggage are to be checked-in as belonging to a crewmember before being handed over for loading onto the aircraft

chunks.heading: 8.1.8.2 Baggage Identification
chunks.text: If local procedures require that crew baggage shall be identified prior to boarding, such identification shall be done personally by the CCM concerned.

chunks.heading: 8.1.9 Apron Security
chunks.text: Only authorized persons are allowed in the vicinity of aircraft or equipment. Staff or appointed agents in ramp areas must be vigilant at all times; any suspicious behaviour is to be questioned, the suspect re- ported to the airport authorities and where possible, kept under observation until the arrival of security staff. All staff in ramp areas or in the airport restricted zone must wear valid I.D cards.

chunks.heading: 8.1.10 Unattended Aircraft
chunks.text: No air bridge/powered gangway or any other means of direct access from terminal or pier to aircraft may be in position against an aircraft unless under surveillance by staff or handling agents or appoint- ed security agents. When the aircraft is left unattended on the ramp, it shall be parked with all doors, hatches and windows closed and steps and ground equipment withdrawn, except when parked within the restricted zone and subject to the surveillance mentioned above.

chunks.heading: 8.1.11 Unscheduled Night Stops
chunks.text: At an unscheduled night stop, where adequate Station staff and good security facilities exist, the PIC’s responsibility for the safety of his aircraft is delegated to the Station Manager/Agent after it has been safely positioned for unloading.

chunks.heading: 8.1.12 Passenger Baggage Search
chunks.text: All passengers, their hand-baggage, and all duty-free items are to be searched except exemptions given by the SriLankan Airlines Security Manual chapter 4.8.12 before boarding the aircraft; the use of elec- tronic metal detectors is approved for this purpose. Local security screening and boarding procedures must not permit passengers to by-pass this personnel search. Any article considered a “security risk” is to be taken from a passenger and not to be loaded in aircraft cabin.

chunks.heading: 8.1.12 Passenger Baggage Search
chunks.text: Any cargo/ baggage or mail loaded in the hold or cabin shall be on completion of an appropriate securi- ty check. Checked/screened baggage shall be under the surveillance of the security staff until loaded on to the aircraft. Particular attention shall be paid to originating passengers possessing tickets purchased on the day of travel and passengers without any records.

chunks.heading: 8.2.1 Airport Categorisation
chunks.text: All airlines and airports have preventive systems on the ground aimed at preventing criminals and their weapons from getting into an aircraft. Such deterrents have played an important part in making aviation safer but they cannot totally prevent a resolute and ingenious criminal from beating the system. The continuing reports of hijack and sabotage incidents bear witness to this. This section provides guidance on handling security situations such as hijacks, and security procedures for crew compliance. The guidelines are recommended by the world’s aviation security or authorities based on in-depth studies of actual hijack and sabotage incidents. These organizations and Civil Aviation Authorities include ICAO, IATA, FAA, and State Civil Aviation Authorities. Every security situation has its own unique features, and certain developments not covered within this handbook, may arise. Nothing in this section is intended to override sound reasoning and good judg-

chunks.heading: 8.2.1 Airport Categorisation
chunks.text:
ment to be applied by crew when such situations develop.
1. Classification of a Bomb warning shall generally be based only on the first hand information
2. All bomb warnings may be classified as SPECIFIC, NON SPECIFIC & HOAX. The more informa- tion given by the caller, the more likely the threat shall be taken seriously. Each threat must be assessed to determine its significant risk it represents, so that appropriate measures may be implemented. SriLankan Airlines employees at home base or overseas shall ensure that contin- gency plans are provided for
• A controlled response by persons receiving bomb threats
• an assessment of the threat and risk involved by accredited personnel employed in positive target identification (P.T.I)
• detection of persons responsible for bomb threats and
• follow-up action
3. Bomb Threat assessors shall assess the threat by working methodically using the Bomb Threat

5. The following section provides criteria for three levels of threat conditions, which correlate to the three sets of suggested counter measures laid out in the risk management matrix

• Level One - Baseline - Green - there is no verifiable intelligence to indicate that any aircraft operator or airport has been targeted for attack, but there is always the possibility of unlawful interference by person or group of persons for numerous reasons.
• Level Two - Intermediate - Amber - verifiable intelligence indicates the probability that civil avi- ation operations have been targeted for attack.

chunks.text:
1. In general a bomb search shall be conducted with extreme caution. Use flashlights and mirrors when searching dark areas
2. Search may not be necessary, if a door compartment or a piece of equipment is properly sealed or secured and there is no evidence of tampering
3. The object of the search is to look for something out of place which does not belong to the air- craft or is not an integral part of the aircraft
4. Those who are involved in the search, shall be assigned specific areas, and be provided with the checklists which is located in the flight deck by the PIC.
5. Passengers shall be requested to keep their cabin baggage on their laps and search their hand luggage and clothing with any cabin crew available
6. Advice passengers of the information that a bomb may be on board and that precautionary measures are necessary although the warning may be a hoax
7. Request them to remain seated with their seat belts fastened

chunks.heading: 8.2.1.6 Discovery of suspect or prohibited articles
chunks.text:
If something is found which does not seem right or in any way suspicious
1. do not move it
2. Inform flight deck immediately, giving the exact location and description and size of the device
3. Where possible move passengers away from that area and instruct them to sit with their heads below tops of seat backs
4. Oxygen bottles, duty free liquor, perfumes, flammables or other stowed equipment which could present a projectile hazard shall be removed from the area
5. Fire extinguishers shall be readily available in case of an explosion
6. Once it is decided that the device is in a safe location, cover it with a split plastic bag to prevent liquid from entering the device. Cover with cushions, soft clothing and / or blankets to a depth and area as large as possible and saturate with water to reduce the risk of fire in the event the device is capable of causing fire

chunks.heading: 8.3 Bomb On Board
chunks.text:
A bomb threat can take many forms. Although not all of them are real, they shall always be considered a threat to flight safety. There are two main types of bomb threats:
1. Specific: Operator, flight number, aircraft type, departure time and destination are positively identified. The location of the bomb on board the aircraft may also be provided
2. Non-specific: May identify a flight by destination, origin or departure time. These type of threat usually takes the form of a telephone call. Bomb threats may also occur on board the aircraft. The following are examples of this:
1. Threats by passengers
2. Anonymous written messages found onboard (e.g.: on the lavatory mirror, on an airsickness bag, etc.). In the event of a threat during the flight, the cabin crew must notify the flight crew immediately.

chunks.heading: 8.3.1 Suspect Object
chunks.text:
The three following questions may help to determine a suspect object:
1. Is the object usually in this location?
2. Was the object visible/not visible?
3. Does the object. look suspicious? If the cabin crew are not sure about the presence of any object on board, they shall report it. The crewmember who finds the object shall:
1. Notify the flight crew immediately
2. Provide clear information: exact location, detailed description of the object, any odors
3. Notify all other cabin crew
4. Wait for instructions from the flight crew. The crewmember that finds the object shall not:
1. Leave the object alone - if needed, they may ask another crewmember to stay and guard the area, to prevent any inadvertent movement
2. Touch or move the object (unless the Captain decides to transfer it to the Least Risk Bomb- Location (LRBL))
3. Cut or disconnect any wires/strings
4. Use electronic devices near the object.
